キャプション1: Scary guy in encyclopedia!!!!
A1 cha 158: P-please calm down, /VAR/-sama. Something scary in the encyclopedia...?
A2 cha 180: It may be that some element of this world has carelessly slipped into a place it has nothing to do with.
A3 cha 168: There was an oversight, and I do apologize most sincerely. I shall lock it completely so that nothing of the sort occurs again.
キャプション2: Yeah, make sure it doesn't come out again!
キャプション3: But it's interesting, so leave it as it is.
B1 cha 170: Understood. Nothing strange will cut into the encyclopedia suddenly any longer, so please rest assured.
B2 cha 168: If /VAR/-sama should change your mind, I will loosen the lock, so please call on me again.
C1 cha 152: Well, /VAR/-sama, you are a bold one.
C2 cha 172: Certainly. Then I shall leave things so that intrusions by things of unknown nature are permitted.
C3 cha 156: If you should wish to have it not appear, please call on me again.

キャプション1: How long have you been here?
A1 cha 158: In fact, not so much time has passed since this world came into being.
A2 cha 180: Since /VAR/-sama arrived not long after I had built this world up, in all honesty the surprise was greater than the joy.
A3 cha 168: So there is no great difference between /VAR/-sama and myself in the time we have spent in this world, I should think.
A4 cha 166: Did you perhaps think I had been here for hundreds of years all this time?
キャプション3: That would be going a bit far...
B1 cha 170: Hee hee hee, I ought to have said so sooner.
B2 cha 168: Though I look like this, I am still in my teens.
C1 cha 152: At any rate, I am a human being the same as /VAR/-sama. It is my fate to age in the ordinary way and to die in the ordinary way.

キャプション1: What food do you like?
A1 cha 158: Food I like... Let me see. There is nothing in particular worth mentioning, but...
A2 cha 180: Though I look like this, I prefer the rich sort of food to the light sort.
A3 cha 168: In all my life I have never once experienced what they call a heavy stomach, and I am perfectly fine with grilled meat first thing in the morning.
A4 cha 166: Ah, but I do watch my figure, so... probably I am all right on that count, I think, but...
A5 cha 162: Even looking the way I do, appearances still matter to me...

キャプション1: I want to see your real face.
A1 cha 158: I am sorry, but that I cannot do.
A2 cha 180: I have a small complex about my face, so I make a point of showing it to no one.
A3 cha 168: In all likelihood I shall never show /VAR/-sama my bare face.
B1 cha 170: A complex, or should I say... that is...
B2 cha 168: I am sorry; if you would let this topic end about here...
C1 cha 152: Please imagine what is under the mask however you like.
C2 cha 172: Ah, but... for what it is worth, I am on the expressive side, even so.
C3 cha 156: So please think of the face under the mask as changing expression each time.

キャプション1: Where did /立木/ come from?
A1 cha 158: I too am originally an inhabitant of an ordinary world.
A2 cha 180: Strictly speaking, it is not the same dimension /VAR/-sama lives in, but...
A3 cha 168: I am not a youkai or an alien, so I am not so far outside human understanding as you may be hoping.
A4 cha 166: For example, I do not think there is a prefecture called 'Sawa Prefecture' in /VAR/-sama's world, nor an era name of Shiyo.
A5 cha 162: In this way, /VAR/-sama's world, the world I was in, and the world of this story look alike and yet each differs in subtle ways.
A6 cha 159: The largest difference for /VAR/-sama would be the point that /VAR/-sama does not exist in my world, nor in the world of the story.

キャプション1: What do you do mid-scenario?
A1 cha 158: Of course, I am checking /VAR/-sama's progress.
A2 cha 180: I have a duty to record your progress and always present /VAR/-sama with the latest state of it.
A3 cha 168: So even if /VAR/-sama closes this world suddenly, all of the progress is recorded, so please rest assured.
A4 cha 166: However, on rare occasions, when unexpected trouble severs the point of contact between /VAR/-sama and this world, a distortion arises in time.
A5 cha 162: In that case I am sorry, but it will begin from the point at which /VAR/-sama last came to this world.
A6 cha 159: So please take good care in managing the interface that connects this world and /VAR/-sama.
A7 cha 142: I do take care that this does not happen, but there are also cases where a defect in this world disconnects you by force.

キャプション1: How many scenarios in all?
A1 cha 158: Quite a lot. You could most likely not read the whole of it through in 24 hours.
A2 cha 180: And for that very reason, a deeply rooted story unfolds.
A3 cha 168: If you go on thinking simply as it comes to you, "Is that how it is?", there may be a pitfall you did not expect.
A4 cha 166: That said, /VAR/-sama has only to watch, so of course there is no danger to your person. Please rest assured.

キャプション1: How long will /立木/ stay here?
A1 cha 158: I have not particularly decided, but...
A2 cha 180: As long as there are guests who visit this world, I intend to receive them.
B1 cha 170: Yes, that is right. /VAR/-sama is my first guest.
B2 cha 168: There are points at which I am inexperienced, but I beg your understanding.
C1 cha 152: However, there are very few who can find this world.
C2 cha 172: So I do not think any other guest is at all likely to come.
C3 cha 156: /VAR/-sama's visit was a probability that could truly be called a miracle.

キャプション1: What kind of world is this?
A1 cha 158: This is a world I built up, a place where a mental image has been given form, so to speak.
A2 cha 180: So whatever I picture can be made to exist here.
A3 cha 168: It is what is called a dream world. Would it be right to say that /VAR/-sama is watching my dream from beside me?
キャプション2: Why did you make a world like this?
キャプション3: What becomes of this world in the end?
B1 cha 170: Why...?
B2 cha 168: Does /VAR/-sama wonder why people dream, each time you dream?
B3 cha 156: It may be that the real me does not even know that I am building this world up.
B4 cha 148: Whether the real me is awake or asleep is not certain either.
B5 cha 178: This is that sort of unstable world.
C1 cha 152: There is no world that lasts forever. In time this world too will perish in some form.
C2 cha 172: What will set it off I do not know either, but it is the same thing as the dream world vanishing when one wakes from a dream.
C3 cha 156: Both I and /VAR/-sama will simply return to the real world.

キャプション1: Don't you get sleepy?
A1 cha 158: There is no occasion on which I am driven by physiological urges in this world.
A2 cha 180: I neither grow sleepy nor grow hungry; I devote myself solely to having /VAR/-sama come to know this world deeply.
キャプション2: Aren't you yawning under that Noh mask?
B1 cha 170: Um...
B2 cha 168: In all honesty, while /VAR/-sama is viewing a scenario I have rather more time on my hands than I need, so...
B3 cha 156: Once in a while, I might just...
B4 cha 148: Ah, ah, but, but, I do check /VAR/-sama's progress properly. On that one point you may trust me!
B5 cha 178: I-I am doing my job properly, so please rest assured.
C1 cha 152: Well, let me see, when appetizing food appears in a scenario I am sometimes tempted, but...
C2 cha 172: I have no need to eat in order to stay alive.
C3 cha 156: Which is to say, it makes no difference whether I eat or not.
C4 cha 152: Oh? In that case, what would happen if I overate. Would I become fat, or would nothing change...? I have never tried it, so I do not know, but...
C5 cha 180: If nothing changes, then my figure will not change any further. Which means there would be no point in dieting even if I wanted to...
C6 cha 180: As long as I am in this world, my figure not changing is a happy thing and also a slightly troublesome one.
C7 cha 168: Of course, I cannot rule out the possibility of overeating and getting fat.

キャプション1: What era is this world in?
A1 cha 158: Do you mean when this world sits on the timeline?
キャプション3: No, the era /立木/ came from
B1 cha 170: This world has no concept of time.
B2 cha 168: It can be called a subspace for going to a particular time and place, so there is no when or where that this world itself is.
B3 cha 156: I do count the time since /VAR/-sama came here, however, so please use that for reference.
C1 cha 152: The world I came from...
C2 cha 172: I think it is probably not much different from the age /VAR/-sama is in.
C3 cha 156: Cars run and there are smartphones, so I do not think the feel of the age differs much between /VAR/-sama and me.
C4 cha 152: Please think of it as the equal of the world /VAR/-sama is in now.

キャプション1: How does /立木/ relate to this?
A1 cha 158: It is not that there is any particular connection.
A2 cha 180: It is blunt to put it this way, but /VAR/-sama should have had no connection to this world either to begin with.
A3 cha 168: Through a tie of some kind you came here all the same. I am much the same.
A4 cha 166: I merely happened to imagine a world like this and give it form.
キャプション2: Why did you imagine this world?
キャプション3: Am I really unconnected to it...?
B1 cha 170: Every one of the stories that unfold here is wretched and cruel. That there is a route which avoids it by a miracle is as I said in my first greeting.
B2 cha 168: I simply took an interest: I wanted to see a world like that.
B3 cha 156: That is, this world did not exist to begin with; it is a world that exists by my will alone.
C2 cha 172: In all honesty, I do not grasp the whole of /VAR/-sama's background, so I cannot declare that there is absolutely no connection.
C3 cha 156: If this world were one deeply connected to /VAR/-sama...
C4 cha 152: That too would be most interesting.

キャプション1: Any tips for the references?
A1 cha 158: I see, I had not yet told you that. Allow me to explain it again.
A2 cha 180: A reference is a side story, or reference material, that you do not necessarily have to view in order to follow the story.
A3 cha 168: As for the quickest way to make use of a reference: view it as soon as you obtain it. And if it is in the object format, please make a point of collecting every node.
A4 cha 166: When your thinking comes to a dead end, it may also be good to look back over the references once through.
A5 cha 162: And this is important, so please keep it well in mind.
A6 cha 159: It is impossible to know all of this world without viewing the references at all.
A7 cha 142: If you wish to see the very end of this world for yourself...
A8 cha 133: The viewing of references will be a help to /VAR/-sama.

キャプション1: Any special controls? 1
A1 cha 158: Yes, there are.
A2 cha 180: The R button for the references, D for the encyclopedia (Dictionary) and T for the chatter (Talk) shortcut from the navigation screen to each menu.
A3 cha 168: Please use them when calling me out each time and then choosing a menu is troublesome.
A4 cha 166: I shall say it once more. The R button shortcuts to the references, D to the encyclopedia, T to the chatter. Only on the scenario navigator screen.

キャプション1: Any special controls? 2
A1 cha 158: Then this time let me explain the controls during a scenario.
A2 cha 180: At the top of the screen during a scenario there is an information bar, where you can see information on the scenario you are viewing.
A3 cha 168: Clicking the information bar releases it from being fixed, and lets you hide the information bar.
A4 cha 166: You may also use the scenario-related option menu with a right-click.
A5 cha 162: Also, holding the Ctrl button down lets you fast-forward the scenario. Please use it as needed.

キャプション1: Any special controls? 3
A1 cha 158: Aside from that... I do not think you will have much use for this, but...
A2 cha 180: Pressing the space key during a scenario lets you hide the text box.
A3 cha 168: If you should wish to look at the background at leisure, please make use of it.

キャプション1: Say something interesting 1
A1 cha 158: What...!
A2 cha 180: That is a most unreasonable thing to spring on me...
A3 cha 168: Well then... a little about the Noh mask.
A4 cha 166: The Noh mask I wear is called a koomote, and it is modelled on a young woman.
A5 cha 162: In fact there are many kinds of Noh mask. The hannya and the oni masks of course, but the hyottoko and the okame masks are classed as Noh masks too.
A6 cha 159: Nogaku and kagura stage masks are collectively called Noh masks, so any mask used on such a stage can be called a Noh mask.
A7 cha 142: Mine covers the whole face, but an ordinary Noh mask leaves the chin out. They are designed so the performer's jaw shows.
A9 cha 110: I am sorry; this is the only sort of story I can manage...
B1 cha 170: Oh...! It is I who am grateful. I am very glad a story of only that much could please you.
B2 cha 168: But I shall not rest content with that. I shall strive so that /VAR/-sama may enjoy your time in this world a little more.
B3 cha 156: I do not wish to be a dull guide who only guides.
C1 cha 152: I am much obliged. I shall strive to polish my art of conversation a little more...
C2 cha 172: Though since there is no one in this world but /VAR/-sama and myself, I have no one to polish it on but /VAR/-sama...
C3 cha 156: If you would not mind, for the sake of my art of conversashion, conversation, I would be glad of your company.
C5 cha 180: I did not trip over my words, all right?

キャプション1: Say something interesting 2
A1 cha 158: Again...!
A2 cha 180: No, as a guide, this sort of training matters for polishing my conversation.
A3 cha 168: Then, right away...
A4 cha 166: There is a tale called Momotaro. An old story about a boy born from a peach who goes off to subdue the oni.
A5 cha 162: But originally, the mainstream version had him as a child born to an old couple who grew young again after eating a peach.
A6 cha 159: Which is to say, the old couple who grew young from the peach went straight on into the night and shared a bed...
A7 cha 142: Honestly, of all the things to do first upon growing young... Do two people really fall into that mood so suddenly?
キャプション2: A dirty joke, of all things?
B2 cha 168: I am glad I am wearing the Noh mask. I could never show you the expression I have just now.
B5 cha 178: I-It is not a dirty joke! It is merely one person's impression! I-It is /VAR/-sama, who thunks, thinks of that as a dirty joke, who is at fault!
B7 cha 138: Right! This topic is finished now!
C1 cha 152: Um... well...
C2 cha 172: Being young is a fine thing...
C4 cha 152: And so the two shared a bed... um...
C5 cha 180: That night, the old couple, one another's newly young bodies...
C6 cha 180: Yes, um, a year later, a healthy boy was born!
C7 cha 168: The child was named Momotaro, grew strong, and went off to subdue the oni!
C8 cha 112: That is all! And so, happily ever after!

キャプション1: Say something interesting 3
A1 cha 158: ...but I shall do my best...!
A2 cha 180: Um... what sort of story shall it be...
B1 cha 170: A funny story, you say...
B2 cha 168: Oh yes, this is from last summer. That night I was making dinner by myself. The menu was somen.
B3 cha 156: The garnish was just green onion. Somen, noodle sauce and onion were set on the table. I ate as usual, dipping onion and somen in the sauce, but...
B4 cha 148: But for some reason that somen had no taste.
B5 cha 178: No, there was a somen-like flavor, but oddly no taste, not appetizing at all. Still, it was strangely refreshing, so I ate it to the end as it was.
B6 cha 160: After eating I opened the refrigerator meaning to drink some barley tea, but...
B7 cha 138: What I had taken for noodle sauce was in fact the barley tea.
B8 cha 104: Ah, um, what I took for sauce was barley tea, so I was eating somen dipped in tea... that is...
B9 cha 120: /小/Uuu... and I thought it was funny...
C1 cha 152: A story to cry over, you say... That was the winter 2 years ago.
C2 cha 172: As I walked along a road with a thin layer of snow on it, I found something black twitching on top of the snow.
C3 cha 156: It was a baby black cat. The baby black cat was badly hurt, and had stained even the snow red with blood.
C4 cha 152: There was no animal hospital nearby. I am allergic to cats, so all I could do was wrap it in the scarf I was wearing...
C5 cha 180: In less than 10 minutes that kitten came to the end of its short life.
C6 cha 180: Had it been abandoned by its parent, or had it strayed and been hurt?
C7 cha 168: Still, at least at the end it could pass the time in a warm scarf and not on cold snow, and even now I truly think that was good.
C8 cha 112: Even now I cannot forget the kitten's last cry and its eyes just before its life ended.
C9 cha 106: Less a good deed than a day that forced my own uselessness on me: in the end I could only let it die.

キャプション1: What are your hobbies?
A1 cha 158: A hobby...? A hobby...
A2 cha 180: Watching movies, I suppose. I enjoy watching more or less any genre.
A3 cha 168: I like both watching at the movie theater and watching at home.
A4 cha 166: Oh yes, just the sort of thing Natsumi Kogori and Haruka Niimura were doing. Seeing a movie at the theater, then viewing it at home later.
キャプション2: What kind of movies do those two like?
B1 cha 170: They seem to like anything. The point seems to be simply that the two of them spend an enjoyable time together.
B2 cha 168: They also seem to play games together and cook meals together.
B3 cha 156: Not only indoors; they apparently go out together often as well.
B4 cha 148: To me, always being with someone feels a little confining, but for them it seems comfortable.
B5 cha 178: Ah... that does not mean being here with /VAR/-sama all the time is confining...
B6 cha 160: Having you keep me company like this makes me very glad.
B7 cha 138: Yes, very. Truly. There is no one for me but /VAR/-sama.
C1 cha 152: I like going out alone as well. Without a thought in my head, just a stroll on my own.
C2 cha 172: Going into a shop I happen to notice, or trying a drink I have never seen before at the convenience store.
C3 cha 156: I only recently realized there is a fresh surprise you can find only alone. How you look at things changes the impression the thing makes.

キャプション1: Mika Tachiki your real name?
A1 cha 158: No; let me state clearly that this is an assumed name. My real name is something else.
A2 cha 180: The keyword of this world is April 8, but what relation does the 'Mika' in my name have to it? [TN: her 'Mika' is written with the characters for 'third day']
A3 cha 168: There may be some connection, or it may in fact be a suggestive nothing with no connection at all.
A4 cha 166: Well, pay it no mind and call me whatever you like.
B1 cha 170: Yes, this is Tachiki.
B2 cha 168: Hee hee, an assumed name though it is, being called by a name is a glad thing.
C3 cha 156: Ah, I see, you mean me. Forgive me.
C4 cha 152: No, it is only that I never expected to be called by my given name with -chan on it...
C5 cha 180: Ah, but I do not dislike that way of calling me either. If anything it is refreshing and I am glad of it.
C6 cha 180: Please, call me whatever you like.
D1 cha 120: Oh my my, so that is how you come at it. Hee hee, very well.
D2 cha 169: Then from now on, please do call me Noh Mask-chan.

キャプション1: Do you have family?
A1 cha 158: Yes. I have a father, a mother, and a younger sister.
A2 cha 180: I am on good terms with both my parents and my sister, so I suppose you could say I have been quite blessed in my surroundings.
キャプション3: What is your little sister like?
B1 cha 170: Being asked outright like that is rather difficult, but...
B2 cha 168: I respect them. I think they poured a great deal of love into me, and I like the way they live and the way they think.
B3 cha 156: I want to become like my parents in the future, but it seems rather difficult.
C1 cha 152: My sister is relatively close to me in age.
C2 cha 172: Our values are fairly close as well, so we often go out together.
C3 cha 156: Well, we are what you often hear called 'a family like friends'.

キャプション1: What do you normally wear?
A1 cha 158: Normally I do not wear the Noh mask, and I dress in an ordinary, current sort of way.
A2 cha 180: If anything, I prefer clothes that are easy to move in over dressing up showily.
A3 cha 168: Accessories and skirts and the like are not to my taste.
A4 cha 166: Well, they are simply not to my taste; it is not that I never wear them...
A5 cha 162: When I am given a skirt as a present I am a little at a loss, but I am glad of it all the same, so I do wear them now and then.
A6 cha 159: Hee hee hee, looking as I do, you could hardly picture me in a miniskirt.

キャプション1: What do you do on days off?
A1 cha 158: On days off I surf the internet at home, or watch movies...
A2 cha 180: And chatting with friends, I suppose. Very ordinary, I think.
A3 cha 168: And /VAR/-sama, what do you do on your days off?
キャプション3: Being here should tell you enough.
B1 cha 170: I see; I like the outdoors as well. Camping, swimming at the beach, that sort of thing.
B2 cha 168: When I cook outdoors I always prepare fried noodles in sauce. Sauce scorched over a strong flame is quite addictive.
B3 cha 156: I should also like to go to a ski resort once. I have never been.
C1 cha 152: Ah... I see, indoors then?
C2 cha 172: There is plenty of entertainment inside the house these days. I am rather fond of indoor things myself.
C3 cha 156: I especially like spending a rainy day indoors at leisure. That feeling of taking your ease between the cold outside and the warmth within...
C4 cha 152: Hee hee, though spending a fine day indoors on purpose is not bad either.

キャプション1: What is a letters reference?
A1 cha 158: A letters reference is a handwritten document made more than 100 years before the year Shiyo 800.
A2 cha 180: They contain important matter that the main story does not tell, so I should very much like you to view them.
A3 cha 168: However, to view a letters reference you must spend the thing called 'points' at the lower left here.
A4 cha 166: Spending points widens the range you can view.
A5 cha 162: However, since the letters references are old things, they are soiled and cannot be read clearly.
A6 cha 159: If you bring the readable range to 100%, the stains and tears are purified and you can view it as clean as when it was first written.
キャプション3: How should I take the contents of a letters reference?
B1 cha 170: To explain roughly how points increase: the more /VAR/-sama comes to know of this world, the more are added.
B2 cha 168: Specifically, they are added according to your progress through the scenarios and the state of your reference viewing.
B3 cha 156: Oh yes, since it is 'of this world', chatter with me also seems to increase them a little.
B4 cha 148: The points /VAR/-sama holds are limited, so it is best to think carefully about which reference to spend them on before viewing.
B5 cha 178: One thing to be careful of: viewing the encyclopedia adds no points at all.
B6 cha 160: The encyclopedia is best used purely for picking up background knowledge or for review.
B7 cha 138: Well, there is information found only in the encyclopedia. Even so, no points are added.
B8 cha 104: And please note that viewing a point-spending reference, like the letters, adds none either.
C1 cha 152: As I said earlier, the letters references contain important information the main story does not tell.
C2 cha 172: Even matter that looks unrelated at first glance will somewhere supplement the information of the main story.
C3 cha 156: Some of them record events of long ago, and I think much of it differs from the historical fact of /VAR/-sama's world.
C4 cha 152: But it is certainly important information about this world, so it would be good to keep it in mind.
C5 cha 180: In what form it will be a hint, and in what form it will be a help to /VAR/-sama. Later on it will certainly come up in some form.

キャプション1: What is a report reference?
A1 cha 158: A report reference appears to be a research report written by a certain person.
A2 cha 180: I do not know the details either, but it seems to set down matters of the utmost importance and the strictest secrecy, bearing on the root of the main story.
A3 cha 168: However, because of that secrecy the reports are in a state you cannot make out by simply looking.
A4 cha 166: Specifically, the reports are torn to pieces, or painted over.
A5 cha 162: So by spending points you can add the parts that were torn away and lost, and restore the report.
A6 cha 159: It is a trouble, but I should like that restoration work to be done directly by /VAR/-sama's own hand.
A7 cha 142: When every part is restored, the places that were hard to read will be fully restored and clear.
A8 cha 133: The repair method also calls for special controls, so I strongly recommend using the 'Help' button each time.
A9 cha 110: Do you understand? With a report reference, please make use of the help.
キャプション2: Is something that important written in them?
B1 cha 170: Yes, I do grasp that something extremely important is written there.
B2 cha 168: For that reason the content itself seems to demand some understanding, but set against the information of the main story it should come smoothly.
B3 cha 156: That is, even if a report means nothing when you view it, much information appears later that connects: "So that was what it meant."
B4 cha 148: A fully restored report can be viewed clean at any time, so you may look back later at whatever concerns you.
C1 cha 152: Let me see; the restoration work runs from easy to extremely difficult, in great variety.
C2 cha 172: Also, gimmicks that obstruct the restoration work appear from time to time.
C3 cha 156: There seem to be several kinds of obstructing gimmick, so for details please see that report reference's help. The gimmicks are explained there.
C4 cha 152: And I have not confirmed the details myself, but there is something I should like you to watch for when restoring.
C5 cha 180: Some of them seem to hold important information that can only be seen before repair.
C6 cha 180: Which is to say, once you complete the restoration you cannot see that information.
C7 cha 168: Do you follow? The restoration work matters, but there is grave information you can only see at that moment. Please keep it well in mind.
D1 cha 120: I imagine /VAR/-sama is using a mouse, and the controls call for the mouse's full range.
D2 cha 169: Those controls can only be confirmed by looking at the help, so if you overlook the help I believe you will have a very hard time.
D3 cha 176: You follow? If the controls trouble you, please check the help.
D4 cha 159: For some report references the restoration work is very hard, so there is also an Assist function as a relief measure.
D5 cha 128: However, the Assist function spends points, so please think well about where to use it.

キャプション1: What is a side-tale reference?
A1 cha 158: A side-tale reference... I am sorry, but I have little information myself; it is a reference with many mysteries.
A2 cha 180: What I do grasp is that it is a reference in the scenario format depicting one particular person's whole life, and that it gathers up the letters and report references.
A3 cha 168: The content is not so hard and viewing costs no points, but the unlock conditions are very strict, and gathering every side-tale reference takes no ordinary effort.
キャプション2: Can I learn the truth from them?
キャプション3: So I should view the side tales properly too?
B1 cha 170: The truth...
B2 cha 168: /VAR/-sama has no need to know the truth; it is enough that you see the happy ending of the characters. So I should like to say, but...
B3 cha 156: If the unlock conditions are as ferociously strict as the side tales', then surely information to match can be had.
B4 cha 148: Even what /VAR/-sama calls the 'truth', at that.
B5 cha 178: Knowing the truth is not asked of /VAR/-sama, but I am in no position to stop that will and those actions.
B6 cha 160: Please judge that for yourself, /VAR/-sama.
C1 cha 152: There is nothing better than viewing them, and I cannot imagine what effect your viewing may have on this world.
C2 cha 172: I leave that judgment to /VAR/-sama.

キャプション1: /立木/: student? Working adult?
A1 cha 158: I am a student. On weekdays I go to school.
A2 cha 180: And what is it that /VAR/-sama does?
キャプション5: Huh? You ask things like that?
B1 cha 170: Oh? Then perhaps we are close in age?
B2 cha 168: Those around me often tell me that 'your student days are your bloom', so I mean to enjoy what I can while I can.
B3 cha 156: Well, even this world might be called an extension of my hobby.
B4 cha 148: If I am wrong, I am sorry.
C1 cha 152: Well, so you are already active out in the world.
C2 cha 172: Since one lives in a capitalist world it is a road most people walk, but seen from a young thing like me, working adults really are impressive.
C3 cha 156: When I think that /VAR/-sama contributes to society too, I cannot help but feel respect.
D1 cha 120: To think you were already retired!
D2 cha 169: To have come this far while tasting so much bitterness in your life so far: I truly respect it.
D3 cha 176: If this world can add even a little pleasure to /VAR/-sama's life, that is all I could wish for.
E1 cha 101: Ah...
E2 cha 142: I see...
E3 cha 168: Well...
E4 cha 156: Life...
E5 cha 134: different for each person...

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 1
A1 cha 158: A question for /VAR/-sama? Let me see...
A2 cha 180: Where are you from?
B1 cha 170: The north side means a cold region, then.
B2 cha 168: In my region a fair amount of snow piles up in winter, but seeing how people in northern Japan live, I am truly impressed by their hardiness.
B3 cha 156: I imagine /VAR/-sama has had all sorts of hardship from the cold and the snow as well.
C1 cha 152: The east side means the Kanto region, or far across the sea, Hawaii or the American mainland...
C2 cha 172: In my own mind eastern Japan gives an impression of cities. Well, of course there must be deep mountain areas and coastal areas too.
C3 cha 156: Perhaps /VAR/-sama is a city child. I should like to live in such a place once myself.
D1 cha 120: Western Japan, or Asia, or far off in Europe...
D2 cha 169: I do like the culture of western Japan. Lightly seasoned food especially is to my taste. I should like to travel there once, over about a week.
D3 cha 176: There are all sorts of tempting things, flour dishes and ramen, and I am interested in the Seto Inland Sea and the islands of Nagasaki as well.
E1 cha 101: South side!
E2 cha 142: South side!
E3 cha 168: A warm region, then? I am no good with the cold, so I have a particular longing for it.
E4 cha 156: Ah... let me say just in case: this outfit is not because of the cold. It is purely to hide myself.
E5 cha 134: Would this outfit be hot in Okinawa in summer? Meaning to hide myself, I collapse and am left exposed, unseemly―
E6 cha 136: No, anywhere in Japan is hot in summer. In case it turns hot here as in summer, I must think of a different costume.

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 2
A1 cha 158: A question for /VAR/-sama... Let me see...
A2 cha 180: What sort of games do you like?
B1 cha 170: The reflex type. I like those too, but I am truly bad at them...
B2 cha 168: I mean to press the button, but somehow only my body moves, and my intention and my posture are not reflected in the game at all...
B3 cha 156: Still, playing with a lot of people is truly fun and I love it. Alone, though...
B4 cha 148: I carry the sorrow of a game over by myself, which makes for a rather forlorn feeling.
C1 cha 152: Strategy types are truly fun once you understand the rules.
C2 cha 172: Until you understand the rules you are groping, but recent games guide you kindly there, so you reach the fun part smoothly.
C3 cha 156: Conversely, I like the retro sort, simple and a little standoffish. Simple, so easy to grasp, and how to beat a strong enemy with limited strategy―
C4 cha 152: Even so, people have their own strategies more than you would think, and hearing them is a pleasure as well.
D1 cha 120: Text-type games, I see...
D2 cha 169: In all honesty I am not very good with print, but made into a game, with the staging of picture and sound, some of them draw you right in.
D3 cha 176: And growing attached to the characters, or minding what comes next so much that you cannot stop; when one takes hold of me it takes hold completely.
E1 cha 101: I see, there are many game genres. Puzzles, rhythm games and more besides.
E2 cha 142: Ah, but personally I like horror. Well, it is that urge to look at frightening things.

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 3
A1 cha 158: A question for /VAR/-sama... And then...
A2 cha 180: What sort of place does /VAR/-sama live in?
キャプション4: A bit rural. The convenience store and supermarket are far.
キャプション5: Deep countryside with no convenience store or supermarket
B1 cha 170: Well, you have your home in a metropolitan area.
B2 cha 168: I have heard it said that Tokyo is a gathering of country folk, and for that very reason dreams and chances must be lying about everywhere.
B3 cha 156: I have never lived in such a place, but I am very interested. Changing trains at random and getting off at an unknown station: I should like that.
C1 cha 152: I see; Motoki-cho, the setting of the story, is exactly that.
C2 cha 172: Motoki-cho's population keeps growing, so though it is designated a 'town' it is apparently already big enough to become a city. It will go on developing.
C3 cha 156: However, until a little while ago Motoki-cho was apparently a place of few people and much nature.
C4 cha 152: There are in fact not a few voices that mourn the Motoki-cho of cherry trees watched over by the goshinboku.
C5 cha 180: Ah, I am sorry. I asked about the place /VAR/-sama lives and then talked about the story instead.
C6 cha 180: If I lived somewhere, a regional city with no real inconvenience would suit me. People neither too many nor too few, some civilization and some nature together: that is the appeal.
C7 cha 168: If you want things you go to the station front; if you want nature you go a little way out. In a sense it may be more convenient than a metropolitan area.
D1 cha 120: The countryside, with the convenience store and supermarket far away.
D2 cha 169: I find myself imagining a place where hills and fields, or the sea and rivers, stretch out wide.
D3 cha 176: I have never lived in such a place, so this is purely imagination, but I suppose that on weekends you go out to a downtown some way off, or to a large shopping mall.
D4 cha 159: Then every weekend would be an event tickling the adventuring spirit. Even a familiar place, steeped in an air you cannot usually feel, is its own pleasure.
E1 cha 101: My, as rural as that...
E2 cha 142: A question arises to begin with as to how /VAR/-sama makes contact with this world at all, but...
E3 cha 168: Well, in these times I suppose the internet has come to take priority over the convenience store and the supermarket.
E4 cha 156: By now the internet has become one lifeline that cannot be done without.
E5 cha 134: And in a place so far from any village, I find myself wondering whether you meet wild creatures more often than people.
E6 cha 136: I have set foot in such places a few times myself, and the local produce eaten there is very good indeed.

キャプション1: Do you play sports?
A1 cha 158: As for sports, I have no particular experience to speak of.
A2 cha 180: But I do not think my athletic sense is so bad. At running and swimming both, I think I can manage better than average times.
A3 cha 168: I still hardly know the rules of baseball or soccer, and I once fouled at the best moment of a sports festival and was terribly embarrassed...
A5 cha 162: Would you like to hear about that great embarrassment?
B1 cha 170: Then, though it is a little embarrassing... It was when I was playing volleyball at a sports festival.
B2 cha 168: It was a crucial moment: one more point and we won, 3 points against and we lost. And the ball that decided it came flying toward me.
B3 cha 156: And that ball was on an extremely doubtful path, where you could not tell whether it was out.
B4 cha 148: My side shouted "Out! Out!", the other side "It's in! It's in!", and I was thoroughly confused about what to do.
B5 cha 178: If it was out, dodge the ball and we win! If it was in, receive it! And while I was thinking this and that, the ball reached me―
B6 cha 160: I caught the ball.
B7 cha 138: I did not know myself what had happened. Catching the ball is of course a foul.
B8 cha 104: My side crumpled, the crowd roared with laughter... It was truly embarrassing.
B9 cha 120: Uh, I know I brought it up myself, but please keep it in your heart alone, /VAR/-sama.
C1 cha 152: Let me see... It is embarrassing even now to recall, so there is nothing to tell at this point.

キャプション1: Are you good at stretching?
A1 cha 158: Haah!? What is this!? That sudden a topic...
B1 cha 170: It is not something I particularly keep secret; I was only startled by the suddenness.
B2 cha 168: Well, I think I am reasonably flexible. I can do a 180 degree split, and I can walk while holding a bridge.
B4 cha 148: I am not going to do it, all right?
C1 cha 152: I should rather have you explain how such a thing came into your head...
C2 cha 172: Ah, no, truly, there is no need to explain...

キャプション1: Are you good at cooking?
A1 cha 158: I believe I cook as well as most. I can use a knife properly, and I manage the heat all right.
A2 cha 180: But holding heavy cookware is hard for me, so I am better at simmered and grilled dishes than at stir-fries.
キャプション2: How did you get good at cooking?
キャプション4: Any dishes you are bad at?
B1 cha 170: Because I often help my mother. My mother cooks by hand almost every day.
B2 cha 168: But I am still no match for my mother. Her skill at cooking is truly of another dimension.
C1 cha 152: Yes, of course I can. I often made them for my sister as well.
C2 cha 172: It takes time, but I often make cakes and sweet buns and the like.
D1 cha 120: Dishes I am bad at... nothing comes to mind at once... Let me see...
D2 cha 169: Chinese stir-fries, after all. You cannot make them taste good without shaking the pan or the wok properly.
D3 cha 176: Ah, in that sense pasta is a little beyond me too. Mixing it quickly with the sauce takes considerable technique.
D4 cha 159: Once I say that, a rice omelet is no good either. I cannot roll it well.
D5 cha 128: I still have far to go. I shall keep at it.

キャプション1: Let me taste /立木/'s cooking!
A1 cha 158: Huh? My own cooking?
A2 cha 180: Making it is no trouble in itself, but the ingredients that matter are not here.
A3 cha 168: I can widen space, but bringing into being what does not exist is impossible. I am sorry.
A4 cha 166: There seem to be all sorts of things in this room, but every one is an unreal image, so you cannot take them in your hand.
A5 cha 162: But should the chance come, I should dearly like to cook for you.
A6 cha 159: What sort of dish do you prefer?
キャプション2: Something hearty that goes with rice!
B1 cha 170: Dishes that go with white rice are my strength. Ginger pork, meat and potato stew, simmered dishes: leave them to me.
B2 cha 168: This is my own way, but to make a dish that goes with white rice, season it sweeter than you would think.
B3 cha 156: Simmered fish especially comes out very well if you add plenty of sugar and cook it until the broth thickens.
B4 cha 148: If you are interested, please try it.
C1 cha 152: I see. I feel somewhat tested, but you will certainly be surprised.
C2 cha 172: Tempura, vinegared dishes, hot pot: you will certainly be pleased.
C3 cha 156: And with Japanese food I should want to be particular about the plating too. The staging on the plate is part of its real pleasure.
C4 cha 152: Not with Japanese food alone: enjoying a dish with all five senses, not the tongue and nose only, is its own pleasure.
D1 cha 120: Sweets, how nice. These I like making with several people rather than alone.
D2 cha 169: If the chance truly comes, I should be glad of /VAR/-sama's help as well.
E1 cha 101: High-class French... so that is how you come at it.
E2 cha 142: With French the dishes themselves matter, of course, but so does which dish in what combination and in what order it is served.
E3 cha 168: Consulting with whatever ingredients can be had that day, I shall make you the very best.
E4 cha 156: But for high-class French, even the ingredients must be costly things...
E5 cha 134: There is rarely a chance to cook such a thing, so I am very excited! I look forward to the making more than the eating!

キャプション1: Rice or bread for breakfast?
A1 cha 158: I am decidedly of the rice camp. Perhaps because of where my parents are from, my breakfast staple has been anything but rice only a handful of times.
A2 cha 180: A hotel breakfast was bread once, and I could not feel I had eaten at all, so I went and bought a rice ball at the convenience store afterward.
A3 cha 168: Which is /VAR/-sama?
B1 cha 170: Ah, lately there are so many of the bread camp that I was at a loss. I feel I have met a comrade for the first time in a long while.
B2 cha 168: I should like to enjoy an elegant breakfast with /VAR/-sama once.
C1 cha 152: Ah... you too...
C2 cha 172: I do not deny eating bread. But eating rice is Japan's food culture, one of the treasures carried on from ancient times.
C3 cha 156: If the chance comes, do please try white rice for breakfast.
D1 cha 120: I see, there are cereals and noodles as well. That it cannot be flatly rice or bread is the troubling part.
D2 cha 169: I recall seeing photographs of breakfasts of the world, and they were truly varied and interesting.
D3 cha 176: Rice in the morning. That is the sure thing, but I too have the wish to try the various breakfasts of the world.
E1 cha 101: Well, that will not do.
E2 cha 142: Breakfast is the source of a day's vigor and the root of spirit and will. I do not say make it rice, so please eat at least a little.
E3 cha 168: My recommendation is seasoned egg over rice. Make a soft-boiled egg beforehand, then steep it sealed overnight in noodle sauce thinned as for cold soba.
E4 cha 156: That alone gives you a superb seasoned egg the next day, so do try it. It keeps, and it is ideal for shoveling down on a busy morning.

キャプション1: Team bamboo? Team mushroom?
A2 cha 180: What on earth are we talking about...
A3 cha 168: But if I must say...
A4 cha 166: I am of the mushroom camp. [TN: rival chocolate snacks shaped as bamboo shoots and mushrooms]
B1 cha 170: Well! I thought myself in the minority, and here you are one of us!
B2 cha 168: Those around me mostly find it distasteful, so I did not much want to speak of it, but...
B3 cha 156: I am glad I could tell /VAR/-sama.
C2 cha 172: I know, I know...! Go to the supermarket and the bamboo shoots mostly outsell them, and everyone around me says bamboo shoot, bamboo shoot...
C3 cha 156: Granting every concession, let us say the bamboo shoot camp is larger! But the bamboo shoot camp must be grateful to the mushroom camp!
C4 cha 152: Humans in the end believe the majority is great. Only because the mushroom minority exists is the bamboo shoot camp drunk on a relative, illusory win.
C5 cha 180: What becomes of the bamboo shoot camp if mushrooms vanish? Passing joy, of course; but with the mushroom camp gone, the concept of a majority goes. They lose their place to flock.
C6 cha 180: Yes, that is what the bamboo shoot camp comes to. By the time they see the mushroom camp's point it is too late: no flock to cling to, and no idea why they clung to bamboo shoots.
C7 cha 168: Their superiority stands only because the mushroom camp exists. Not noticing that, they insult and despise it. A foolish crowd, blind to essence and to worth.

キャプション1: Some topics I can't choose?
A1 cha 158: Ah... so you noticed after all...
A2 cha 180: Guide though I am, there are times I hesitate over whether a topic is really one I may discuss with /VAR/-sama...
A3 cha 168: So it is a matter of the distance between us, or should I say... it may be a rude way to put it, but...
B1 cha 170: Let me see; put plainly, that is what it comes to.
B2 cha 168: As conversations with /VAR/-sama build up I do feel a closeness growing, so the more you talk with me, the more that 'affection' rises.
B3 cha 156: You may think it forward, but I too have feelings, so I beg you to understand.

キャプション1: Do you have a boyfriend?
A1 cha 158: /大文字//揺れ/Wh...!
A2 cha 180: /大文字//揺れ/Wh-wh-wh...!
A3 cha 168: /小/Th-that is, well...
A4 cha 166: I leave it to your imagination...
A5 cha 162: No, to begin with, there could not be a man who would care for a Noh-mask woman like this...
キャプション3: What if you took off the mask?
B1 cha 170: Thank you... /VAR/-sama, you are kind.
B3 cha 156: But! But still, to ask a question like that... well...
B4 cha 148: You have no delicacy...
B5 cha 178: N-now then, nyat shall we talk about?
B6 cha 160: /小/...I bit my tongue...
B7 cha 138: Whew...
C1 cha 152: Even if I took off the Noh mask, getting a boyfriend...
C2 cha 172: No, quite the reverse. A man who judges a woman by whether she wears a Noh mask would surely not suit me.
C3 cha 156: Am I being selfish...

キャプション1: Let's have a staring contest
A1 cha 158: A staring contest...?
A2 cha 180: Hee hee, /VAR/-sama, you have more of a child's heart than I expected.
A3 cha 168: Very well. Shall we begin, then?
B5 cha 178: Uh...
B6 cha 160: Since I am wearing a Noh mask, I do not think there can be a winner or a loser...
B8 cha 104: I am sorry. I have made it awkward...
B9 cha 120: /小/Ah... if I had laughed it would not have turned awkward...

キャプション1: Spring, summer, fall, winter?
A1 cha 158: The season I like...
A2 cha 180: I like summer. The nights especially.
A3 cha 168: As a diary written by a noble of old has it, summer's charm lies in its nights. It is the season when natural light, moonlight and fireflies, shows best.
A4 cha 166: I only remember it because I heard it in class recently.
A5 cha 162: But it is true; the fireflies I once saw deep in the summer mountains were truly splendid.
A6 cha 159: Which does /VAR/-sama like?
B1 cha 170: Spring. A great many people like it. Of course I like it too.
B2 cha 168: That thrill of having finally got out of the cold air, and the lovely flowers and the fresh wind, belong to spring alone.
C1 cha 152: Well, /VAR/-sama too? Then we are of a kind.
C2 cha 172: Summer is the season when even cold-blooded reptiles and insects move about briskly. That air brimming with life is summer's own.
C3 cha 156: Yeah, I do like the glaring summer afternoon as well.
D1 cha 120: Fall. The fall of the harvest, the season when food tastes best.
D2 cha 169: I especially like the new rice of that time. No, not the new rice alone; it is a truly splendid season for the mountain's bounty as well.
D4 cha 159: Forgive me. Where fall is concerned my appetite is stirred whether I will or not...
E1 cha 101: Oh? Only about 4% of people like winter, they say. /VAR/-sama has quite an individual sensibility.
E2 cha 142: Though according to surveys the commonest reason for liking winter best is the negative one that there are no insects.
E3 cha 168: Others say they can do winter sports, or that they like snow, or that they can dress in layers, and those too belong to winter alone.
E4 cha 156: In my case, common as it is, ice cream at the heated table cannot be left out. Ice cream is best not in summer but in winter. I say it flatly. Winter.

キャプション1: How far does this world go?
A1 cha 158: Do you mean how far the scenarios go on?
キャプション3: No, how far can /立木/ widen space?
B1 cha 170: The hint is the completion rate on the scenario navigator. That is the scenarios you have viewed so far against the number of scenarios in that arc.
B2 cha 168: However, this world is extremely unstable. On some trigger it swells greatly or shrinks, or even collapses.
B3 cha 156: That I cannot tell either.
C1 cha 152: If I meant to widen it, it would widen without limit, but doing so has no meaning. Space merely widens.
C2 cha 172: Would it give you the picture to call it the space you imagine inside your head? Inside your head you can widen imagined space as far as you like.
C3 cha 156: But doing so does not produce any productive phenomenon. It is an abstract explanation, but there is no other way to put it.

キャプション1: Can I go anywhere from here?
A1 cha 158: Yes, that is possible. The age of the dinosaurs or the far end of the universe, either is possible.
A2 cha 180: However, you cannot go physically; you can do no more than see and hear what happens.
A3 cha 168: And I present a scenario at each point I think important, so which place in which age you go to depends entirely on my will.
A4 cha 166: I am sorry to say it, but I should like /VAR/-sama to follow my guidance and view the story from this world.
キャプション2: Do stories of the future come up too?
キャプション3: Do stories of the past come up too?
B1 cha 170: As for stories of the future―
B2 cha 168: No, nothing so far ahead. 2 years at the most, I suppose.
B3 cha 156: As a rule you cannot see anything unrelated to this story. But if some element reached 100 years ahead, you would be able to see it.
C1 cha 152: There are stories of the past as well. A few years, a few decades, and hundreds of years ago.
C2 cha 172: You will have obtained the thing called 'letters' among the references; that is the proof of it.
C3 cha 156: Only what relates to this story can be seen across time. What is unrelated, regrettably...
C4 cha 152: The age differs, but the writing should be such that /VAR/-sama can read it, so do please look.

キャプション1: Not going back to your world?
A2 cha 180: For the present I have no plans to.
B1 cha 170: I believe I once said that 'this world is something like the inside of a dream'.
B2 cha 168: /VAR/-sama views this world through an interface, and I exist in this world by sending my will into it.
B3 cha 156: As long as the real me does not wake, I will not go back.
B4 cha 148: Put that way you may think I am escaping reality, but I came to this world of my own will.
B5 cha 178: It is the same for /VAR/-sama. As long as no thought of returning to your original world works in you, you will go on seeing this world.
B6 cha 160: You may think it vague, but there is no other way to put it.
C1 cha 152: I am glad you understand.
C2 cha 172: So /VAR/-sama is free to come here or to go home. This is that sort of world.

キャプション1: How many people in this story?
A1 cha 158: My memory is hazy, but about 15.
A2 cha 180: Well, that is... the further in you go the richer the characters are, so please take care not to get a heavy stomach...
A3 cha 168: From the first arc to the third there is no great difference.
A4 cha 166: From the fourth arc the air changes completely and many characters are added.
A5 cha 162: For the rest, please see for yourself.

キャプション1: Nobody else in this world?
A1 cha 158: Yes, there is only myself and /VAR/-sama.
A2 cha 180: At present I am shutting out intrusion from outside, so no guest other than /VAR/-sama will come.
キャプション3: Then I can take it easy.
B1 cha 170: You are right; just the two of us, myself and /VAR/-sama, is a lonely thing.
B2 cha 168: But I find it comfortable. The time with /VAR/-sama, who chatters with me like this, puts my heart at ease.
B4 cha 148: Oh dear, I have said something rather embarrassing...
C1 cha 152: Yes, please relax at your leisure, without reserve.
C2 cha 172: This world has no concept of time. You may advance the scenarios at whatever timing /VAR/-sama wishes.
C3 cha 156: Ah, but chattering alone will not do, so to widen the topics, do please advance the scenarios.

キャプション1: Did /立木/ make this story?
A1 cha 158: No, it was not I.
A2 cha 180: Strictly speaking, it was not my will.
A3 cha 168: To begin with, a story is not something someone makes; it is the sum of the tracks of how people thought and how they acted at the time.
A4 cha 166: So if I must say, it comes to this: the characters built this story up.
A5 cha 162: We only follow that story. We do not interfere with it.

キャプション1: Is anyone but /立木/ involved?
A1 cha 158: No, no human besides myself is involved.
A2 cha 180: It is not that I built this world up with a purpose... that is...
A3 cha 168: It is a little hard to explain...
A4 cha 166: The unconscious region of me built this world up. And I am shut inside it. Please think of it that way.
キャプション2: Don't you think of leaving this world?
B1 cha 170: I do not. As long as there are guests who come to this world, I remain here.
B2 cha 168: That is my mission and the reason I exist.
C1 cha 152: Whether I like this world...
C2 cha 172: I do not, in all honesty.
C3 cha 156: However, when the only choices are bad fortune and great bad fortune, one can only choose bad fortune.
C4 cha 152: That is my circumstance.

キャプション1: What happened in /立木/'s world?
A1 cha 158: I wonder... As I said earlier, this world was built by the unconscious region of me, so why it came to be is unknown.
A2 cha 180: If I knew what happened in the world I was in, the purpose of this world coming to be might become clear.
A3 cha 168: At the least, I think it was nothing very good.
キャプション3: Is it hard for you now?
B1 cha 170: It is not that I have lost my memory, but...
B2 cha 168: There are things I too would rather not recall... Forward of me though it is, I should be grateful for your consideration.
C1 cha 152: I wonder... It is my own affair, and yet I do not really know.
C2 cha 172: But it is only because of this world that I can speak with /VAR/-sama. For me even that alone―
C3 cha 156: No, it is nothing.

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 4
A1 cha 158: If I had a question for /VAR/-sama...
A2 cha 180: Let me see: how did you come to take an interest in this world?
キャプション4: Just came to take a peek.
キャプション5: Because I like blood and corpses.
B1 cha 170: I am glad you think so. Since you have come, I want you to enjoy it.
B2 cha 168: Whatever the ending, nothing would please me more than for it to lead to even a little joy for /VAR/-sama.
B3 cha 156: All the same, /VAR/-sama, you do seem very fond of blood. Hee hee hee.
C1 cha 152: Oh? Is this world so well known? It should be posted only in special places.
C2 cha 172: Even so, in this world there are only the two of us, /VAR/-sama and myself. No one else comes.
C3 cha 156: Perhaps parallel worlds exist, and in a world just like this one a person who is my spitting image is receiving other guests.
D1 cha 120: Just came to take a peek...?
D2 cha 169: For that, you seem to have been here a very long time already. Have you perhaps taken a liking to this world?
D3 cha 176: If so, nothing could please me more.
D4 cha 159: Please, savor this world to your heart's content.
E1 cha 101: I see, /VAR/-sama is of that sort after all.
E2 cha 142: That is quite all right; it is precisely such people I want to come to this world, and they should enjoy it.
E3 cha 168: Though as the guide of such a world I too may be thought to have questionable taste.

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 5
A1 cha 158: I have come to want to know all sorts of things about /VAR/-sama.
A2 cha 180: That said, let me try a slightly risky question about myself.
A3 cha 168: What do you imagine my bare face is like?
B1 cha 170: I see; so this mask plays its part in stirring up that sort of imagination.
B2 cha 168: In that case I can all the less take this Noh mask off. I have no confidence of meeting /VAR/-sama's expectations.
B3 cha 156: But I should like /VAR/-sama to go on imagining me as a beautiful woman.
B4 cha 148: I am a woman too. Being thought of that way is a glad thing.
C1 cha 152: It is true; with an injury like that one would not want to be seen. All the more so for a woman.
C2 cha 172: I cannot say whether I have such a mark, but if I did... even then I might not go so far as to wear a mask.
C3 cha 156: Oh, that gives away that there is no bad injury on my face. How careless of me.
C4 cha 152: Yes, I have no particularly conspicuous injury. That much I may say.
D1 cha 120: I see, a perfectly natural guess. If I were too ugly every guest in this world would flee.
D2 cha 169: Of course, being told such a thing does not put me out of temper. That /VAR/-sama takes an interest in me at all is what makes me glad.
E1 cha 101: My word...!
E2 cha 142: Hmm... actually a man...
E3 cha 168: An interesting premise.
E4 cha 156: Then shall I try talking a little like a man?
E5 cha 134: Hey, /VAR/! How about it if I talk like this!? Still feels off?
E6 cha 136: Well, which sex I am doesn't matter either way, so let's get along!
E7 cha 130: But me turning out to be a man, you've got it rough getting mixed up with a weirdo. Hahahaha!
E9 cha 120: A failure of characterization... If anything I have turned into Haruka Niimura. Difficult...

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 6
A1 cha 158: So I may ask another question.
A2 cha 180: Then let me ask another slightly risky question. Talking with you is a pleasure.
A3 cha 168: Which of the characters is to your taste?
B1 cha 170: Natsumi Kogori, I see.
B2 cha 168: A frail girl with a little shadow on her. That sort of thing does stir the imagination.
B4 cha 148: Oh, me... why did I use a word like imagination...
B5 cha 178: Ah, uh, I do not mean it indecently! Only imagination in the sense of what might be hidden in that shadow, that sort of, uh―
B6 cha 160: Oh, me... Why did I make excuses when no one even asked... That makes it worse...
C1 cha 152: Haruka Niimura, is it.
C2 cha 172: A woman who pulls those around her along as the older one, and who carries herself while taking all the care she can.
C3 cha 156: And her plain, unspiteful character must be her charm.
C4 cha 152: But she has a side that fixes hard on an idea, and cannot easily say plainly what is inside her. That this complicates the incident you have seen.
C5 cha 180: If you understand that much of her, she will surely make a good partner.
D1 cha 120: Erina Goto, is it. I see, I see...
D2 cha 169: She is certainly clever, bright, plucky and earnest. Very charming, I think.
D3 cha 176: However, her height is said to be about the average for a fifth-grade girl, so saying you like her is bound to invite misunderstanding.
D4 cha 159: No, I do not suspect /VAR/-sama of such tastes. I was merely speaking of tendencies.
D6 cha 132: I do suspect you.
D7 cha 146: Ah, sorry, I misspoke. I do not suspect you.
D8 cha 155: Yes, not in the least do I suspect you.
E1 cha 101: Ooh, Momoko Goto.
E2 cha 142: She is on bad terms with her sister Erina Goto and is said to be the type who is seldom at home.
E3 cha 168: Momoko Goto is mostly spoken of from her sister's point of view, but seen objectively, is she the type who goes her own way?
E4 cha 156: She seems a woman of considerable independence, so taking hold of her heart may be quite hard.
E5 cha 134: But if /VAR/-sama says you will face that challenging trial, I shall cheer you on with all my strength.

キャプション1: Is there no tea or anything?
A1 cha 158: Tea...?
A2 cha 180: I am sorry; there is nothing in this world you can take in your hand. It is all unreal images...
A3 cha 168: I am most sorry, but could /VAR/-sama provide such things yourself?
B1 cha 170: I am glad you understand.
B2 cha 168: If I ever meet /VAR/-sama in the real world, I should dearly like to take tea together.
B3 cha 156: Talking over tea and sweets is more enjoyable than with nothing at all.
C1 cha 152: Not particularly. If it were set in front of me I would take it, but...
C2 cha 172: ...I have started to want a little tea.
C3 cha 156: But there are no drinks, so I can only bear it.
C4 cha 152: Ah, /VAR/-sama, please pay it no mind and take whatever is in your own world.

キャプション1: I want to lie down a bit
A1 cha 158: Are you tired? Please rest as you like.
A2 cha 180: This world has no concept of time. Please spend it exactly as /VAR/-sama pleases.
B1 cha 170: Is that so. How you spend it is also /VAR/-sama's own freedom.
B2 cha 168: It is a place with nothing in it, but pay me no mind and do as you please.
C1 cha 152: /大文字//揺れ/Haah!!?
C3 cha 156: F-forgive me.
C4 cha 152: Being told so suddenly, I was only a little startled...
C5 cha 180: Uh, waking up with a Noh mask like this in front of your eyes would be most unpleasant, I think, so it would be better to refrain...
C6 cha 180: But if you insist...
C7 cha 168: That, then, another time...

キャプション1: A hint for this scenario
A1 cha 158: A hint? Let me see...
A2 cha 180: In fact I do not know everything myself. Speaking from that vantage―
A3 cha 168: Checking a reference that looks meaningless more carefully, or thinking back over a scene that seemed not to matter.
A4 cha 166: What is called foreshadowing is laid out all over. And not the coded sort, wordplay or riddles.
A5 cha 162: There are many scenes written as plain, clear hints.
A6 cha 159: Erina Goto said it, did she not. Force a hypothesis into being, then set it against the facts and test it.
A7 cha 142: That way may be the best suited for thinking this world through.
A8 cha 133: For a more concrete way of thinking, the reference 'Erina Goto's Memo' is worth consulting.

キャプション1: How many arcs in all?
A1 cha 158: The number of arcs? I have no objection at all to telling you, but...
A2 cha 180: It amounts to what is called a spoiler; do you truly wish to hear?
B1 cha 170: Understood. Then I shall tell you.
B2 cha 168: The scenarios of this world make 5 arcs in all. The volume differs a good deal by arc, though: the longest and the shortest differ by about 5 times.
B3 cha 156: Would it do to say that an arc here means a route split off at some large branch point?
B4 cha 148: A different arc does not mean an entirely different world or dimension.
B5 cha 178: You know that there are branches within the scenarios; please understand that a large-scale branch of that kind divides into different arcs.
B6 cha 160: For instance, what would have happened if the Megasawa City incident had not occurred.
B7 cha 138: This is as much as I can say now. For the rest, please see for yourself.
C1 cha 152: Yes, I think that is best. You will see it with your own eyes in time, so it is better to save the pleasure.

キャプション1: What does that outfit mean?
A1 cha 158: Come to think of it, at the third ending of the Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse] there was someone dressed the same as I am.
A2 cha 180: Shall I say this outfit was simply convenient? If this story has a Noh mask and red vestments that hide a figure, I merely thought I might as well hide with them.
A3 cha 168: So there is no connection between me and the one who appeared then.
A4 cha 166: But this Noh mask and these red vestments are both unreal images.
A5 cha 162: Under these clothes there is only the real me and my clothes.

キャプション1: How about a better outfit?
A1 cha 158: A better outfit? You mean this Noh mask and these red vestments?
A2 cha 180: Yes, as you say, I am aware this outfit is quite eerie, and I certainly have not the courage to walk the town in it.
A3 cha 168: So, as /VAR/-sama says, it is not as if I could not receive you in different dress, nor am I so particular about it.
A4 cha 166: Wanting to show as little of my own person as possible, I chose an imitated outfit.
A5 cha 162: That way my identity is less likely to be known.
キャプション3: If you could choose freely, what would you wear?
B1 cha 170: Um...
B2 cha 168: Thank you. I shall take that as praise.
B3 cha 156: For guiding a world like this, the outfit may be good for the staging.
C1 cha 152: Let me see... if I could hide myself and choose freely...
C2 cha 172: How about Western armor? The type that covers the whole body in metal plate and hides the face completely.
C3 cha 156: I should like to wear that once. Walking about clanking sounds like fun.
C4 cha 152: But it must be heavy. Add a sword and a shield and I might not even be able to walk.
C5 cha 180: ...In that case perhaps I should have worn it here instead. Weight is no matter for an unreal image.
C6 cha 180: No, but... if Western armor came out it might confuse my guests all the more... It does not fit the world at all...
C7 cha 168: After all, this outfit does seem the least bad for me.

キャプション1: More about the characters! 1
A1 cha 158: About the characters, is it.
A2 cha 180: Very well. Which of them shall we talk about?
B1 cha 170: Natsumi Kogori was a bright, lively, spirited girl from early childhood.
B2 cha 168: Because of the April sickness she is drawn with a shadow on her during the scenarios, but past that season you would see a brighter side of her.
B3 cha 156: She is liveliest in summer, and in fall the food is good so she eats heartily and stores up nourishment for winter.
B4 cha 148: Then in winter she idles at the heated table as if hibernating. She does not seem to mind gaining some weight.
B5 cha 178: And in spring her health goes, her weight drops, and she returns to her old shape.
B6 cha 160: She seems to have her own yearly internal cycle.
C1 cha 152: It may surprise you, but as a child Haruka Niimura had long hair and often dressed in a girlish way.
C2 cha 172: She takes a boyish manner now, but she was probably more girlish than Natsumi Kogori back then.
C3 cha 156: I hear that when Haruka Niimura came back from Megasawa City to Motoki-cho she cut her hair right off and her bearing turned somewhat boyish.
C4 cha 152: It is interesting to consider why such a change took place inside her.

キャプション1: More about the characters! 2
A1 cha 158: Next, let me see, shall we make it these two?
B1 cha 170: Erina Goto is probably the type older people take to. She has a detached side compared with others her age, so she seems to find classmates hard to get along with.
B2 cha 168: You will know this already, but behind the cheerful, innocent manner there is a calculating mind.
B3 cha 156: Someone who can understand that much could become a one-of-a-kind friend to her; someone who cannot will think her sly and black-hearted.
B4 cha 148: This story draws her as able to get along with anyone, but that is likely why no scene has her actively engaging with anyone outside the cast.
B5 cha 178: If anything, she suits a person who builds deep relationships within a narrow circle better than one with many friends and wide acquaintance.
C1 cha 152: Momoko Goto ― Erina Goto's older sister. Born early in the year, she is 4 years older than her sister, five school years apart.
C2 cha 172: The bad blood between the sisters is emphasized, but for now the scene that shows its cause ― in fact, you can see it in a much, much later arc.
C3 cha 156: Do they really get along so badly, or are they merely passing each other by somewhere? I should like you to watch that point as well.
C4 cha 152: It is described in one scenario or another: her looks and her figure are both said to be quite something.

キャプション1: More about the characters! 3
A1 cha 158: Then, next are these two.
B1 cha 170: Akane Kogori and Mifuyu Niimura began their association through a certain connection not long after they were born. They seem to be a pair who need each other.
B2 cha 168: Akane Kogori is the type who pulls Mifuyu Niimura along, and I hear she gave her warm counsel over her adolescent troubles in particular.
B3 cha 156: Even after more than 40 years they are still right beside each other, so the bond tying them must be stronger than one would imagine.
B4 cha 148: In fact, I hear Akane Kogori was hooked on pachinko when she was young.
B5 cha 178: But Ryoji Kogori, her sweetheart even then, hates gambling of any kind, so she seems to have kept it secret all this time.
B6 cha 160: If her pachinko past were ever to reach Ryoji Kogori's ears...
B7 cha 138: Hee hee hee hee hee! It thrills me just to imagine it!
C1 cha 152: Mifuyu Niimura's appearance made quite an impact, did it not?
C2 cha 172: She dresses young, yet she is past 40 and it is starting not to work, and Natsumi Kogori seems to think of her as a sad older woman.
C3 cha 156: For all that, I hear she was very shy until she married, so innocent that she could not even talk properly with a man.
C4 cha 152: Her catchphrase then was 'Uugh...', and she was often downcast, so it came out every time.
C5 cha 180: The one who kept supporting her through that, I hear, was Akane Kogori.
C6 cha 180: Akane Kogori is, if anything, the type who could live on her own, but where Mifuyu Niimura was concerned she could not leave her be.
C7 cha 168: Being as they are, that is surely how they have kept a well-balanced association all this time.

キャプション1: More about the characters! 4
A1 cha 158: Next are these two.
B1 cha 170: Talking too much would amount to a spoiler, so I shall avoid the subject of the case; his daughter Natsumi Kogori is quite the daddy's girl.
B2 cha 168: Apparently the two of them still bathe together. She is in her second year of high school now, and still bathing with her father...
B3 cha 156: I could never conceive of it myself, but I learned recently that there are unexpectedly many women like that.
B4 cha 148: But still, I could not... family or not, bathing with the opposite sex is beyond me.
B5 cha 178: Also, he is very fond of drink, and I hear he is a nasty drunk with his daughter and with his neighbor Haruka Niimura.
B6 cha 160: Once he nearly stripped in front of everyone, and Akane Kogori scolded him severely for it.
B7 cha 138: Oh, I have talked of nothing but things that lower Ryoji Kogori's reputation.
B8 cha 104: In fairness to him: he is very capable at work, and always spends his days off with his family.
B9 cha 120: A man who balances work and home; a good husband and a good father, one might say.
C1 cha 152: As for Daijiro Ise, I doubt much explanation is needed...
C2 cha 172: Well, his defining trait is lopsided enough that it can be put in a single word.
C3 cha 156: But apart from that point: a very earnest, good-looking police officer who rises quickly. A most attractive man, I should think...
C4 cha 152: To think that a single hobby could disillusion women to this degree...
C5 cha 180: ...I am sorry, that turned into mere backbiting.
C6 cha 180: I say all this, but it is not that I dislike him. If anything I think him a splendid police officer.
C7 cha 168: Which is just why... how shall I put it...
C8 cha 112: Well, he truly is a disappointing man.

キャプション1: How to use the encyclopedia? 1
A1 cha 158: The encyclopedia is material that sets down this world from an objective viewpoint. It is good to look back over it now and then.
A2 cha 180: Scenarios and references can give you information enough, but subjective matter from the viewing character creeps in, so I find them somewhat short of fair.
A3 cha 168: The encyclopedia is swept clean of such subjectivity, so please use it when you want accurate information.

キャプション1: How to use the encyclopedia? 2
A1 cha 158: Another feature of the encyclopedia is that it holds a great deal of information the scenarios and references never tell.
A2 cha 180: For example, under encyclopedia → Places → Motoki-cho there is an entry called 'Zahha Store No. 35'.
A3 cha 168: In the scenarios Zahha is drawn as no more than a family restaurant, but the encyclopedia carries a great many behind-the-scenes stories about it.
A4 cha 166: To learn the underside of this story, viewing the encyclopedia is surely the best way.

キャプション1: How to use the encyclopedia? 3
A1 cha 158: There are two kinds of encyclopedia unlock: the kind that unlocks and stays as it is, and the kind that keeps updating with the latest information.
A2 cha 180: What keeps updating is People; everything else, once unlocked, does not change to the end.
A3 cha 168: So it is best to check People often and keep the information in order.
A4 cha 166: The other categories hold mostly behind-the-scenes material, so I think they are best read as a breather.

キャプション1: What is your type in men?
A1 cha 158: What!? That subject, all of a sudden!?
A2 cha 180: Um... I have not spoken of such things to anyone much, so I do not know how I should put it...
A3 cha 168: Someone earnest, the sort who would quietly support me without making a show of it... perhaps.
キャプション4: Do you want to be treated on dates?
B1 cha 170: Naturally one cannot live with a person on that alone, so I should want him to have at least a minimum of good sense and a head for money.
B2 cha 168: He need not be rich, and he need not be flashy.
B3 cha 156: When I am finding things a little hard, to be quietly supported is a great comfort.
B4 cha 148: In return I should like to devote myself to him as well, though...
B6 cha 160: L-let us leave it at that!
C1 cha 152: Looks...? Certainly a good-looking man is fine, but it is not something I ask of my own partner.
C2 cha 172: I cannot think looks alone make anyone happy... looks do not matter. Though a lack of cleanliness is a little much...
C3 cha 156: How shall I say it; this may be only me, but...
C4 cha 152: I cannot quite trust good-looking men. I cannot explain it well, but I am simply bad with them...
C5 cha 180: After all, other women would like him too, and I have little confidence that such a man would look only at me...
C6 cha 180: It is not jealousy, but I feel I would be uneasy the whole time we were together, and probably could not bear it partway through.
C7 cha 168: Good-looking people are just right for me at the distance of television and photographs.
D1 cha 120: Being treated on a date...
D2 cha 169: Honestly, I do rather admire the idea. Being treated at the moment that matters, and so on.
D3 cha 176: Ah, by the moment that matters I mean my birthday and occasions of that kind.
D4 cha 159: If I were told we were splitting the bill at my own birthday celebration, I would draw back a little...
D5 cha 128: In return, on his birthday I mean to give him the best hospitality I can.
D6 cha 132: Conversely, to be treated on ordinary dates would feel confining. A one-sided giving is uncomfortable...
D7 cha 146: My ideal date splits the bill as far as possible.
D8 cha 155: And, as you will already have noticed.
D9 cha 110: I have never been on a date.

キャプション1: Do you have a dream?
A1 cha 158: By a dream, do you mean a prospect for the future?
A2 cha 180: To speak honestly, I have none now. Or rather, I had no clear dream before I came here either.
A3 cha 168: I think my days were vague ones, wondering whether I would live on ordinarily and end ordinarily.
A4 cha 166: But I do not believe I spent those days idling. If anything I think they were quite full.
A5 cha 162: Which may be just why my eyes did not turn much toward the future.
B1 cha 170: Well, I think it is a way of thinking much like young people today. Put that way, it may be misleading.
B2 cha 168: For it seems that since the age of ancient Greece people have gone on saying 'young people these days will not hold a dream'.
B3 cha 156: So what one is now was in fact one's own dream. A dream may be a thing that is already there when you notice it.
C1 cha 152: My dream now...
C2 cha 172: For now, my duty is to receive guests here. I have no reason to exist beyond that.
C3 cha 156: Now, rather than a dream, well...
C4 cha 152: No, it is nothing. Please forget it.

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 7
A1 cha 158: A question for /VAR/-sama...
A2 cha 180: You have let me hear so much already that nothing comes to mind at once.
A3 cha 168: But since we have the chance...
A4 cha 166: What sort of character do you think you have yourself, /VAR/-sama?
B1 cha 170: I see, so you are the sort who actively keeps company with your acquaintances.
B2 cha 168: The internet has developed a great deal, so this is an age when one can communicate without meeting face to face ―
B3 cha 156: Still, there is a great difference between actually meeting and not.
B4 cha 148: Whatever I may look like, I am fond of company myself. Otherwise I could not do a guide's work.
B5 cha 178: That said, I prefer a deep and narrow acquaintance to keeping company with many friends.
B6 cha 160: Making a noise with a large group is fun too, but time spent at ease with someone close is exceptional.
B7 cha 138: Oh, I am sorry. Here I am talking about myself.
C1 cha 152: I see; these days not only mail but social media and video calls come easily.
C2 cha 172: What I find most attractive in that ease is meeting people unknown to you. There is a limit to how many one can meet in person.
C3 cha 156: And it is good that one can meet people whose values are close to one's own. To find someone of the same tastes, the internet is now common sense.
C4 cha 152: I have never met anyone unknown to me over the internet, though ―
C5 cha 180: Oh?
C6 cha 180: Hee hee hee, forgive me. In a sense one could say /VAR/-sama and I met through the internet.
C7 cha 168: /VAR/-sama is the first person I ever came to know over the internet.
D1 cha 120: Ah, someone who treasures time alone. I think that is splendid.
D2 cha 169: This is an age when you can get anything and do anything without leaving the house, and just because of that I think treasuring time alone takes considerable skill.
D3 cha 176: This too is possible only in a networked society: you need not go out to buy things, and payment is settled at home. Only someone truly versed in this age can manage it.
D4 cha 159: The only occasion to go out may now be taking out the trash.
D6 cha 132: Could it be that liking to be alone did not mean that at all?
D7 cha 146: Simply that you like being alone because you are bad with people, perhaps...
D8 cha 155: Um, I do sometimes speak from my own assumptions...
D9 cha 110: I consider it a fault of mine. I am sorry for carrying on alone.
E1 cha 101: I see, this is an age when you can choose how you meet people.
E2 cha 142: Once there was a culture of brokering ties: feelings sent in classical verse, matches made by formal introduction. Now that is scarcely seen.
E3 cha 168: In a sense, meeting people has become something you seek out and deepen at your own responsibility. That has good sides and bad.
E4 cha 156: Still, being able to choose how you meet people is a very great thing. If you wish, you can connect easily with anyone in the world.
E5 cha 134: I am glad to have been born in this age.

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 8
A1 cha 158: As for what I still do not know about /VAR/-sama...
A2 cha 180: What hobbies do you have?
B1 cha 170: Well, so you are fond of karaoke. I envy you.
B2 cha 168: I say that because I am rather bad at singing in front of people...
B3 cha 156: There is the option of karaoke alone, but singing itself puts me off a little...
B4 cha 148: But when I see people enjoying karaoke I cannot help envying how purely they enjoy it.
B5 cha 178: Truly, it is a thing that would change with nothing but my own frame of mind.
C1 cha 152: Surfing the internet: I like that too. It really is enjoyable.
C2 cha 172: In my case, once the computer is up I go around all my regular sites, and from there I search out whatever information catches my interest.
C3 cha 156: Oh yes, I saw it said that cherry trees contain a substance related to stimulants. Similar information appears somewhere in this world's story.
C4 cha 152: Because such a substance is in them, spring makes people giddy and perverts come out, or so it goes.
C5 cha 180: Speaking of perverts, there is a summary site ranking the perverts of Japanese history, and I once laughed at it until I held my sides.
C6 cha 180: If it interests you, do search for it on the internet.
C7 cha 168: Um, let me say for the record that it is not that I like deviants.
D1 cha 120: Oh, reading. Being bad with print myself, I truly respect those who like to read.
D2 cha 169: Is it a contradiction for me, guiding a story such as this, to say a thing like that?
D3 cha 176: I am often told the aversion is because I have not yet met a book that suits me...
