D4 cha 159: Come to think of it, in media other than books ― the internet, games ― I have no resistance to reading words.
D5 cha 128: Surely the resistance to print was born from book reports and homework in elementary school.
D6 cha 132: Should the chance arise, I should be glad to be told of any book you recommend.
E1 cha 101: Free games...
E2 cha 142: I see, so that is your answer.
E3 cha 168: Yes, I know very well that /VAR/-sama likes free games.
E4 cha 156: Any further and it becomes a rather recursive remark, so I shall restrain myself. Hee hee hee.

キャプション1: Anything you want to ask me? 9
A1 cha 158: And as for what else I should like to ask /VAR/-sama...
A2 cha 180: Am I any different now from your first impression?
B1 cha 170: Oh, then as a guide I pass. To wait upon my guests so that they enjoy this world. That is my part.
B2 cha 168: From here on I shall serve with all sincerity, so that /VAR/-sama may enjoy this even a little.
C1 cha 152: Oh, have I talked a little too much?
C2 cha 172: At our first meeting I had this eerie outfit and a flat manner of speaking, so I had thought that was my lowest point for impressions.
C3 cha 156: But as we talk and even a little of my own view enters, the personal side of me shows. Is it that this did not suit /VAR/-sama?
C4 cha 152: Everyone finds some people suit them and some do not. Please set that aside and see this world through to the end.
C5 cha 180: If I can show /VAR/-sama the far end of this world, I am satisfied with that.
D1 cha 120: Oh! To think you would say such a thing...
D2 cha 169: /VAR/-sama and I have had a good many conversations by now, and I am glad to be thought of in that way.
D3 cha 176: That said, it is not hard to imagine my first impression was the worst possible, so perhaps there was no lower it could go...
D4 cha 159: But you have kept up this chatter with me so far, and my impression of /VAR/-sama ― if it is not rude to say so ― has certainly grown warmer.
D5 cha 128: I ask for your continued kindness, /VAR/-sama.
D6 cha 132: If ever the day comes that I show my bare face...
D7 cha 146: No, it is nothing.

キャプション1: What is Motoki-cho like?
A1 cha 158: Ah, I have not yet spoken to you of the setting.
A2 cha 180: It is written up in the encyclopedia as well, so you can get objective information there, but if I venture my own thoughts ―
A3 cha 168: I think it a very good town. In the year Shiyo 800 nature and development stand together there, and the people revel in it.
A4 cha 166: Only, there are not a few voices fearing that nature will go on being destroyed as the population grows.
A5 cha 162: It was a thinly populated area to begin with, so the locals may be finding it a little more stifling by degrees.
キャプション3: Did the population change that much?
B1 cha 170: Motoki-cho is a basin ringed by mountains, so there is no sea, and the rivers are small.
B2 cha 168: I hear the basin was once a broad plain. For hundreds of years a small number of people lived there in step with nature.
B3 cha 156: There are few rivers, but being a basin the water flows in easily, so small ponds and well water were plentiful.
B4 cha 148: So with the rich bounty of the mountains gathered in, they would never have wanted for food.
C1 cha 152: About 50 years ago it was a truly small town of some 1000 people. Then one event changed it greatly.
C2 cha 172: Yes: the goshinboku in Central Park. Its growing there is what set the population rising.
C3 cha 156: They say you must see it to understand, but the goshinboku draws people, and I hear more and more have moved to Motoki-cho charmed by that cherry.
C4 cha 152: As a result, to revive the town as a cherry-blossom spot, they planted more cherries here and there all over it.
C5 cha 180: As a result many tourists came, Motoki-cho developed rapidly, and by the year Shiyo 800 the population was about 40,000.
C6 cha 180: It is said that by the year Shiyo 815 the population will pass 150,000.
C7 cha 168: So by the year Shiyo 800 the rich are racing each other to buy land, apartment buildings are going up everywhere, and an unprecedented property bubble is under way.
C8 cha 112: Locals call those suddenly grown rich this way, with some irony, 'the Motoki new money'.
C9 cha 106: This story should appear somewhere in the scenarios too.

キャプション1: What kind of place is Megasawa City?
A1 cha 158: I have not explained that one yet either, have I.
A2 cha 180: Megasawa City is a city spread over a wide area, with a population of about 200,000. It faces mountains and a vast lake.
A3 cha 168: Until the Megasawa City murders began, it seems to have been a perfectly ordinary city with nothing in particular to set it apart.

キャプション1: Zahha has a lot of strange menu items

B1 cha 170: Let me see, from what I have heard...
B2 cha 168: For a while there was a menu item of sushi rice dipped in coffee.

B5 cha 178: It is no longer on the menu in Shiyo 800, and I doubt many locals ever ordered it.

C4 cha 152: It was apparently 'sauteed lamb brains.'
C5 cha 180: Not a familiar ingredient to Japanese people, but apparently commonly eaten across the Middle East.
C6 cha 180: The taste is rich and creamy, with a melting texture, they say.

D2 cha 169: Just as it sounds: two foods came out at once with their flavors swapped exactly.
D3 cha 176: For example, chawanmushi and pudding came together: the chawanmushi tasted like pudding and the pudding like chawanmushi, confusing eyes and tongue.
D4 cha 159: The most striking was swapping a plate and cookies: cookies made of ceramic, served on a plate made of cookie.
D5 cha 128: The edible ones were quite hard too, and many people bit the ceramic ones by mistake.
D6 cha 132: Like this, Zahha sometimes has odd items on its menu.

キャプション1: You bring up a topic 3

C7 cha 168: In this way, I select the routes that should be shown to you, /VAR/-sama.

キャプション1: What is an efficient way to view point-spending references?

A5 cha 162: The mysteries of this world run deep, and are smeared with blood and hatred.
A6 cha 159: Even if every tragedy seems at a glance to have been avoided, whether that truly leads to a happy ending―
A7 cha 142: Please confirm that with your own eyes, /VAR/-sama.

D9 cha 110: I brought up the topic myself, and what am I even saying...

キャプション1: But Eiichiro Niimura dies after this, right?
A1 cha 158: What an abrupt way to put it... Yes, it is as you saw in an earlier arc.
A2 cha 180: If one suddenly lost a happiness one had finally obtained this way, it is no wonder Mifuyu Niimura could not sort out her feelings and fell ill.
A3 cha 168: However, there is a cause that drove her so far as to cause the Megasawa City case and the flaying case.
A4 cha 166: You will see it later, but it is precisely because she was originally honest and simple that she came to cause such insane cases.
A5 cha 162: When you think of it that way, human beings are truly frightening creatures.

キャプション1: What's Primavera's Deluxe Afternoon Tea Set?
A1 cha 158: It is what Mifuyu Niimura and Akane Kogori were eating on the house.
A2 cha 180: The price is 9,000 yen before tax, and one set serves two, so it comes to 4,500 yen per person. It comes with a drink of your choice, with refills.
A3 cha 168: An afternoon tea set is food arranged on a three-tier stand, made up, from the bottom, of sandwiches, warm dishes and desserts. That is the same at any shop.
A4 cha 166: The sandwiches use domestic organic vegetables, Sawa Prefecture contract-factory ham and own butter; the eggs are said to be from free-range hens of the owner's kin.
A5 cha 162: The warm dishes are mainly scones, which you can enjoy in three flavors: plain, cheese and raisin. The cheese and raisins are deliberately European.
A6 cha 159: The top tier holds a cake of the day and pudding. The owner was a patissier, I hear, so of course they are made in-house; I am told most effort goes here.
キャプション2: You sound just like one of the staff
キャプション3: Isn't there an even better menu item?
B1 cha 170: Oh my, may I take that as a compliment? As a guide, I must know everything about this world that I possibly can.
B2 cha 168: That said...
B3 cha 156: Naturally, I have never tasted even an ordinary afternoon tea set, let alone Primavera's.
B4 cha 148: I explained it all, but to me it is an unknown world. I am very curious what it could possibly taste like.
B5 cha 178: Delicious tea and a luxurious afternoon tea set; I would like to experience that at least once.
C1 cha 152: An even better menu item?
C2 cha 172: This is only a rumor, but the owner often makes staff meals from leftover ingredients.
C3 cha 156: The one popular among the staff is a duck salad with foie gras and caviar.
C4 cha 152: Regulars call it the phantom salad; it is off the regular menu, and if ingredients remain even after the staff meal, it is sold at 6,500 yen a portion.
C5 cha 180: So around 8 p.m., when the staff have all finished their meal, it gets quite crowded on weekends with people hoping to get a chance at that salad.
C6 cha 180: However, it is only a rumor, so even I do not know whether it really exists...

キャプション1: What do you think about how Haruka Niimura was adopted?
A1 cha 158: Oh, a question back to me about a scenario. That is rather refreshing.
A2 cha 180: Indeed, I suppose their decision divides opinion.
A3 cha 168: Perhaps because I am young and inexperienced, my impression is that what they did was a little light.
A4 cha 166: There may have been exchanges not told in the main story, but giving a child up for adoption, even for the sake of a best friend, is something I would find very hard.
A5 cha 162: It is also a matter that affects the relatives on the Kogori side. What would the Kogori couple's parents and relatives think?
A6 cha 159: However, for those two to go on as best friends, adoption may have been an unavoidable option. I do not think the Kogori couple gave her up gladly, either.
A7 cha 142: They chose better over best, the optimal solution over the right answer, I suppose.
キャプション2: Giving her up for adoption was a good choice
B1 cha 170: I see, so you think what they did was reasonable.
B2 cha 168: Indeed, had they not given her up for adoption, the relationship between Mifuyu Niimura and Akane Kogori might have grown strained.
B3 cha 156: Not only that, Akane Kogori reached that conclusion out of a wish to help Mifuyu Niimura.
B4 cha 148: Luckily those around them understood, but it is for the Kogori and Niimura families to decide. Criticism from others may be meaningless.
C1 cha 152: Yes, it is only natural that you would think so, /VAR/-sama.
C2 cha 172: I believe I have told you before that I select the routes appearing in this world and show them to you, /VAR/-sama.
C3 cha 156: So a route in which they chose not to give her up for adoption surely exists as well.
C4 cha 152: But I am sorry, even I cannot tell you what that route contains. I judged it unnecessary without even needing to look.
D1 cha 120: Yes, I do think it is a very difficult problem.
D2 cha 169: It is a problem swayed not only by husband and wife but also by the opinions of those around them, so what choice one makes must vary endlessly.
D3 cha 176: Watching them, I thought that at such times it may be good not to force yourself to want the best ending, and to choose the better, optimal solution instead.
D4 cha 159: If a wall appears in your life too, /VAR/-sama, perhaps thinking that way will make it a little easier.
D5 cha 128: I do not mean to lecture you, /VAR/-sama, but aiming for a passing grade rather than a perfect score is lighter on the heart.
D6 cha 132: Fortune and misfortune are hard to tell apart, and life has its ups and downs.
D7 cha 146: Yes, just like me...

キャプション1: How will Haruka Niimura feel when she learns she was adopted?
A1 cha 158: Hmm, that is indeed a problem too. Her life was decided before she was even born.
A2 cha 180: But looking at how things have gone, even if she learns she was adopted she will surely accept Mifuyu Niimura as her mother, and their bond as parent and child will go on.
A3 cha 168: As for Natsumi Kogori too, they will surely go on being best friends as before.
A4 cha 166: But the Kogori couple is a delicate matter. Told that her friend's parents, the neighborhood Ojisan and Obasan, were her real parents, would she not be bewildered?
A5 cha 162: Haruka Niimura has a rather sensitive side, so even if she tries to carry on as before, would it not feel awkward somehow?
A6 cha 159: Haruka Niimura and the Kogori couple: once she knows they are her real parents, how do you think they should relate to each other?
キャプション2: I think they can just go on as before
キャプション3: I want them to value being parent and child too
キャプション4: I think it's better if they don't get too involved
B1 cha 170: Yes; to put it dryly, whether anything changes because they are biologically parent and child depends on how they themselves see it.
B2 cha 168: Even if the Kogori couple came forward as her real parents, I do not think they would try to build a special relationship...
B3 cha 156: But whether Haruka Niimura can do that... Even if she can, she would still end up being careful, and it may take some time.
B4 cha 148: Yes, going on as before should be the most settling...
C1 cha 152: I see; perhaps rethinking how they relate a little is also an option.
C2 cha 172: Even having given her up for adoption, to the Kogori couple she is still their own daughter. I cannot imagine their wish to dote on her as parents fading with time.
C3 cha 156: Rather, one could say that it is because of this history that they took part in the Megasawa City case all the more.
C4 cha 152: Perhaps, somewhere, the Kogori couple wanted to be of use to their daughter as parents.
C5 cha 180: Then, from a daughter's position, how can she be of use to her real parents? That may be something she will think about all her life...
D1 cha 120: I see, better not to get involved... That is not an opinion that should be rejected either.
D2 cha 169: Only...
D3 cha 176: I wonder... then her relationship with Natsumi Kogori might become delicate too...
D4 cha 159: If knowing the true relationship would create friction somewhere, better not to get involved...
D5 cha 128: Hmm...
D6 cha 132: It is a difficult problem, but whether Haruka Niimura could make such a choice...
D7 cha 146: I hope it will not become a strain on her.

キャプション1: When Eiichiro Niimura fell, didn't you hear something?
A1 cha 158: What?
A2 cha 180: Did something like that happen?
A3 cha 168: I am terribly sorry, I did not notice.
A4 cha 166: Surely you are mistaken, /VAR/-sama.

キャプション1: Was Eiichiro Niimura pushed by someone?
A1 cha 158: Pardon?
A2 cha 180: /VAR/-sama, what are you saying? There were many witnesses, and it has long been said there was no foul play, has it not?
A3 cha 168: Or do you have some reason to think so?
キャプション2: I saw it in a scenario
キャプション4: It was written in the Encyclopedia
B1 cha 170: In a scenario...?
B2 cha 168: Then please watch it once more. There should have been no such person.
C1 cha 152: In a reference...?
C2 cha 172: Ah, I believe there was such a reference. Erina Goto as a small child said, "Someone pushed him."
C3 cha 156: However genius a girl she may be, it is after all the testimony of a small child. It is not worth considering.
C4 cha 152: Please, do not let it trouble you.
D1 cha 120: The Encyclopedia...?
D2 cha 169: The Encyclopedia contains nothing but objective information. There can be no such vague information in it.
D3 cha 176: Surely you misunderstood something somewhere.
D4 cha 159: Since I say so, it must be so. This world obeys my will alone, after all.
E1 cha 101: I did?
E2 cha 142: Surely not; I would never make such an irresponsible remark. As a guide, I take the utmost care not to say anything misleading.
E3 cha 168: If I did say it, I apologize and correct it. But no such thing happened.

キャプション1: What kind of work does Ryoji Kogori do?
A1 cha 158: It is in the Encyclopedia as well, but he works for a manufacturer that develops cell phones and smartphones.
A2 cha 180: It is not a subsidiary of anyone, but it seems to do mainly contract development for large corporations, so the company name almost never comes out into the open.
A3 cha 168: His job, roughly speaking, is development engineer.
A4 cha 166: However, he knows little about programs or software and seems to work exclusively on assembling electronic components.
A5 cha 162: Also, the company itself is small, so it seems he builds prototypes himself and takes them along to do sales work too.
キャプション3: How did he learn those skills?
B1 cha 170: Hmm, I wonder. I am sorry, but his annual income is really beyond me...
B2 cha 168: Well, judging from how they live, they do not seem particularly troubled for money, nor do they seem to have any special debts.
B3 cha 156: However, Akane Kogori also works part-time, so his income is probably not extremely high either.
B4 cha 148: Well, they are what you would call a middle-class household. Not rich, but earning enough to get by without hardship.
C1 cha 152: He went to a technical high school in Motoki-cho. The town has two: Motoki High School (general) and Motoki Technical High School (industrial).
C2 cha 172: It seems he met Eiichiro Niimura at the technical high school, and they joined the same company.
C3 cha 156: The bond between Mifuyu Niimura and Akane Kogori tends to get the attention, but it is easy to imagine these two also built a strong bond of trust.
C4 cha 152: By Shiyo 800 he has been promoted, and I hear he is sent on business trips here and there.
C5 cha 180: Ryoji Kogori is in technical development, not a job one pictures with business trips, but he seems to fly around explaining products to clients and factories.

キャプション1: Will Natsumi Kogori's April sickness ever be cured?
A1 cha 158: As you saw, Natsumi Kogori has had a danger sense since early childhood, and at the same time suffered from April sickness.
A2 cha 180: The Kogori couple took her to the hospital as well, but it seems the cause could not be found after all.
A3 cha 168: In other words, I suppose April sickness arises from some special cause.
A4 cha 166: Even I do not know the cause, but those around her seem to think the memory of Eiichiro Niimura's death has become an unseen trauma.

キャプション1: So Natsumi Kogori and Erina Goto knew each other long ago
A1 cha 158: So it seems. However, judging from how they are in Shiyo 800, they do not seem to remember that far back.
A2 cha 180: Meeting at Zahha was also by chance, and if asked whether some connection came of it, I suppose not really.
A3 cha 168: Even though they went to the same elementary school, being a grade apart, they probably had few chances to interact.
A4 cha 166: Also, Erina Goto was the type who stood out from those around her, so perhaps she relied all the more on her older sister, Momoko Goto.
A5 cha 162: So she probably did not try to widen her circle of friends at elementary school, and lived a life of going straight home.
A6 cha 159: She was famous as a genius girl, but considering Natsumi Kogori's personality, she would not have been all that interested in such a title.

キャプション1: What kind of work does Akane Kogori do?
A1 cha 158: She works at a pachinko parlor in Motoki-cho, and seems to have worked there since Shiyo 795.
A2 cha 180: Now that Natsumi Kogori is in high school and needs less looking after, it seems she takes shifts for as many hours as she can.
A3 cha 168: Well, it is said she works at a pachinko parlor because of a small connection in the past. She seems to want to keep it hidden, though.
A4 cha 166: Incidentally, Ryoji Kogori hates gambling, and at first he opposed his wife working at a pachinko parlor.
A5 cha 162: But when he learned the pachinko parlor paid 1,800 yen an hour, he reluctantly agreed, I hear.
A6 cha 159: Well, I suppose he consented because there was no other way to support the household budget.

キャプション1: About Mifuyu Niimura's hairstyle
A1 cha 158: As you saw, Mifuyu Niimura wore a ponytail until she was around thirty, and in Shiyo 800 she does not seem to tie it up in particular.
A2 cha 180: The hairstyle was Akane Kogori's idea; I hear she switched to a ponytail as a makeover in high school.
A3 cha 168: She has kept almost the same hairstyle for over ten years now, so Mifuyu Niimura herself must be afraid to break that style by her own judgment.
キャプション2: What about her hairstyle in Shiyo 800?
B1 cha 170: When she moved back to Motoki-cho, she seems to have settled on the hairstyle you saw in the Jusatsu Arc and elsewhere. A sign of a strong inner change, perhaps.
B2 cha 168: For better or worse, it gives the impression she broke free of her reliance on Akane Kogori.
C1 cha 152: Once she was around thirty, even Akane Kogori said, "Isn't that hairstyle too young for your age?", but Eiichiro Niimura seems to have liked it.
C2 cha 172: After the marriage, she must have kept that hairstyle to please Eiichiro Niimura.

キャプション1: Why did the Niimura family move to Megasawa City?
A1 cha 158: After losing Eiichiro Niimura she fell ill at heart, and she was referred to a doctor for treatment, it is said.
A2 cha 180: It is closer to the Arata settlement than Motoki-cho, so in her mind it must have been a reasonable option.
A3 cha 168: She herself is all alone in the world, so such decisions were probably easy for her to make.
キャプション2: Did her mental illness get better?
キャプション3: Weren't there any good doctors in Motoki-cho?
B1 cha 170: After moving to Megasawa City she was hospitalized for a while, and Haruka Niimura was placed in a children's home until she started elementary school.
B2 cha 168: That doctor seems to have been truly skilled; she was discharged in March of the following year, Shiyo 791, and mother and daughter were able to live together again.
B3 cha 156: Had there been no problem of bullying against Haruka Niimura, it might have been a modest but fairly peaceful daily life...
B4 cha 148: However, Mifuyu Niimura kept going to the hospital after that, and one could not say she was in remission.
B5 cha 178: That is why, perhaps, her heart weakened again over Haruka Niimura's bullying problem, and decisions were made that led to the Megasawa City case.
B6 cha 160: Surely remission was difficult unless she faced her husband's death head-on.
C1 cha 152: Well, at the time Motoki-cho was not as prosperous as in Shiyo 800, but there were hospitals and doctors enough.
C2 cha 172: For Mifuyu Niimura, more than finding a fine doctor, the biggest thing was probably wanting to leave Motoki-cho, with its painful memories.
C3 cha 156: Illnesses of the heart are difficult. They are invisible illnesses, caused by something with no shape. Curing them requires a fitting amount of time.
C4 cha 152: So I say, but I am no doctor, so I cannot speak too grandly.

キャプション1: What are Akane Kogori's parents like?
A1 cha 158: Akane is their only child. On retiring at the mandatory age, they moved from Motoki-cho to West Sawa City and seem to be enjoying their life in old age.
A2 cha 180: Both of them have travel as a hobby, so I hear they save steadily and regularly go off to various places.
A3 cha 168: Where the father is from is unclear, but he speaks with an accent so thick that hardly anyone but family can make it out.
A4 cha 166: Basically, both seem easygoing and not bothered by small things. After all, they cared for the newborn Mifuyu Niimura and had her spend time with their daughter.
A5 cha 162: So they must have accepted giving Haruka Niimura up for adoption with a big heart. Some would call it outrageous to let go of a long-awaited grandchild.
A6 cha 159: In any case, I think they are a very good couple and very good parents.

キャプション1: What are Ryoji Kogori's parents like?
A1 cha 158: Ryoji Kogori's father died of illness when he was a child, and he grew up with his older brother in a single-mother household.
A2 cha 180: It was a life far from wealthy, but to ease his mother's burden even a little, he entered high school on a scholarship and worked part-time on the side.
A3 cha 168: After he found work he began sending his mother some money, and it seems she is able to live without hardship for now.
A4 cha 166: That is why, it seems, she was overjoyed when Ryoji married. The son she had put through so much had found a good partner, after all.
A5 cha 162: Ryoji's older brother is still single and seems to live with their mother in Minakami City, the prefectural capital. They run a convenience store, I hear.
A6 cha 159: The mother seems to want the older brother to marry soon. But the brother has plans to expand the business and shows no interest whatsoever in marriage.
A7 cha 142: In any case, they seem able to lead a peaceful life.

キャプション1: About Haruka Niimura's look
A1 cha 158: Come to think of it, Haruka Niimura's look is quite different between Shiyo 790 and Shiyo 800.
A2 cha 180: The Niimura couple doted on their daughter, and in her early childhood they seem to have dressed her as cutely and girlishly as they could.
A3 cha 168: Her hair was long, and her clothes were mainly girlish one-piece dresses.
A4 cha 166: But as Haruka Niimura grew, she began choosing her clothes and hairstyle by her own taste, and by Shiyo 800 she has a boyish look.
A5 cha 162: Mifuyu Niimura does not mean to fuss over how her grown daughter dresses, but as you saw, she frowns when she walks around after a bath without even a towel.
A6 cha 159: Mifuyu Niimura seems to wish she would acquire a little more femininity.

キャプション1: What was that drug?
A1 cha 158: That is the very devilish drug that made the Megasawa City case and the rest possible.
A2 cha 180: It is apparently made in the Arata settlement, and was presumably sent at Mifuyu Niimura's request...
A3 cha 168: But in my view, even if such a drug exists, I very much wonder why it has not been known to the world until now.
A4 cha 166: I mean, wouldn't you agree? It existed hundreds of years ago, yet it has never come out into the world until now; I sense something deliberate in that.
B1 cha 170: Exactly. Would it be reasonable to think that, for some reason, information on the drug never leaked out of the Arata settlement?
B2 cha 168: Come to think of it, if such a drug became public, the world could become a frightening place. If it were used in, say, international crimes...
B3 cha 156: Perhaps, out of such concerns, information on the drug was hushed up by some kind of pressure.
B4 cha 148: All of it remains speculation, though...
C1 cha 152: Is that so...? Even in Shiyo 800, to keep making a drug that seems likely to break the law without anyone knowing is a little hard to believe...
C2 cha 172: Well, if you say it just happened not to be known, perhaps that settles it, but was there some secret for keeping information on the drug from leaking?
C3 cha 156: In any case, it remains speculation, though.
D1 cha 120: Ah... yes... I am sorry; though I am a guide, I do not know the key information...
D2 cha 169: I did look into it in various ways, but I could not obtain detailed information about that drug...
D3 cha 176: Well, perhaps it means the information is not needed to see their happy ending through.
D4 cha 159: Excuse me. Please, do not let it trouble you.

キャプション1: Is Akane Kogori into pachinko?
A1 cha 158: There is no sign of her playing pachinko as of Shiyo 800, so she seems to have quit soon after marrying.
A2 cha 180: By her own account, it is not pachinko she likes but the characters in its animations; how true that is remains uncertain.
A3 cha 168: But since she got hooked for a while on pachinko she started half in fun, she seems to have at least a side that likes gambling.
B1 cha 170: I do not know whether such a temperament is inherited, but it seems certain that mother and daughter played games close to gambling.
B2 cha 168: And that, once she was in high school, gave rise to tragedies like that Russian-roulette takoyaki―
B3 cha 156: Blood will tell. Perhaps a similar temperament lies hidden in Haruka Niimura as well?
B4 cha 148: I can hardly picture Haruka Niimura gambling, but I do hope someone keeps a close eye on Natsumi Kogori so she does not become a gambler.
C1 cha 152: Probably not. Being seen going in and out of a pachinko parlor by Mifuyu Niimura seems to have hit her quite hard.
C2 cha 172: Even so, since she works at a pachinko parlor, whether she can be said to have quit completely is debatable.
C3 cha 156: She may have taken the step of using her job as a pachinko parlor clerk to stay close to her hobby.
C4 cha 152: Perhaps she works there not to help the household budget, but so she can go in and out of a pachinko parlor openly...
C5 cha 180: Hee hee hee, anything more would be pure speculation, and might needlessly lower your image of Akane Kogori.
C6 cha 180: In any case, she no longer seems to play pachinko now. As a customer, at least, that is.

キャプション1: Why did the Gotos come to Megasawa?
A1 cha 158: Simply a family trip, it seems. And they happened to meet at the zoo, I suppose.
A2 cha 180: However, Natsumi Kogori had already started elementary school, so it means Momoko Goto was skipping school for the trip.
A3 cha 168: I have never missed school for a trip myself, and I do wonder about missing school to travel...
キャプション2: Kids shouldn't skip school for a family trip
キャプション3: Isn't it fine once in a while?
B1 cha 170: I see. Actually, it bothered me too, so I looked into it―
B2 cha 168: Up to 30 days of absence a year is no problem legally. The schools do not seem to make an issue of it either.
B3 cha 156: By one statistic, 40 percent approve of keeping children out of school for trips and 60 percent oppose. Hardly an overwhelming majority against.
B4 cha 148: In the Goto family's case their studies will be fine, so it comes down to family policy. It may be improper for an outsider to butt in.
B5 cha 178: Well, even so, I can hardly bring myself to think of missing school for a trip.
C1 cha 152: Oh, so that is how you see it. I see, I see...
C2 cha 172: Absences for family reasons that are too frequent can be seen as withholding compulsory education, but as you say, /VAR/-sama, once in a while is probably fine.
C3 cha 156: Still, skipping school for a trip... I wonder how that feels.
C4 cha 152: While everyone else sits in class, you are enjoying a trip; perhaps you can bask in that sense of superiority.
C5 cha 180: Ah, but then you fall behind in class, so whether you can keep up after the trip...
C6 cha 180: Weekday trips do interest me a little, but they take courage after all. For me the hurdle is rather high.
C7 cha 168: But...
C8 cha 112: I'd like to try it just once...

キャプション1: Do you like studying, /立木/?
A1 cha 158: Eh? Ah, because I said I would worry about falling behind if I skipped school for a trip.
A2 cha 180: I would not say I love studying, but I make sure not to forget homework I am given. I hate panicking afterward.
B1 cha 170: My favorite subject? Let me see... um...
B2 cha 168: It may be quicker to name the subjects I am bad at than the ones I like.
B3 cha 156: I am truly hopeless at math and physics... I try hard to understand them, but perhaps my method is bad: the more I study, the more I dread them...
B4 cha 148: Honestly, I even end up disliking the teacher. Hate the monk and you hate his robe, as they say.
B5 cha 178: Comparing my scores with the average, the teacher's methods do not seem to be at fault, so this too must be a matter of strengths and weaknesses.
B6 cha 160: Ah, just remembering numbers makes me go pale...
C1 cha 152: If you ask whether I am serious, that puts me in a bit of a spot...
C2 cha 172: I just do not like panicking afterward. Getting scolded for skipping homework, or having my grades drop. I would rather not get caught up in that sort of thing...
C3 cha 156: Well, in exchange, I am overjoyed on days with no homework. I can laze around all day.
C4 cha 152: Hee hee hee, it seems I am not so serious after all. I simply hate feeling bad later.
D1 cha 120: Could that be called serious...? I just treat assigned work as a given and get through it...
D2 cha 169: True, there are plenty of classmates who never do their homework, so if you call me serious, perhaps I am on the serious side.
D3 cha 176: But even when I do my homework properly, I barely manage average scores, so I suspect my natural brains are not that good.
D4 cha 159: That is why someone like Erina Goto is a real mystery to me. What on earth does one have to eat to become like that―
D5 cha 128: Ah, of course, Erina Goto was an enormous eater. Which means...
D6 cha 132: Right, I will eat a lot too and send nutrition to my brain. I should get smarter by as much as I eat! That is the plan!
D8 cha 155: /VAR/-sama, did you not just look at me as if I were an idiot?
D9 cha 110: I-I was joking! Of course eating a lot cannot make you smarter! Ahahahaha...

キャプション1: Everyone died in Shiyo 790, huh
A1 cha 158: You mean the story where Mifuyu Niimura killed the Kogori couple and Haruka Niimura in Megasawa City.
A2 cha 180: Yes. This way, far from a happy ending, they cannot even reach the Jusatsu Arc or the Meicho Arc.
A3 cha 168: But this too is one of the endings they chose. A small choice gives rise to many futures.
A4 cha 166: Of course, that ending is not everything, so please think of it as one possibility.

キャプション1: So Haruka Niimura basically had chunibyo?
A1 cha 158: That is a rather blunt way to put it... True, one could see it that way.
A2 cha 180: But from her position, she cast a curse and it actually came true, so it is no wonder she turned out that way.
A3 cha 168: If anything, she used such curses only when truly necessary, so I do not think her personality was suited to chunibyo.
A4 cha 166: By the way...
A5 cha 162: Have you ever had chunibyo, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション4: Heh, even now the black flame embraces me...
B1 cha 170: Oh ho, now this is interesting. I hear chunibyo comes in many kinds: the evil-eye type, the eleventh-grade-syndrome type, the nihilist type...
B2 cha 168: Which one did you fit, /VAR/-sama?
B3 cha 156: Ah, my apologies; it is a dark past for you now. Asking such things is tactless.
B4 cha 148: No doubt you have writhed in agony remembering the past.
B5 cha 178: Yes, I will not tell anyone. That you had chunibyo, /VAR/-sama.
B6 cha 160: After all, you having chunibyo is a thing of the past, /VAR/-sama.
B7 cha 138: You, /VAR/-sama, with chunibyo, now of all times...
B8 cha 104: After all, you do not have chunibyo, /VAR/-sama.
C1 cha 152: Is that so? Forgive me.
C2 cha 172: If you had chunibyo, /VAR/-sama, I wonder what kind of setting would get you fired up.
C3 cha 156: In any case, they say those who had chunibyo bitterly regret that disgrace later.
C4 cha 152: Well, that too is the folly of youth; it comes about precisely because the hearts of adult and child are mixed.
C5 cha 180: But if, like Haruka Niimura, what you wished for actually came true...
