B2 cha 168: Well, setting aside whether that is true, beyond that...
B3 cha 156: But... did she recognize danger only through Eiichiro Niimura's voice...
B4 cha 148: If I remember, in the Jusatsu Arc...
B5 cha 178: Ah, no, it is nothing.
C1 cha 152: Ah, um... well...
C2 cha 172: How embarrassing. What I know is actually limited, too.
C3 cha 156: I certainly cannot lie to you, /VAR/-sama, so what I do not know, I intend to say plainly that I do not know.
C4 cha 152: I am sorry to be such an unreliable guide, but I will still support you with all my strength.

シナリオ名: 今は楽しいことだけを。
キャプション1: Then tell me whatever you can 1
A1 cha 158: Let me see... In fact, there are facts not revealed in the scenarios or References.
A2 cha 180: Do you remember? In the Jusatsu Arc's 'In the Moon's Shadow,' Natsumi Kogori and Haruka Niimura fled deep into the mountains by train, but were attacked by the shinigami.
A3 cha 168: Then Haruka Niimura was about to be cut with the nata, but in the nick of time Natsumi Kogori shoved her aside and she was not cut.
A4 cha 166: Which would mean Mifuyu Niimura tried to hack Haruka Niimura to death... Do you see her true intent, /VAR/-sama?
B1 cha 170: Oh my, you knew already? Then there is no need for me to explain.
C1 cha 152: Then let me give you just a small hint about this.
C2 cha 172: Look closely at the scene in the Jusatsu Arc's 'In the Moon's Shadow' where Haruka Niimura is nearly cut. It happens in an instant.
C3 cha 156: In it, you can see evidence that denies a clear intent to kill. If she truly meant to kill―
C4 cha 152: Hee hee, please check the rest for yourself.

シナリオ名: 今は楽しいことだけを。
キャプション1: Then tell me whatever you can 2
A1 cha 158: Hmm... in that case...
A2 cha 180: The Jusatsu Arc's 'What I Can Do' is the scenario showing what happened at the hospital after Haruka Niimura was hit by a car deep in the mountains and fell into a coma.
A3 cha 168: That time, Erina Goto urged Akane Kogori to turn herself in. Let me explain that in detail.
A4 cha 166: There was a scene where Akane Kogori worried about Haruka and Mifuyu Niimura, was there not?
A5 cha 162: In other words, Akane Kogori knows Mifuyu Niimura is involved in the case. From this, one can infer that Akane Kogori is involved too.
A6 cha 159: Moreover, before speaking to her own daughter Natsumi Kogori, she at once tried to check on Haruka Niimura, who should be a stranger to her.
A7 cha 142: Erina Goto likely took that to mean Akane saw Natsumi Kogori and Haruka Niimura as equals.
A8 cha 133: Assuming the two are sisters, she could roughly deduce who did the killing in the Megasawa City case, so she pressed Akane Kogori.
A9 cha 110: Erina Goto called it 'a hunch,' but Akane Kogori's confession proved she had seen the truth.

キャプション1: Then tell me whatever you can 3
A1 cha 158: Then the next thing to talk about would be...
A2 cha 180: In the Meicho Arc's 'Bright Red ××' there is a scene where Mifuyu Niimura prepares for the crime: the scene where she returns home and readies drugs and such.
A3 cha 168: As that depiction shows, Mifuyu Niimura was not regularly obtaining drugs and other weapons from the Arata settlement.
A4 cha 166: She was only using what was left over from the Megasawa City case.
A5 cha 162: So one can state flatly that the Arata settlement truly had nothing to do with the flayed-body case.
A6 cha 159: To begin with, she committed the crime on impulse after Ryoji Kogori's negotiation, so the Arata settlement could not have lent a hand.
A7 cha 142: The question here is how she could also prepare items like the red robes and Noh mask in such a hurry.
A8 cha 133: Do you know what was behind it?
B1 cha 170: Oh my, forgive me. Perhaps that was too easy for you, /VAR/-sama.
B2 cha 168: Well, that is how it is. Hee hee hee.
C1 cha 152: Do you remember at what times and in what places Mifuyu Niimura committed her crimes after the flayed-body case?
C2 cha 172: Dark places at night: that is the situation common to the whole Jusatsu Arc.
C3 cha 156: Put simply, the Noh mask was a toy, and the red robes a simple red coat, gathered in a hurry.
C4 cha 152: In a dark place, even if Haruka Niimura saw her, she could not tell the quality of the gear.
C5 cha 180: Likewise, I would like to say Haruka Niimura did the same when she trapped Mifuyu Niimura at home, but...
C6 cha 180: No shop had the 'old woman' mask Haruka Niimura asked for, so Daijiro Ise hurriedly asked the prefectural police in Minakami City to rush one to the scene.
C7 cha 168: It cost 30,000 yen before tax, so Daijiro Ise was apparently scolded by his superior.
C8 cha 112: Well, considering it caught the culprit behind a string of grisly murders, perhaps it was a bargain.

キャプション1: Then tell me whatever you can 4
A1 cha 158: Mm... let me see...
A2 cha 180: Shall I tell you about Mifuyu Niimura's origins?
A3 cha 168: As you know, her mother died in childbirth and her father of illness as she entered high school. No grandparents, no siblings: she was all alone in the world.
A4 cha 166: She has distant relatives, but she hardly knew them, so she grew close to someone nearer: Akane Kogori, that is, the Tonosaki family.
A5 cha 162: But that does not mean she lived with the Tonosakis; she lived alone from high school on. Thanks to that, she can handle housework almost perfectly.
A6 cha 159: In fact, Mifuyu Niimura's parents apparently eloped, marrying over everyone's objections. So perhaps her birth was not much celebrated.
A7 cha 142: Growing up like that, she likely longed strongly for a warm family.
キャプション2: What did she live on after her father died?
キャプション3: Didn't she have any other friends?
B1 cha 170: Her father seems to have left a considerable fortune. To raise Mifuyu Niimura, he worked desperately day and night to earn money.
B2 cha 168: Thanks to that she never wanted for money until she found work, but that image of her father must have stayed with her strongly.
B3 cha 156: After she married and Eiichiro Niimura died, she worked at any hour, at any job. All so Haruka Niimura would never know poverty.
B4 cha 148: The person called Mifuyu Niimura seems to have been strongly shaped by these images of family.
C1 cha 152: There were classmates who were kind to her, but she was painfully shy then, and could not open up to them as she did to Akane Kogori.
C2 cha 172: Also, after her makeover men began approaching her aggressively, so perhaps her classmates found her harder to be around.
C3 cha 156: Though the makeover did not change her inner self or how she dealt with people, so this is only about how others saw her.
C4 cha 152: In short, Akane Kogori was her one true best friend, and so she found others hard to trust. Quite like her, given her extreme side.

キャプション1: Then tell me whatever you can 5
A1 cha 158: And then, um...
A2 cha 180: In the Jusatsu Arc's 'I'm Sorry After All.' Akane Kogori burst into the Goto home dressed as the shinigami. Let me tell you the truth behind it.
A3 cha 168: As the References around that point show, Akane Kogori came home to look for the missing Natsumi Kogori.
A4 cha 166: There she ran into Mifuyu Niimura, who was preparing to kill, took her weapons and drugs, and headed to the Goto home.
A5 cha 162: With Ryoji Kogori murdered, whatever happened next held only despair. She believed Mifuyu Niimura and the Arata settlement were about to reach for them.
A6 cha 159: So her true aim was to burst into the Goto home and flee Motoki-cho with Natsumi Kogori and Haruka Niimura.
A7 cha 142: But the police were there as well, so she could not reveal who she was at once, and in the end she was shot dead.
A8 cha 133: She knew the police were watching the Goto home, so she had to disguise herself like that and rely on the drug.
B1 cha 170: Come to think of it, it said Mifuyu Niimura later went missing. She did not kill herself, and the police did not catch her.
B2 cha 168: She could not take Haruka Niimura with her, so it is hard to imagine she fled to the Arata settlement alone.
B3 cha 156: Was she killed when Akane Kogori took her weapons, or did something else happen...
B4 cha 148: I am sorry, but this is something even I cannot tell.
C1 cha 152: If I remember, Haruka Niimura moved to the Arata settlement alone, seen off by Natsumi Kogori and Erina Goto.
C2 cha 172: But she went missing for two years, and the two headed to the Arata settlement to look for her.
C3 cha 156: And at the end a girl with odd eyes appeared, and the Jusatsu Arc ended, I believe.
C4 cha 152: As you have surely realized, the one who appeared at the end was Kana Niimura, Haruka Niimura's cousin.
C5 cha 180: But what became of Haruka Niimura, and what Kana Niimura was trying to say, I am sorry, but...
C6 cha 180: One thing is certain, though: Haruka Niimura is alive in the Arata settlement.

キャプション1: Is the Arata settlement surprisingly modern?
A1 cha 158: The Arata settlement has electricity, gas, water and even internet access, so it is not an area all that cut off from the world.
A2 cha 180: However, the Arata district is state-owned land, so ordinary people cannot enter freely. It seems fine with the permission of its head, Erika Niimura, though.
キャプション2: Why do people live on state-owned land?
キャプション3: Why did it become state-owned land?
B1 cha 170: The order is the other way around: it is better to say that a place where people already lived was designated state-owned land.
B2 cha 168: To the state, people living there seems to be no great problem, so it lets them go on living on the state-owned land.
B3 cha 156: I do not know the circumstances in that much detail myself, though...
C1 cha 152: Actually, long ago, a certain group apparently intervened in the Arata settlement.
C2 cha 172: Its purpose, it is said, was the cherry trees of the Arata district: they wanted them and carried most of them away.
C3 cha 156: I do not know whether that is true, but if so, why they took those cherry trees, and why it then became state-owned land, is a real mystery.
C4 cha 152: Its becoming state-owned land suggests that, at the very least, that group had ties to the state.
C5 cha 180: This part is full of mysteries, and I am sorry, but I do not know either.

キャプション1: What food comes from the Arata settlement?
A1 cha 158: The Arata district is said to be rich in rare animals and plants.
A2 cha 180: But because of their peculiar naming sense, the names alone seem to call weird food to mind; the taste, though, is said to be exceptional.
A3 cha 168: The reason for such names is apparently to keep outsiders from overharvesting them.
キャプション2: It isn't sold in the outside world?
キャプション3: Why is there food like that?
B1 cha 170: As I said before, the Arata district is state-owned land, so outsiders almost never enter.
B2 cha 168: So the food is hardly likely to reach the outside world either.
B3 cha 156: It is also said the Arata district is state-owned to protect such rare animals and plants, but whether that is true is unknown.
B4 cha 148: Either way, if you want to taste Arata cooking, you would need the Grand Witch's permission to visit as a guest.
C1 cha 152: The soil of the Arata district is very fertile; not only rare varieties but even ordinary ones grow big and well.
C2 cha 172: Long ago, some men of power aimed at that fertile land and tried to take the Arata district for themselves, but history says they were driven off by force.
C3 cha 156: With soil this attractive, people have long coveted the Arata district, and one can guess it became state-owned land to put a stop to that.

キャプション1: From what I've seen, the Arata settlement doesn't look that sketchy
A1 cha 158: True; modern IT has made its way into the settlement too, so its common sense is not wildly out of step with the world.
A2 cha 180: Well, there are unique customs such as its funerals, but basically they do not seem so different from people in the outside world.
A3 cha 168: But it is a fact that the drug and the customs that aided the Megasawa City case exist. Judging by surface appearances may be dangerous.
A4 cha 166: Well, that may become clear little by little.

キャプション1: What is Erika Niimura like?
A1 cha 158: As you saw, she seems to be terribly fond of impressions and cosplay.
A2 cha 180: Haruka Niimura was apparently coached in impressions by Erika Niimura; one could say that is how she got Mifuyu Niimura arrested in the Meicho Arc.
A3 cha 168: Also, despite her age she has otaku hobbies; she seems to like anime and such.
キャプション2: Why does she have hobbies like that?
B1 cha 170: Actually... the previous Grand Witch was apparently an anime fan, and when she spread the word to Erika Niimura, Erika got hooked even deeper than she was.
B2 cha 168: I believe one of the references covers it in detail, so if you already have it, please look there.
B3 cha 156: Even so, dragging the people around her into it as well... What a nuisance.
C1 cha 152: Quite a painful sight, it seems. She cosplays as teenage girls without a second thought, and sometimes even attends such events.
C2 cha 172: It may be hard to tell from the silhouette, but her figure really is good. Still, considering her age... it is a bit...
C3 cha 156: Yes, well, this could turn into bad-mouthing, so I will leave it at that...

キャプション1: Is Chigaya Niimura really that bad a drunk?
A1 cha 158: I am not sure I need to be the one to say such a thing...
A2 cha 180: Yes, it seems she is quite a violent drunk.
A3 cha 168: Beautiful in appearance, and well-mannered when sober. If not for drink, she would surely attract many men...
A4 cha 166: Well, as you can guess, because of her excessive drunkenness, the men all make sure never to deal with her again.
A5 cha 162: Chigaya Niimura does seem to want a wonderful match, but once she has had a drink, she would rather drink and have fun than that...
A6 cha 159: And the next morning, she apparently writhes under her futon in self-loathing.
A7 cha 142: She does seem to reflect on it, but once a little drink is in her, she stops caring. A violent drunk indeed...
A8 cha 133: I sincerely hope a big-hearted man appears who will take such drinking habits head-on.

キャプション1: Doesn't Natsumi Kogori make a weird sound when she yells?
A1 cha 158: Oh, you noticed.
A2 cha 180: Yes, when Natsumi Kogori gets excited, p-sounds, that is, pa pi pu pe po, seem to slip into her speech here and there.
A3 cha 168: Haruka Niimura has apparently called her out on it, but she herself just answered, "I don't know."
A4 cha 166: Well, like sneezes or screams, exclamations differ from person to person, so in Natsumi Kogori's case it is just a pronunciation that stands out a little.
キャプション2: Does it have to do with the case?
B1 cha 170: Ah... I see... So that is what you think...
B2 cha 168: To be blunt...
B3 cha 156: It has nothing to do with it, practically speaking. Yes, of course not. Mm-hm.
B4 cha 148: If Natsumi Kogori were attacked while alone and screamed, that scream might let one identify the victim, but...
B5 cha 178: Well, please think of it as a mere quirk of hers.
B6 cha 160: Seriously, it has nothing to do with anything...
C1 cha 152: Hm... the reason Natsumi Kogori says pa pi pu pe po...
C2 cha 172: Perhaps saying pa pi pu pe po relieves the stress that builds up when she gets excited?
C3 cha 156: Or as a child she watched an anime character who talked in pa pi pu pe po, and because of it, even now, pya... pa pi pu pe po is a habit?
C4 cha 152: Pa pi pu pe po... pa pi pu pe po...
C5 cha 180: Pya pyu
C6 cha 180: I did not trip over my tongue, you know? My enunciation is rather good.
C7 cha 168: See, pa pi pu pe po! Pa pi pu pe po! Pa pi pu pe po!
C8 cha 112: Pa pi pu pe po! Pya pa pi pu pe po!

キャプション1: Is an Arata-style contest really ghost stories?
A1 cha 158: Yes, such a tradition does seem to exist.
A2 cha 180: Originally, they say, the aim was to toughen the spirit by telling ghost stories, so one could move without fear even at night deep in the mountains.
A3 cha 168: So a rather peaceful rule came about: when a quarrel breaks out in the settlement, it is settled with a ghost-story contest.
キャプション3: I'm not good with scary stories...
B1 cha 170: Oh, you would like to hear my ghost story?
B2 cha 168: Hee hee, you say rather amusing things.
B3 cha 156: Very well, I shall tell one in the next topic.
C1 cha 152: You are not good with scary stories, /VAR/-sama...?
C2 cha 172: Ufufufufu! You must be joking again! You have been steeped in the stories of this world for so long, and you say you are scared of scary things!
C3 cha 156: That said...
C4 cha 152: Actually, I am quite bad with ghost stories myself...
C5 cha 180: No, I am interested, but I cannot listen unless I am wrapped in a blanket.
C6 cha 180: Ah, you just thought, "What is she saying, dressed like that?" didn't you?
C7 cha 168: But... scary stories really are not my thing...

キャプション1: Mika Tachiki's Ghost Story Night Show 1
A1 cha 158: Then, if I may be so bold, I shall present a ghost story.
A2 cha 180: Once upon a time, there was a single office worker.
A3 cha 168: He took the shinkansen on a business trip and bought a station bento. What he bought was a shumai bento.
A4 cha 166: He sat in his seat on the shinkansen and eagerly opened the lid of that shumai bento.
A5 cha 162: And what do you know!
B1 cha 170: Wha...!
B2 cha 168: No...! That was my best one...!
B3 cha 156: To think it was such a famous story...
B4 cha 148: Ugh... I shall work harder...
C1 cha 152: One of the shumai had vanished!
C2 cha 172: Strange! There was clearly a gap the size of one! The man was so startled he shut the lid.
C3 cha 156: He calmed down and opened the lid once more...
C4 cha 152: And what do you know, this time every shumai had vanished! All the shumai that should have been there were gone!
C5 cha 180: The shumai had vanished, I tell you! The shumai...!
C6 cha 180: Oh, huh...? Not scary...?
C7 cha 168: W-well, the punch line is that the shumai were stuck to the underside of the lid, so it is a little funny story...
C8 cha 112: Oh, good grief! How embarrassing! I thought it would be either scary or funny...!
C9 cha 106: Ugh... I must tell a better story...

キャプション1: Mika Tachiki's Ghost Story Night Show 2
A1 cha 158: Th-this time I shall pick a properly scary one!
A2 cha 180: Long, long ago, there was a blasphemous man. A man who did not revere the Buddha and would relieve himself on the Jizo statues.
A3 cha 168: But had divine punishment finally come? The man's wife died in an unforeseen accident.
A4 cha 166: Was this divine punishment after all? Thinking so, the man rushed to a temple and asked for an exorcism.
A5 cha 162: The man knelt formally while the head priest desperately drove at the spirit. At last it seemed to appear through his body, and he collapsed with a thud.
A6 cha 159: The priest held the man in his arms and cried, "You evil spirit! What do you want! What is it you're after!"
A7 cha 142: Then these words came out of the man's mouth.
B1 cha 170: Ah, um...
B2 cha 168: Yes, it is a funny story: you think he collapsed from an evil spirit, but his legs just fell asleep from kneeling formally...
B3 cha 156: W-well, I am bad with scary stories! This is the best I can do!
B4 cha 148: I am sorry... I could not tell a satisfying story...
C1 cha 152: Ah, I am terribly sorry! Was it too scary!?
C2 cha 172: Th-the truth is, it is a funny story disguised as a scary one, and, um, um, um, I did not mean to frighten you...!
C3 cha 156: Ugh... I am a guide, yet I am bad at talking...
C4 cha 152: Next time, a better story...

キャプション1: Mika Tachiki's Ghost Story Night Show 3
A1 cha 158: Th-then I shall take the plunge and tell you the real deal this time!
A2 cha 180: A high school girl was standing on a train, enjoying social media on her smartphone.
A3 cha 168: She left the station and walked home, looking at her smartphone. Up to there, all was well...
A4 cha 166: The moment she entered her home, a message arrived on her social media. It said―
A5 cha 162: Nice to meet you! I followed you! Looking forward to it! Along with that comment was attached a photo of her entering her home.
B1 cha 170: Yes, from the train all the way home she was absorbed in her smartphone and forgot to pay attention to her surroundings.
B2 cha 168: In a society like this, let us be careful of the eyes around us too.
B3 cha 156: Ah, scary...
C1 cha 152: In other words, someone she had never met followed her and found out where she lived.
C2 cha 172: What is more, absorbed in social media, she did not notice someone peeking at her screen on the train, and her account was exposed.
C3 cha 156: Being followed is one thing, but if such a person even knows your social media account, your privacy will be gravely violated.
C4 cha 152: Please be careful too, /VAR/-sama...

キャプション1: Mika Tachiki's Ghost Story Night Show 4
A1 cha 158: Then, my best one...
A2 cha 180: In a mansion overseas there lived a very beautiful girl. Her name was Elsa, and the mansion was very lovely and large, the envy of everyone.
A3 cha 168: Elsa's heart was as beautiful as her looks; she could be kind to anyone. Everyone raised her with great care.
A4 cha 166: One day, Elsa got into a car with the master of the mansion and went out to town.
A5 cha 162: In truth, it was Elsa's first time outside the mansion, and she was very excited. Big trees, rivers, cars: all of it was scenery Elsa had never seen.
A6 cha 159: Then the car stopped at a certain place. A very lively place, crowded with people.
A7 cha 142: And the master handed Elsa over to a man.
A8 cha 133: Huh? Why? Elsa wondered. Then the man who had taken Elsa shouted to the crowd:
A9 cha 110: Step right up! Today's star item! A sow raised with loving care, Elsa!
B1 cha 170: It may be a bit different from a scary story, but the twist is that the opening makes you think she is a human girl, when she was really livestock.
B2 cha 168: With a longer story it might have been more immersive, but too long would be a bit much, so this is about right.
B3 cha 156: Yes, the point-of-view character is not necessarily human.
C1 cha 152: Yes, she was raised with care so she could be sold dear as meat.
C2 cha 172: Calling the pig girl beautiful was surely the livestock farmer's point of view. To an ordinary person, whether she was beautiful would be impossible to tell.
C3 cha 156: A girl so beloved, yet since the aim from the start was to sell her, she was sold off as meat.
C4 cha 152: It surely happens in real society too, but I am rather bad with stories like this...
C5 cha 180: Oh, I love eating meat, though. It is just that, when the point of view gets shifted like this...

キャプション1: Okay, time to tell a ghost story
A1 cha 158: Ugh...
A2 cha 180: I am terribly sorry; actually, that was the last of my material...
A3 cha 168: You see, with scary stories I either cover my ears or try to forget them right away, so my stock of ghost stories is extremely thin...
A4 cha 166: I-if that is not enough for you, I think it would be good to advance the main scenarios! Th-those are surely much scarier than my stories!
A5 cha 162: Ugh... I should have collected proper ghost-story material for times like this...

キャプション1: What kind of company does Mifuyu Niimura run?
A1 cha 158: Ah, that does not come up in the main story, so let me explain here.
A2 cha 180: At present she seems to run a security camera wholesale business in Motoki-cho.
A3 cha 168: As you saw in the Jusatsu Arc, Motoki-cho had little crime-prevention awareness and few security cameras, so Mifuyu Niimura spotted a chance there.
A4 cha 166: Having come close to committing murder herself, she perhaps came to think about Motoki-cho's safety instead.
A5 cha 162: When she started out she had no knowledge of machines or camera installation, but she founded the company aiming to make the town safe.
A6 cha 159: From there she studied all sorts of things and widened her network, and by Shiyo 800 she has even opened a Tokyo branch; business seems to be going well.

キャプション1: Who is Motokizakura-sama?
A1 cha 158: As in the ghost-story scenario, Motokizakura-sama is a yokai from a Motoki-cho urban legend.
A2 cha 180: However, there are many Motokizakura-samas, and they seem to differ in whether they are good or evil.
キャプション2: Why did such an urban legend come about?
キャプション3: Do Motoki-cho residents believe in it?
B1 cha 170: Hmm... The origin of Motokizakura-sama... I had never thought about it.
B2 cha 168: But at the very least, the rumor is confirmed to have existed since Mifuyu Niimura and the others were small.
B3 cha 156: So it is quite an old story, yet for some reason it still seems widespread in Motoki-cho.
C1 cha 152: Most think of it as no more than an urban legend, but as in Natsumi Kogori's story, there really are families that worship Motokizakura-sama.
C2 cha 172: Still, worshipping something on the level of an urban legend seems a bit much to me...
C3 cha 156: Perhaps there is some deeper circumstance behind the origin of that rumor.

キャプション1: So Motokizakura-sama was in a magazine
A1 cha 158: Ah, yes, there was a reference with that kind of description.
A2 cha 180: That a goshinboku research team in Motoki-cho was killed, and that the culprit was Motokizakura-sama.
A3 cha 168: I see, blaming a yokai for such an inexplicable case. Well, that is a common enough origin for an urban legend, I suppose.
キャプション2: But didn't Motokizakura-sama exist before the case?
B1 cha 170: Um...
B2 cha 168: Ah, that is right. According to the reference, it is written as if its existence was confirmed before the case, so it may have been around much earlier.
B3 cha 156: Forgive me. For a guide to get the chronology wrong...
C1 cha 152: Hee hee hee, of course not. It is only an urban legend. Nothing more than a form of popular entertainment.
C2 cha 172: But something must have given rise to that urban legend. That trigger was a case that happened long ago in Motoki-cho.
C3 cha 156: Come to think of it, no story about that case has come up even once so far...
C4 cha 152: Well, perhaps it means it has nothing to do with this world. It may not be worth worrying much about.
C5 cha 180: It should be enough to keep it in the back of your mind.

キャプション1: What kind of college student is Chigaya Niimura?
A1 cha 158: She is enrolled at a university in Tokyo. As of Shiyo 800 she is a third-year, and she seems to have no particular problems with her studies.
A2 cha 180: Well, as she said herself, she seems to put effort not only into her studies but also into enriching her private life.
A3 cha 168: She said her nights are spent either at drinking parties or at her part-time job.
キャプション2: What part-time job does she have?
キャプション3: What are the drinking parties like, exactly?
B1 cha 170: She seems to work in the kitchen of a family restaurant. With looks like hers, she apparently avoids jobs that put her in public view.
B2 cha 168: She once served customers at the same restaurant too, but being from Arata she knew little of the world, and customers often hit on her, so she got little work done.
B3 cha 156: She also takes gig jobs in the gaps between her university lectures, I hear. Moving work, event setup and the like.
C1 cha 152: To put it bluntly, they are activities in search of a wonderful encounter. In the story they are consistently called "drinking parties."
C2 cha 172: With looks like hers she is invited often, so she never lacks chances to meet people.
C3 cha 156: But as you know, she is a terrible drunk, so it ends at meeting; it has never once developed into anything more.

キャプション1: Why did Chigaya Niimura go to Tokyo?
A1 cha 158: She seems to have a strong interest in social welfare, and there is no faculty around the Arata settlement where she could study it.
A2 cha 180: Well, at her age, a strong longing for Tokyo is hardly unusual, I think.
キャプション2: Will she be a social worker?
B1 cha 170: She seems not to have decided on a future career yet, but in fact, as of April Shiyo 800, she is set to study abroad.
B2 cha 168: At a university in Northern Europe, I believe, planned for around summer.
B3 cha 156: Her future after that is unconfirmed, but I think she will return to the Arata settlement eventually.
B4 cha 148: She may have gone to Tokyo, but her attachment to the Arata settlement seems great.
C1 cha 152: I wonder... That much I cannot tell, but...
C2 cha 172: In the Arata settlement, the only one younger than Chigaya Niimura is her sister Kana Niimura, so the settlement is fated to fill up with old people eventually.
C3 cha 156: Perhaps she means to look after everyone herself in preparation for that.
C4 cha 152: Well, this is only my own idea; there is no knowing without asking her.

キャプション1: Is a new case on the way!?
A1 cha 158: Yes, it seems certain that some tragedy will occur in the Shigatsu Arc too.
A2 cha 180: Is it because the Megasawa City case was avoided, or because Natsumi Kogori and the others went to the Arata settlement...
A3 cha 168: On that, I would very much like you to see for yourself, /VAR/-sama.
A4 cha 166: One thing I can say: even compared with the Megasawa City case and the flayed-body case, there are a great many baffling points, which may be hard to grasp.
A5 cha 162: Please make good use of the references and the encyclopedia to sort out the information.

キャプション1: Tell me about the cherry tree at the Niimura main house
A1 cha 158: At the Niimura main house there is a tree resembling the goshinboku in Central Park, Motoki-cho.
A2 cha 180: It is certainly a large and splendid tree, but it seems to be old, and it does not appear to have the power to trigger Natsumi Kogori's danger sense.
A3 cha 168: It still blooms with many cherry blossoms now, but there are probably only a few more years left to see them.
キャプション2: Are there no other cherry trees?
キャプション3: Why is there such a splendid tree here?
B1 cha 170: No, in the Arata settlement there is only the one at the Niimura main house.
B2 cha 168: Of course, there were originally many cherry trees, but some organization or other apparently carried them all off several decades ago.
B3 cha 156: How true that is remains uncertain, but Natsumi Kogori will probably not be able to use her danger sense in the Arata settlement.
C1 cha 152: It is said that the settlement began when the founder of the Arata settlement was drawn to those cherry trees and put down roots.
C2 cha 172: So it was not people who brought the cherry trees; one could say people gathered because the cherry trees were there.
C3 cha 156: Besides, the land of Arata has rich soil, so the founder was surely drawn by how pleasant it was to live there, too.

キャプション1: Are there branches in the Shigatsu Arc too?
A1 cha 158: Yes, there certainly are. I could tell you a little more, but...
A2 cha 180: Would you like to hear?
B1 cha 170: Understood.
B2 cha 168: In fact, you have already passed every branch point. So from here on there is no branch splitting off into another route.
B3 cha 156: Now, how about it? Can you tell where the branch points were, /VAR/-sama? Hee hee hee.
C1 cha 152: That is fine too, I think. It would be a spoiler, after all.
C2 cha 172: Of course, even if you did listen, I would not say anything that spoils your fun...

キャプション1: What kind of girl is Kana Niimura?
A1 cha 158: As of April Shiyo 800, Kana Niimura is 10 years old, born and raised in the Arata settlement.
A2 cha 180: Having grown up in such an environment, her physical ability seems quite high. She walks to school on that mountain road every day.
A3 cha 168: However, there are no children her age in the Arata settlement, so she seems to have spent her time mostly with her sister Chigaya Niimura.
キャプション2: She's a pretty crude kid, huh
B1 cha 170: True. Well, Kana Niimura is the only child in the settlement, so she must have been doted on as she grew up.
B2 cha 168: In turn, she often joined in the adults' talk, which is probably how she picked up crude knowledge like a drunk old man's.
B3 cha 156: But she seems to get along well with others at school, so I imagine she knows when to switch.
C1 cha 152: Yes. Since she was little she has played at hunting in the mountains with her sister Chigaya Niimura, so one could call her a wild child.
C2 cha 172: The adults hunt with guns, but children cannot be allowed to handle such things, so she hunts relying more on physical ability.
C3 cha 156: That said, not every adult in the settlement can move as well as she does.
C4 cha 152: Think of Kana Niimura as especially outstanding.

キャプション1: Tell me about the witches of the Arata settlement
A1 cha 158: The witches of the Arata settlement are something like priests. Only women of the Niimura family can hold the post.
A2 cha 180: In Shiyo 800 there is the Grand Witch, Erika Niimura; the other witches are Mifuyu Niimura and the newly appointed Chigaya Niimura.
A3 cha 168: Well, though they are called witches, they have no supernatural powers; it is fine to think of it simply as a post.
A4 cha 166: They also do work like officers who run the settlement. Simply put, the Grand Witch is something like the head of a neighborhood association.
キャプション3: They don't have any supernatural powers?
B1 cha 170: Yes. Apart from the eerie name of the post, what they do is not so far beyond human understanding.
B2 cha 168: Besides, several hundred years have passed since the post of witch came about, so parts of it have probably become a mere formality.
C1 cha 152: They seem to have no power of that kind. Mifuyu Niimura, who came from outside, holds the post too, after all.
C2 cha 172: I think you may safely assume that gaining supernatural power through the succession rite is impossible.
C3 cha 156: However, there are cases like Natsumi Kogori, who has danger sense. It may be hasty to say no supernatural phenomenon at all can exist in this world.
C4 cha 152: Well, Erina Goto would think there is some scientific basis even for that power of premonition.

キャプション1: Why does the Grand Witch speak Portuguese?
A1 cha 158: It is said to be the influence of Westerners who reached the Arata settlement long ago.
A2 cha 180: It is said that the concepts of "witch" and "shinigami," which did not exist in Japan at the time, also came from them.
A3 cha 168: The teachings and words of the Westerners must have come to be used as rituals just as they were.
キャプション2: Is Erika Niimura fluent in Portuguese?
キャプション3: So it's influenced by foreign countries?
B1 cha 170: No, in fact she says she does not really understand anything beyond the ritual terms either.
B2 cha 168: Well, it is probably like the nembutsu in Buddhism. Practiced so many times the mouth remembers it, while the meaning stays unclear.
B3 cha 156: So the people of the settlement should know almost no Portuguese. It is used only during rituals.
C1 cha 152: You may take it that way, but the culture of the Arata settlement is influenced not only by the West but also by Buddhism and Shinto.
C2 cha 172: The tenth-year memorial service came up before; that is said to be the influence of Shinto.
C3 cha 156: What is strange, though, is that the Arata settlement has no idol to worship. I would not find it strange for there to be one...
C4 cha 152: Was there never such a thing, or did one exist and vanish for some reason?
C5 cha 180: A polytheism like Shinto does not necessarily need idols, and even monotheisms sometimes forbid idol worship...
C6 cha 180: Well, it just struck me personally as a little strange that with so many cultures mixed together, there is not a single idol.

キャプション1: How many people live in the Arata settlement?
A1 cha 158: Roughly 20 to 30 people. In households, just under 10, I would say.
A2 cha 180: The headcount is low for the number of households because in modern times more young people have left Arata to live in cities.
A3 cha 168: Eiichiro Niimura is a good example. He left Arata and built his life in Motoki-cho. Well, it is what is called depopulation.
A4 cha 166: Also, in this settlement one often sees people with the same surname in separate households.
A5 cha 162: They originally share the same ancestors, but over several hundred years the households came to split at some point, I hear.
A6 cha 159: It is common in ordinary Japanese society too. Total strangers with the same surname are nothing unusual.
A7 cha 142: The Arata settlement is a small-scale version of that: the same ancestors at root, but separate houses.
キャプション2: Did the family have a falling-out long ago?
キャプション3: Has no one moved in from elsewhere?
B1 cha 170: I wonder. Over several hundred years, branching into separate houses is hardly unusual...
B2 cha 168: But over such a long time, there surely were falling-outs of a sort.
B3 cha 156: Whether it was a big incident or a small one, I cannot tell...
B4 cha 148: I only caught wind of it myself, but I have heard that several hundred years ago some people left the Arata settlement.
B5 cha 178: Apparently there was something on which they decisively disagreed with the settlement's course.
B6 cha 160: Well, a settlement with this much history has surely seen mergers and splits.
C1 cha 152: Not many nowadays. Long ago, Westerners settled there, and people who collapsed on the road were rescued and stayed for good, I hear.
C2 cha 172: So the population seems to have been larger in the past. At its largest, about 100 people.
C3 cha 156: But nowadays no one collapses on the road, let alone moves to the Arata district, which is state-owned land. The population can only keep shrinking.
C4 cha 152: Unless someone marries in from outside like Mifuyu Niimura and settles in Arata with her child, there will be no newcomers.

キャプション1: How many people stay in the settlement?
A1 cha 158: As of Shiyo 800, nearly all the residents stay in the settlement. The outflow from Arata I mentioned was most noticeable in the Shiyo 750s and 760s.
A2 cha 180: That is because by around Shiyo 770 there were no longer enough people to leave; the children then were just Eiichiro and Kotaro Niimura and the late Sakura Niimura.
A3 cha 168: Probably, as the population shrank, the will to protect the settlement themselves grew stronger.
キャプション2: Do people who left long ago come back for funerals?
キャプション3: So a lot of people now are attached to the settlement
B1 cha 170: No, nowadays even their whereabouts seem unknown. As you know, it is a settlement with a bit of a dark side, and quite a few left because they hated that.
B2 cha 168: So even while people from the settlement are alive, some never show themselves in Arata again. Effectively, they have cut ties.
B3 cha 156: Well, in that case, those who cut ties are very unlikely to be involved in cases tied to the Arata settlement. They left because they hated it.
C1 cha 152: Indeed, now it seems only people who love the Arata settlement live there.
C2 cha 172: There are exceptions like Mifuyu Niimura and Chigaya Niimura, but their lives are simply based outside; their attachment to Arata seems unchanged.

キャプション1: Is Sakura Niimura's death central to the Shigatsu Arc?
A1 cha 158: /VAR/-sama, a superb observation. That is exactly right.
A2 cha 180: Sakura Niimura's death eventually covers this Arata settlement in a menacing air. This is what lies at the heart of the tragedy this time.
キャプション2: Is it connected to the Megasawa City case?
キャプション3: Why does it involve the Motoki-cho group?
B2 cha 168: Well, I think this much is all right to tell, so shall I share a little?
B3 cha 156: As you saw, Mifuyu Niimura confessed to Erika Niimura what happened in Megasawa. Sakura Niimura overheard, ran out of the settlement, and was found dead.
B4 cha 148: Naturally, in the routes where the Megasawa City case happened, Mifuyu Niimura would not have made such a confession.
B5 cha 178: In other words, when the Megasawa City case occurs, there was nothing to make Sakura Niimura run out of the settlement and die.
B6 cha 160: Hee hee, that is all I can say. I hope it helps you even a little, /VAR/-sama.
C1 cha 152: What a person comes to fear is subjective. It depends not on others' will but on the will and values of the one who feels fear.
C2 cha 172: Do you understand what that means?
C3 cha 156: Because of values hard for us to grasp, people grow hostile toward things that would not normally frighten anyone, and in time it grows into a major case.
C4 cha 152: The Motoki-cho group may have elements that are seen as dangerous in that way.
C5 cha 180: Hee hee, that is all I can say.

キャプション1: How did the old people kill themselves?
A1 cha 158: It seems to have varied a great deal.
A2 cha 180: Alone deep in the mountains, some slit their own throats, some fell from cliffs to their deaths.
A3 cha 168: What is certain, though, is that it was not the doing of settlement people. Given the times and methods, settlement people were in no position to do it themselves.
キャプション3: Isn't it weird that everyone is cleared every time?
B1 cha 170: Hanging...?
B2 cha 168: I see, hanging is the standard method of suicide. Certainly, if one means to kill oneself, it takes less trouble...
B3 cha 156: Was there some reason they could not hang themselves, or should the judgment of suicide itself be reconsidered...
B4 cha 148: Either way, the manner of death is certainly a little baffling. It may be worth keeping in mind.
C1 cha 152: I see, now that you mention it...
C2 cha 172: There are two questions I have. One is that everyone has a solid alibi.
C3 cha 156: The other is that they killed themselves at a time when everyone had an alibi.
C4 cha 152: Dying at precisely a moment when everyone has an alibi seems somehow too perfect...
C5 cha 180: Come to think of it, this resembles the Megasawa City case. Mifuyu Niimura tried to establish an alibi using the funeral and the Kogori couple.
C6 cha 180: I do feel it is hasty to think of them as mere suicides after all...
C7 cha 168: This seems to be a big loophole, a question that cannot be filled. Strange for a suicide, yet no one could have killed them. So it has to be called suicide.
C8 cha 112: If someone unknown to anyone were hiding and that person were the culprit, it might work...
C9 cha 106: Well, living deep in the Arata mountains all that time without anyone knowing may be a stretch in itself.

キャプション1: I want to exchange more views on the old people's suicides
A1 cha 158: Understood.
A2 cha 180: I said that "it is too perfect to call suicide."
A3 cha 168: Suicides happening every time at a moment when everyone has an alibi seems a little impossible to me.
A4 cha 166: As I thought, I cannot consider them suicides.
A5 cha 162: What do you think, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション3: Everyone in the settlement was in on it and killed them
B1 cha 170: I see, so that is how you see it, /VAR/-sama.
B2 cha 168: Certainly the settlement people, Erika Niimura first among them, must have suspected murder at some point too.
B3 cha 156: But that explained nothing, so by elimination they had no choice but to judge it suicide.
B4 cha 148: It is a passive judgment, but suicide does make sense too.
B5 cha 178: If so, what bothers me is the motive for suicide. Whether there was a clear reason, as with Sakura Niimura.
B6 cha 160: Well, that is literally a case of dead men telling no tales. The truth will be hard to learn.
C1 cha 152: Everyone in on it...! I see, then...!
C2 cha 172: No, wait a moment, please.
C3 cha 156: The suicides began around Shiyo 740, I believe. That means that by Shiyo 800, everyone would be killing everyone.
C4 cha 152: So everyone will eventually be killed by settlement people. Not only oneself, but one's family too.
C5 cha 180: An example would be something like ubasuteyama. Once you are old, you must die.
C6 cha 180: But even if the settlement had a custom requiring old people be killed, making a fuss of calling it suicide seems odd...
C7 cha 168: Even if, as you say, /VAR/-sama, the settlement is in on killing the old, perhaps it is not everyone but only some of them.
C8 cha 112: You see, Erika Niimura said so, didn't she? That there is no telling what goes on beneath the surface.
C9 cha 106: Hmm, a group murder by the settlement... Quite interesting.
D1 cha 120: Someone unknown is hiding... I see...
D2 cha 169: The Arata district is vast, so if someone were hiding there, they might be able to live without being noticed.
D3 cha 176: Besides, Arata has a custom called the mountain seclusion. A rite of passage in which a woman shuts herself in the mountains for a year to train.
D4 cha 159: If one has been through the mountain seclusion, one cannot rule out that someone gone from the settlement lurks in the mountains and kills the old.
D5 cha 128: Hmm, if so, at a time when everyone has an alibi, they lure or carry off the victim to a convenient place and kill them...
D6 cha 132: Hmm... Even if it is someone's doing, they are remarkably efficient...
D7 cha 146: Perhaps they are using that drug. Then they could snatch people away in an instant without being seen.
D8 cha 155: If so, what are they doing it for...
D9 cha 110: As you say, /VAR/-sama, the theory that a hidden someone did it deserves consideration.
E1 cha 101: A supernatural phenomenon...
E2 cha 142: I see, for an unknown phenomenon that conclusion is only natural.
E3 cha 168: Then not only the suicides but Sakura Niimura's death, and the murders across ten years, might also be supernatural...
E4 cha 156: If so, one might say it is beyond prevention. To end it, there would be nothing for it but for the settlement to be emptied of people―
E5 cha 134: Hm? Then does it happen because there are people in the Arata settlement? Without people, there could be no suicides or murders...
E6 cha 136: Say the settlement is fairly modern, and TV or cell signals interfere with something and send people signals urging suicide...
E7 cha 130: Ah, no, perhaps I am stretching it too far.
E8 cha 142: Even if it is supernatural, there must be a reason. If we could get to the bottom of it...

キャプション1: Why did Mifuyu Niimura go out of her way to confess about Megasawa City?
A1 cha 158: As was said, it seems she meant to speak honestly about the breach of the rules she had committed.
A2 cha 180: In particular, she asked Erika Niimura not to hold Sakura Niimura to account for it.
A3 cha 168: However, from that conversation, it seems there was no such confession in the routes where the Megasawa City case happened.
A4 cha 166: In other words, it is fair to say that Erika Niimura truly knew nothing of the involvement in the Megasawa City case.
キャプション2: If she hadn't confessed, Sakura Niimura wouldn't have died?
キャプション3: So Sakura Niimura's death was a coincidence?
B1 cha 170: Probably so. At the very least, she would never have run out of the settlement and tried to kill herself.
B2 cha 168: So I think there is no problem in telling you this...
B3 cha 156: In the routes where the Megasawa City case happened, that is, the Jusatsu Arc and the Meicho Arc, Sakura Niimura is alive.
B4 cha 148: Whether Sakura Niimura was involved in the later cases is unclear...
C1 cha 152: That is how it would be. She learned of Mifuyu Niimura's confession, could not bear the guilt, and ran out of the settlement.
C2 cha 172: Had Mifuyu Niimura not made that confession, Sakura Niimura would not have died.
C3 cha 156: But it is odd. Mifuyu Niimura said Sakura Niimura had turned down her request for support.
C4 cha 152: If Sakura Niimura truly was not involved, hearing the confession would give her no reason to kill herself...
C5 cha 180: Then does it mean Sakura Niimura was involved somewhere that was left untold?
C6 cha 180: Hmm... Something smells a little fishy...

キャプション1: Think further on the possibility that 'they really are suicides'
A1 cha 158: Hmm, if we dig deeper into the possibility of suicide...
A2 cha 180: That everyone kills themselves should be seen less as 'wanting to die' than as having no choice but to die.
A3 cha 168: But where the cause lies is known only to those who killed themselves, and even Erika Niimura, the oldest, seems not to know.
A4 cha 166: What do you think, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション2: I still think it's an endemic disease that makes people suicidal
キャプション3: They realize why they must die in the spring they turn 75
キャプション4: No more suicides will happen, so the reason will never be known
B1 cha 170: I see, so we return to the first hypothesis. An endemic disease that drives people to suicide...
B2 cha 168: There are even things like parasites that control the will of their host. If such a thing caused the endemic disease...
B3 cha 156: Would they kill themselves even after fleeing the settlement? Or would the parasites vanish once they escaped the settlement...
B4 cha 148: Nothing can be said for now, but to borrow Erina Goto's words, one can 'force a hypothesis to fit and correct it later if it is wrong.'
B5 cha 178: For now I think it is not a mistake to think along those lines.
C1 cha 152: Oh, they realize why they must kill themselves in the spring they turn 75...
C2 cha 172: If so, the age of 75 is the keyword. What on earth does 75 mean...
C3 cha 156: Simply put, it is "late-stage elderly," but physical aging varies by person, so aging is probably unrelated.
C4 cha 152: Then it is the number 75. I have no information on it so far...
C5 cha 180: Did we overlook something?
C6 cha 180: It is hard to get past guesswork.
D1 cha 120: I see. Indeed, it switched from suicide to murder. Shiyo 791 should have been the first clear murder.
D2 cha 169: If for some reason the factor driving suicide disappeared, then murder―
D3 cha 176: Hm? Then that means someone was egging on the suicides, right?
D4 cha 159: Then this is not suicide after all. Even if it was suicide, someone must have existed who controlled its cause.
D5 cha 128: If we could make contact with that someone, the reason for the suicides would become clear, but...
D6 cha 132: Does such a person really exist, and what was their method? It is extremely interesting.

キャプション1: Think further on the possibility of 'group murder by the settlement'
A1 cha 158: As I said earlier, if the whole settlement did it, there are two ways to think. Either everyone is in on it, or it is the work of some group.
A2 cha 180: If everyone is in on it, it is like ubasuteyama. Then making a fuss about suicide is itself nothing but a farce.
A3 cha 168: But if it is the work of some people, that changes things. That is plain murder.
A4 cha 166: If several people did it, they could split roles as lookout and kidnapper and build alibis.
A5 cha 162: But probably, nine times out of ten, Erika Niimura is innocent. If guilty, saying such things to the Motoki-cho group, outsiders, would be very dangerous.
A6 cha 159: Even so, there must be someone leading it. A leader who kills and makes it look like suicide.
A7 cha 142: Who do you think is leading it, /VAR/-sama?
B1 cha 170: Someone in the Niimura family, then...
B2 cha 168: The one who could be the ringleader would be Kotaro Niimura, I suppose.
B3 cha 156: Certainly there are all sorts of unsavory rumors about him. Even taking them as separate from the curse-killings since Shiyo 791.
B4 cha 148: But suicides were rampant even before he was born in Shiyo 758, so has he taken over and been killing the old people...
B5 cha 178: Hmm... In that case there must have been a clear reason to kill the old since before he was born. Information only part of the settlement could know.
B6 cha 160: If Erika Niimura is innocent, how would her son Kotaro Niimura have come to know it?
B7 cha 138: It looks to be a deep-rooted story.
C1 cha 152: People outside the Niimura family, I see...
C2 cha 172: Then, at the very least, the Niimura family would be isolated from the settlement.
C3 cha 156: Could the aim be to bring down the family that represents the settlement?
C4 cha 152: If so, the cause would be the very existence of the Niimura family.
C5 cha 180: The Niimura family's existence harms the other residents. If they ruin the leading family's credibility through suicides and murders, and seize authority over the settlement...
C6 cha 180: The possibility cannot be ruled out.
C7 cha 168: Then we must think about why the Niimura family is in the way. Whether there is some special factor...
C8 cha 112: The view gets murky from here, so it is best to continue the analysis with the references and the encyclopedia.
D1 cha 120: Someone from outside the settlement, you say. But that―
D2 cha 169: No, that possibility is entirely plausible.
D3 cha 176: The Arata district is state-owned land, and outsiders are basically not permitted to enter.
D4 cha 159: Besides, rare plants and animals thrive in the Arata district, so one could say it is special to the state as well.
D5 cha 128: So the state kills the residents in its way, perhaps to remove them and freely obtain the plants and animals.
D6 cha 132: Then the culprit's aim is to drive the people out of the settlement. And to make free use of the mountains of the Arata district.
D7 cha 146: It is the place where that drug originates, in particular. I very much doubt the state would just stand by and look away.
D8 cha 155: We have come to quite an interesting analysis. A crime by someone outside the settlement. It is by no means something to make light of.

キャプション1: Think further on the possibility that 'someone in hiding is the culprit'
A1 cha 158: If it is the work of someone in hiding, then, as I said earlier, they are most likely lurking in the mountains.
A2 cha 180: Considering the mountain seclusion, a rite of passage, staying hidden in the mountains is not impossible either.
A3 cha 168: In that case, what we should consider is why they kill while making it look like suicide, and why they lurk in the mountains.
A4 cha 166: What do you think, /VAR/-sama?
B1 cha 170: A yokai... I see...
B2 cha 168: Then it may no longer be a situation people can handle. The murders since Shiyo 791 are probably that yokai's doing too.
B3 cha 156: A yokai lives where nature remains, and kills because it wants to drive away the humans in its way.
B4 cha 148: Killing while making it look like suicide had no visible effect, so next it switched to blatant murders that stir up more fear: the curse-killings.
B5 cha 178: Yes, that was just an example of a reason, but it makes things somewhat clearer.
B6 cha 160: Then will the time come to face the yokai one day? Hee hee hee, I look forward to it already.
C1 cha 152: An undiscovered tribe...? That idea never occurred to me.
C2 cha 172: In a place as deep in the mountains as the Arata district, an undiscovered tribe living there is not out of the question.
C3 cha 156: Finding the Arata settlement in their way, they have kept killing people for decades.
C4 cha 152: If so, will the Arata residents, with their strong sense of self-defense, also take up arms and fight?
C5 cha 180: If that tribe knew of the Arata settlement residents and made it look like suicide because an open fight would bring many casualties...
C6 cha 180: Yes, that is possible too. Your point of view was quite refreshing, /VAR/-sama.
D1 cha 120: Animal attacks... You mean the work of bears or wild boars.
D2 cha 169: Hmm... But...
D3 cha 176: Then the falls to their deaths aside, the cases of slitting one's own throat with a blade cannot quite be explained...
D4 cha 159: I am sorry to reject your opinion, /VAR/-sama, but calling it the work of beasts seems a bit of a stretch.
D5 cha 128: Still, such an outlandish idea will surely be useful somewhere. Do not hold back; please consider all sorts of possibilities.

キャプション1: Think further on the possibility of 'a supernatural phenomenon'
A1 cha 158: If it is a supernatural phenomenon, the place called the Arata settlement itself must hold the conditions for it.
A2 cha 180: It is probably something unknown, but if that were the reason it was designated state-owned land...
A3 cha 168: The Arata settlement might be a geographically very dangerous place.
A4 cha 166: To begin with, it is a place that makes drugs like a doping drug. If the ingredients are there, it is clear it is no ordinary place.
A5 cha 162: What danger do you think the Arata settlement holds, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション2: Poison gas that drives murder and suicide is leaking out
キャプション3: There's something wrong with the food
キャプション4: The Niimura main house's goshinboku is suspicious
キャプション5: Strange signals are given off, and every case is an illusion
B1 cha 170: Hmm, poison gas that drives suicide and murder... And it appears every April.
B2 cha 168: Then there must be a vent somewhere. And that vent opened around Shiyo 730.
B3 cha 156: Then there is nothing left but to flee the settlement or plug the hole. It is not a problem deduction can solve.
B4 cha 148: At times like this, since it is state-owned land, I think the state ought to take proper safety measures...
B5 cha 178: Well, this is going a bit far, but the state may be using the people of Arata to keep studying the gas's effects.
B6 cha 160: Either way, the state must be hiding something. Otherwise there is no point in making it state-owned land.

キャプション2: Is there nothing fun in Toyotake Village?

C4 cha 152: When they truly must carry large loads or move many people, they use rental cars.

キャプション1: What do topics with a time limit, like 'topics in season,' mean?
A1 cha 158: Yes, I think this one needs an explanation.
A2 cha 180: A topic in season is, as the words say, a topic you can only choose at that time; once the time limit passes, it can no longer be selected.
A3 cha 168: The reason is that once the season has passed, what the topic would discuss has already come to light.
A4 cha 166: For example, when '173 Is a new case on the way!?' appeared, no case had happened yet in the Shigatsu Arc.
A5 cha 162: But once the scenarios advance to a certain point, the case comes to light, so that topic is no longer suited to the time.
A6 cha 159: In this way, 'topics in season' appear and vanish according to your progress, /VAR/-sama.
A7 cha 142: So, so as not to miss the season, please do come here from time to time.

キャプション1: Why did the Kogori couple stay in Motoki-cho?
A1 cha 158: As you saw, because Erina Goto was late, the chance of running into the Kogori couple grew large.

A4 cha 166: Well, they could have forced their way along, but that would have made Natsumi Kogori and the others uneasy.
A5 cha 162: In any case, the big difference in the third route of the Shigatsu Arc is that the Kogori couple stay in Motoki-cho.

キャプション1: Who did the Niimura sisters inherit their green eyes from?
A1 cha 158: Let me... see. Come to think of it, Kotaro Niimura's eyes are black and Sakura Niimura's blue.
A2 cha 180: Their eye color is said to be from birth, so it is certainly not acquired.
A3 cha 168: Which means... the cause of the green eyes is...
B1 cha 170: O-oh... I see, one can read it that way, too...
B2 cha 168: That Sakura Niimura was unfaithful, and those sisters were the children she conceived...
B3 cha 156: Hmm, but I wonder. The sisters are the only green-eyed people in that small settlement, and even if she lay with a man outside, to bear two...
B4 cha 148: Besides, if that were possible, Kotaro Niimura would have suspected it too.
B5 cha 178: Ah...
B6 cha 160: So could Kotaro Niimura have suspected infidelity and killed Sakura Niimura...?
B7 cha 138: It does not go beyond speculation, but infidelity is possible, and if so, many things are strange...
B8 cha 104: I am sorry, I cannot tell any more than this...

E4 cha 156: But theirs is from birth, and Chigaya Niimura, for one, looks healthy even past 20...
E5 cha 134: Well, even if it is an illness, it is probably not glaucoma.

キャプション1: Were Kotaro Niimura, his brother and Sakura Niimura a love triangle?
A1 cha 158: From what we heard, Eiichiro Niimura and Sakura Niimura do not seem to have had that kind of relationship.
