A2 cha 180: Usually she seems to recognize it as Eiichiro Niimura's voice... Is there some condition, perhaps?
キャプション3: Hasn't she perceived it by sight before?
B1 cha 170: Hmm, in fact I too have thought something was odd about danger sense.
B2 cha 168: To begin with, is the very ability to sense danger like that not strange in itself?
B3 cha 156: For an ordinary high school girl to have something so like a psychic power...
C1 cha 152: Before now? Um... was that so...
C2 cha 172: Ah, come to think of it...!
C3 cha 156: I remember now! The first time Natsumi Kogori used her danger sense in the Jusatsu Arc!
C4 cha 152: If I recall, when they left Zahha and Erina Goto said she was going to cram school, Natsumi Kogori saw an image of a Noh mask.
C5 cha 180: I see, now I am sure as well. Natsumi Kogori's danger sense is, at the very least, not a power to hear Eiichiro Niimura's voice.
C6 cha 180: If you ask me what it is, then, that is where I am stuck, but...
C7 cha 168: It may be best not to rely too much on danger sense. Something seems to be behind it.

キャプション1: Do Arata residents use the convenience store a lot?
A1 cha 158: They do not seem to use it very often.
A2 cha 180: Normally they buy what they need at a supermarket during the day, so they rarely go all that way at night.
A3 cha 168: If they go to the supermarket, there is no need to shop at a convenience store either. A convenience store that is not nearby is quite inconvenient.
キャプション2: Who uses the convenience store in Arata?
キャプション3: No way, life without a convenience store must be a pain!
B1 cha 170: The main customers are people living nearby and, with elementary and middle schools close by, their students. The clientele is not that unusual.
B2 cha 168: That said, young people hardly ever hang around late at night, so at night there is almost no one there.
B3 cha 156: Ah, by the way, the one that appeared was not an 'Arata convenience store' but the Toyotake one. It is right by Toyotake Station.
C1 cha 152: Oh my, do you like convenience stores, /VAR/-sama? Having one nearby is handy, since you can buy all sorts of things easily.
C2 cha 172: I rather like convenience stores too. Not so much the shopping as the atmosphere, I would say.
C3 cha 156: Spacing out on the bench in front, looking for store-exclusive items... even a small shop is fun in all sorts of ways.

キャプション1: Can you tell how close sisters are by their boob size?
A1 cha 158: /大文字//揺れ/Wha!?
A2 cha 180: Ah... come to think of it, Kana Niimura said something like that. That sisters who don't know each other's chest size don't get along...
A3 cha 168: /大文字/I mean, how would I know that! It depends on the person!
キャプション2: Didn't /立木/ say she has a little sister?
B1 cha 170: Huh? Ah, yes, I did answer that way before, but...
B2 cha 168: Wait, you're not about to ask about my sister's chest size, are you!?
B3 cha 156: Th-that's indecent! Me is one thing, but my sister too...!
B5 cha 178: Hee hee, I know, you're enjoying my reactions like this, aren't you?
B6 cha 160: I've mostly figured out your patterns by now, /VAR/-sama. Things won't go your way so easily, you know?
B7 cha 138: Right! This meeting is adjourned! /VAR/-sama, keep the dirty talk in moderation!
C1 cha 152: /大文字/Argh!
C2 cha 172: So it was just sexual harassment after all!
C3 cha 156: /大文字/Argh!
C4 cha 152: You did it before too, didn't you!? Asking my chest size, trying to harass me using my eyesight as an excuse!
C6 cha 180: Somehow, I think I'm getting used to it. I was bad with dirty jokes, but trading words with you, /VAR/-sama, I sort of... how should I handle it...
C7 cha 168: Fine, I'll just come out and say it! I'm pretty well-endowed! You'd be amazed if I took my clothes off!?
C8 cha 112: There! You're satisfied now, right!? The end!

キャプション1: So it's pretty voluminous...
キャプション2: You're going to ignore me in silence?
B1 cha 170: Ugh...
B2 cha 168: When you call me out so seriously... I'm a little weak to that...
B3 cha 156: Anyway, can't we drop that topic already! I answered your long-standing question properly!
B4 cha 148: /小/I really did try pretty hard, you know...?
C4 cha 152: Ah, I can't take it! I can't stand an atmosphere like this!
C5 cha 180: Being answered with silence is pretty painful, isn't it... Excuse me.
C6 cha 180: /小/Huh? Is this my fault...?
C7 cha 168: /小/Oh well...
D1 cha 120: W-wait a moment... If you make that face...
D2 cha 169: U-um, I just wanted to put up a little resistance. Please don't be so down... I wasn't really angry...
D3 cha 176: Uuu... what do I do... (flustered)
D4 cha 159: /VAR/-sama, it's all right now. Look, see my face? I'm not angry, right?
D6 cha 132: That's where you're supposed to call me out!? Like, 'I can't see your face behind a Noh mask!?'...!
D7 cha 146: Ah, what do I do! I depressed you, and my joke fell flat. This is the worst...!
D8 cha 155: Uuu... /VAR/-sama, please don't abandon me... I'll end up all alone...
D9 cha 110: /小/Phew... Time to get my fighting spirit back up...

キャプション1: What was the pot Natsumi Kogori saw?
A1 cha 158: As Kengo Shirozaki said, it is one of the ritual implements used at memorial services.
A2 cha 180: Giant bullfrog oil is put inside and heated until it catches fire. The mourners then drip the prepared liquid into it, the way one offers incense.
B1 cha 170: Yes, a liquid named 'falsificaso,' if I remember. It is said to be made in the settlement.
B2 cha 168: It will appear in a scenario before long, so please check it then.
C1 cha 152: Yes, that is its only use. So, pot though it is, it is nothing special, just an ordinary one, I think.
C2 cha 172: Strictly speaking, 'crock' is the correct word. Generally, a vessel with a small mouth is called a pot, and one with a wide mouth a crock.

キャプション1: Can Natsumi Kogori see the past too?
A1 cha 158: What she saw at the convenience store in Arata was a very rare case, I think. Before or since, that was the only time she saw the past.
A2 cha 180: Why she saw such a thing, I cannot say, but at the very least it was information she needed to know.
キャプション2: The truth about danger sense is getting really suspicious
B1 cha 170: Indeed, it is probably not simply an ability to foresee danger.
B2 cha 168: Though if you ask what it really is, even guessing is hard...
B3 cha 156: It seems better to doubt the very idea of danger sense.
B4 cha 148: For example, there are points worth rethinking: when she sensed danger in the past, did it really lead to avoiding danger?
B5 cha 178: Especially in the Jusatsu Arc. She sensed danger several times, but how did those turn out...
B6 cha 160: There were often times when going against the danger sense seems like it would have been better...
C1 cha 152: Certainly, it could simply be that Natsumi Kogori has an illness of the brain, and so sees and hears things that are not there...
C2 cha 172: Or I have heard that some mental illnesses come with such hallucinations as well.
C3 cha 156: But even so...
C4 cha 152: It is true that Natsumi Kogori let them avoid danger many times. Whether one may call that an illness...
C5 cha 180: At the very least I think Natsumi Kogori is different from ordinary people, but we cannot simply decide it is an illness.

キャプション1: /立木/'s looks and personality are totally different, huh
A1 cha 158: Huh? What is this all of a sudden...
A2 cha 180: Well, of course, dressed like this, the first impression must be eerie, but...
A3 cha 168: Um... what is your impression now?
B1 cha 170: C-cute? Oh, stop...!
B2 cha 168: No one has ever said that to me before...
B3 cha 156: I-it must be that! This outfit is just stirring your imagination, /VAR/-sama, and, um...
B4 cha 148: If you saw what I really look like, you might be disappointed...
B5 cha 178: Somehow, the purpose of this outfit is changing. At first it was to hide my true self, but now it is to keep your impression of me from souring, /VAR/-sama...
B6 cha 160: /大文字/Ah!
B7 cha 138: You must be teasing me!? I will not fall for that, you know!?
B8 cha 104: Honestly, /VAR/-sama! Please stop toying with me!
B9 cha 120: /小/But... even as flattery, I am a little happy...
C1 cha 152: Playful...?
C2 cha 172: Is that so? I thought I was behaving quite normally...
C3 cha 156: But if I am playful, does that mean I have given you at least some fun, /VAR/-sama?
C4 cha 152: Then I could wish for nothing more. I shall go on behaving 'normally,' and I hope your time here will be worthwhile, /VAR/-sama.
D1 cha 120: Oh, cheerful, you say.
D2 cha 169: Well, yes, I do not think my true personality is a gloomy one either. I am not good with gloomy airs or quiet atmospheres...
D3 cha 176: Analyzing myself a little more, I think I am the type whose emotions show clearly. I do not hide my feelings much.
D4 cha 159: As you have surely noticed by now, /VAR/-sama, I have an impulsive side...
D5 cha 128: Some people may find me hard to get along with. There must be those who dislike that kind of woman.
E1 cha 101: I-intelligent!?
E2 cha 142: That is quite an unexpected answer... I never imagined you saw me that way.
E3 cha 168: It is probably this: I tell you so much about this world that it just makes me look that way.
E4 cha 156: As for general common sense in the normal world... honestly, I am not that confident.
E5 cha 134: Also, I try to conduct myself as neutrally as I can, so perhaps that helps too.
E6 cha 136: But being called intelligent makes me genuinely happy. It feels just like a guide should.

キャプション1: Then let's give /立木/ a general knowledge test!
A1 cha 158: Ehh... are you serious...
A2 cha 180: I'm really not confident at that sort of thing... You'll find out how dumb I am...
A3 cha 168: N-no! That doesn't mean I should chicken out!
A4 cha 166: All right! Bring it on!
キャプション3: What's the second-highest mountain in Japan?
キャプション4: Which great figure first made a map of Japan by actual survey?
キャプション5: What in the solar system is classed as a 'dwarf planet'?
B1 cha 170: The Edo shogunate...? I am sorry, but my world differs from yours, /VAR/-sama, so there is no such thing as an Edo shogunate.
B2 cha 168: But I believe Tokyo has a place called Edogawa, so might you mean the Tokyo shogunate, founded over 400 years ago?
B3 cha 156: In that case, in this world it was founded by a man named Yasuie Togawa.
B4 cha 148: ※Explanation※\nFounded by Tokugawa Ieyasu, made shogun in 1603. The Edo period lasted until power was returned to the emperor in 1867.
B5 cha 178: In this world, the similar Tokyo shogunate was founded in Shiyo 345 by Yasuie Togawa.
C1 cha 152: The second!? You certainly aim for a tricky spot...
C2 cha 172: Hee hee, actually, I know this one. I am good at this sort of thing.
C3 cha 156: The second-highest mountain is Kitadake in Yamanashi Prefecture. At 3,193 m, it is the highest non-volcanic mountain in Japan.
C4 cha 152: Incidentally, the third-highest are two mountains, Okuhotakadake and Ainodake, at 3,190 m.
C5 cha 180: My common sense is not bad at all, right? Is it not the same in your world too, /VAR/-sama?
D1 cha 120: The person who first made a map of Japan is...
D2 cha 169: Ino...
D3 cha 176: Um, what was it...
D4 cha 159: Ino...
D5 cha 128: Tatataka!
D6 cha 132: Huh? That's not it... Dadadaka? Tatadaka?
D7 cha 146: W-well, it should be about right!
D8 cha 155: ※Explanation※\nIno Tadataka made the Dai Nihon Enkai Yochi Zenzu (strictly, his disciples and Takahashi Kageyasu finished it after his death).
D9 cha 110: In Mika Tachiki's world too, Ino Tadataka seems to have existed with the same achievements.
E2 cha 142: A dwarf planet...?
E3 cha 168: What is that? Not a planet?
E4 cha 156: Oh, /VAR/-sama, really, trying to toy with me using a made-up word like that. Ho ho ho.
E5 cha 134: /小/Ho ho...
E6 cha 136: ※Explanation 1※\nA class of solar system bodies defined in 2006: in short, bodies too small to call planets. Pluto is the best known.
E7 cha 130: ※Explanation 2※\nAs of 2018, besides Pluto, Eris, Ceres, Makemake and Haumea are designated dwarf planets.
E8 cha 142: It is almost the same in Mika Tachiki's world.

キャプション1: You're good at geography?
A1 cha 158: Yes, of my studies, geography and classics are my strong points.
A2 cha 180: In exchange, I am hopeless at science and math. Sometimes I even get my multiplication tables wrong...
キャプション2: Then let's test /立木/ on her strong subjects!
キャプション3: Then let's test /立木/ on her weak subjects!
B1 cha 170: Oh, so that is your move. Very well. Let us try it in the next topic.
C1 cha 152: Ugh, seriously... A test, at this point...
C2 cha 172: W-well, fine. If you say so, /VAR/-sama, I will take the challenge in the next topic!

キャプション1: Mika Tachiki takes on geography!
A1 cha 158: All right, bring on anything! ...If you please.
キャプション2: What's the largest desert in the world?
キャプション3: Which mountain has the highest climber death rate in the world?
キャプション4: Which island is the farthest from any other land in the world?
キャプション5: What's the lowest land in the world?
B1 cha 170: Oh, quite a good question.
B2 cha 168: Generally, the Sahara in northern Africa is the largest. Its area is about 10 million square km, nearly the same as the United States.
B3 cha 156: But by some definitions Antarctica is the largest desert: about 14 million square km, a dry region with little precipitation.
B4 cha 148: Hee hee hee, you surely did not imagine there would be two answers, did you?
C1 cha 152: This one is easy.
C2 cha 172: Annapurna, in the Himalayas. The tenth-highest mountain in the world.
C3 cha 156: Its climber death rate is about 38%. It may be even harsher than surviving in this world.
C4 cha 152: Incidentally, the mountain with the most deaths is Tanigawadake in Japan, with over 830. That is said to be more than all the 8,000 m peaks combined.
C5 cha 180: Hee hee hee, I would like a slightly more challenging question.
D1 cha 120: A famous one: Bouvet, an uninhabited Norwegian island in the South Atlantic, over 2,000 km from Africa's southern tip.
D2 cha 169: The nearest other land is Antarctica, about 1,600 km away. No other place this far from other land has been found so far.
D3 cha 176: Bouvet Island is surrounded by high cliffs, so even landing is said to be difficult. The weather is also very bad, and being near Antarctica, it has many blizzard days.
D4 cha 159: Not only its location but its terrain and weather too make it a true lonely island in a remote sea, a land at the edge of the world.
E1 cha 101: The lowest land in the world means a hollowed-out landform where water easily flows in.
E2 cha 142: In other words, a place that has become a lake, with nowhere else for the water to flow out.
E3 cha 168: This means the substances dissolved in the water cannot flow out, so the dissolved components grow more and more concentrated.
E4 cha 156: And the typical substance that dissolves in water is salt. The lake with the highest salinity is the lowest place.
E5 cha 134: The answer is the Dead Sea, a lake on the Arabian Peninsula shared by Israel and Jordan. Its elevation is -418 m.
E6 cha 136: Because of its high salinity, things float easily in the Dead Sea. Have you seen photos of people floating while reading a newspaper?
E7 cha 130: The Dead Sea: a sinister name, but recent resort development has made it bustling. I would love to go once.

キャプション1: Mika Tachiki takes on the classics!
A1 cha 158: Hee hee hee, I am rather confident, you know?
キャプション2: How does 'The bell of Gion Shoja' continue?
キャプション3: What's the only verb with the ka-row irregular conjugation?
キャプション4: What's the oldest history book in the world?
キャプション5: Which text gave rise to the phrase 'throw away shame'?
B1 cha 170: It may differ from your world, /VAR/-sama, but it is the opening of the Tale of Tara. I have it all memorized.
B2 cha 168: The bell of Gion Shoja echoes the impermanence of all things.
B3 cha 156: The color of the sala flowers reveals the truth that the mighty must fall.
B4 cha 148: It is also what Hoichi the Earless recites in the famous ghost story. Old literature is truly 'ito okashi'―most delightful.
B5 cha 178: ※Explanation※\nIn Mika Tachiki's world it is the Tale of Tara, but in the real world it corresponds to the Tale of the Heike.
C1 cha 152: That would be 'kuru,' to come.
C2 cha 172: An old Japanese verb with the special conjugation 'kozu,' 'kita,' 'kuru,' 'kururu,' 'kureba,' 'koi.'
C3 cha 156: Well, something like this is, for me, 'ito yasuki koto'―a most easy matter.
D1 cha 120: That would be the Kojiki.
D2 cha 169: Together with the Nihon Shoki, it is said to have laid the foundation of Japanese mythology, and if you want to learn Japanese history, it is a good place to start.
D3 cha 176: ※Explanation※\nIn Mika Tachiki's world too, the Kojiki seems to have been compiled just as in the real world.
E1 cha 101: Ah, that is the Tale of the Bamboo Cutter.
E2 cha 142: Five noble princes step forward to marry Princess Kaguya, and as a condition each is told to bring a treasure that does not exist.
E3 cha 168: One of them, Prince Ishitsukuri, is told to bring 'the Buddha's stone begging bowl,' and brings an ordinary bowl instead.
E4 cha 156: Even after the lie came out, he threw away the bowl and kept courting her, so 'throwing away the hachi (bowl)' became 'throwing away haji (shame).'
E5 cha 134: Truly, 'ito utateshi,' is it not?
E7 cha 130: ※Explanation※\nIn Mika Tachiki's world too, the Tale of the Bamboo Cutter seems to have been written just as in the real world.

キャプション1: Mika Tachiki takes on math!
A1 cha 158: Uuu... please go easy on me...
キャプション2: If x squared is 4, what is x?
キャプション3: You buy something for 80 yen with 200 yen cash. How much change do you get?
キャプション4: What do all the integers from 1 to 1000 add up to?
B1 cha 170: /VAR/-sama, surely I know at least that much.
B2 cha 168: A number that makes 4 when multiplied by itself, right?
B3 cha 156: The answer is 2! 2×2=4! That is common sense!
B4 cha 148: ※Explanation※\nThe correct answer is 2 or -2, since -2×-2 is also 4. Note that Mika Tachiki's answer would only get half the points.
C1 cha 152: Honestly... that is elementary school level, is it not...
C2 cha 172: 200-80 is 120. The change is 120 yen.
C3 cha 156: ※Explanation 1※\nIf you had two 100-yen coins, you would only use one, so the change is 20 yen.
C4 cha 152: ※Explanation 2※\nEven with 10-yen coins mixed in, the change never exceeds 20 yen. So the change is either 0 or 20 yen.
D1 cha 120: Um, all the numbers from 1 to 1000 added together, yes? One moment, please...
D3 cha 176: /暗転/2 hours later...
D5 cha 128: /暗転/3 hours later...
D8 cha 155: I did it! The answer is 500500! It took some time, but well, even an elementary schooler could manage it!
D9 cha 110: ※Explanation※\nThe answer is (1+1000)×500=500500. The sum of all integers from A to B is (A+B)×count÷2.
E1 cha 101: Pardon?
E2 cha 142: What was that? What did you say?
E3 cha 168: There was a whole string of unknown words in there...
E4 cha 156: No one can do something like that in their head in an instant. I am sure even Erina Goto could not. Ho ho ho.
E5 cha 134: ※Explanation※\ntan17°×π×(a-b) looks complicated, but a=b, so a-b=0. Thus tan17°×π×0. Anything times 0 is 0, so the answer is 0.

キャプション1: Mika Tachiki takes on science!
A1 cha 158: S-science! It is probably better than math, I think...
キャプション2: Why does water boil at exactly 100°C (its boiling point)?
キャプション3: What is it called when an insect goes egg→larva→pupa→adult?
キャプション5: What are the seeds that ferns and mushrooms release called?
B2 cha 168: Now that you mention it... Water freezes at exactly 0°C and boils at exactly 100°C...
B3 cha 156: Amazing! How amazing! Water is incredible!
B4 cha 148: Water is the basis of everything, so it surely reads the room and changes at nice round numbers.
B5 cha 178: Yes, water is incredible!
B6 cha 160: ※Explanation※\nThe temperature at which water boils under 1 atmosphere was defined as 100°C (strictly, 99.974°C).
C1 cha 152: Ah! I know that one! I know it!
C2 cha 172: Meta... metamorphosis! It is metamorphosis!
C3 cha 156: Complete metamorphosis!
C4 cha 152: How is that? I got it, did I not? Complete metamorphosis!
C5 cha 180: ※Explanation※\nInsects that go egg→larva→pupa→adult undergo complete metamorphosis. Those that go larva→adult with no pupa undergo incomplete metamorphosis.
D1 cha 120: The lightest of the elements?
D2 cha 169: Hee hee, I know this one.
D3 cha 176: The lightest is hot air! Air rises when it gets hot, after all! Hot air is the lightest!
D4 cha 159: ※Explanation※\nThe lightest element is hydrogen, made of one proton and one electron.
E1 cha 101: Um... I have heard of it... What was it again...
E2 cha 142: Sp...
E3 cha 168: Spe...
E4 cha 156: Sp...
E5 cha 134: /大文字/Sperm!
E6 cha 136: I am fairly sure it was a name like sperm...
E7 cha 130: ※Explanation※\nFerns and fungi such as mushrooms reproduce by spores.

キャプション1: Why are you only good at humanities?
A1 cha 158: Hmm... that is a hard one to answer...
A2 cha 180: Perhaps just because I do not feel bad at them. I do not clearly know the reason myself.
A3 cha 168: Ah, but even among humanities subjects, I am a little weak at English... I can barely get the average score.
キャプション2: Shall we do an English test?
キャプション3: You can't get interested in English?
B1 cha 170: Ah, no, please spare me that... If any more of my foolishness is exposed, I will lose all dignity as a guide...
B2 cha 168: Things I cannot get interested in, I am truly bad at... I do the homework and such, but none of it sinks in.
C1 cha 152: Exactly... One can live perfectly well with Japanese alone, so it is hard to find the will to go and study English...
C2 cha 172: Besides, nowadays you can translate easily online, so I see even less point in studying it.
C3 cha 156: Well, that is the hard part of being a student. You have to learn things even when they do not interest you.

キャプション1: What's beyond the iron bars underground?
A1 cha 158: You mean Kana Niimura's secret base.
A2 cha 180: I hear that place has been sealed off for decades. No one alive now, myself included, would know.
キャプション2: Is there a key to the door?
キャプション3: Did they really put iron bars there because of a cave-in?
B1 cha 170: Yes, the Niimura family seems to keep it. So anyone who wanted to go in could.
B2 cha 168: However, that is strictly forbidden by the rules. No one may enter without Erika Niimura's permission.
C1 cha 152: Ah... now that you mention it...
C2 cha 172: Indeed, for a cave-in, a sign saying 'Do not enter' would seem enough. Only people from the settlement go in there, after all.
C3 cha 156: Going to the trouble of iron bars does seem a little too strict.
C4 cha 152: Are they going that far to keep anyone from ever entering, or is it that from the other side―
C5 cha 180: No, it is nothing.

キャプション1: There's a lot even the residents don't know, huh
A1 cha 158: Indeed. The underground passage, Sakura Niimura's danger sense, and so on: much is still unexplained.
A2 cha 180: If what lies behind them were known, it would be possible to find out the truth of the curse-killings.
A3 cha 168: To begin with, these things are forbidden or kept secret by the settlement's rules, which is why many facts are unknown, I think.
A4 cha 166: Which means whoever made the rules long ago would know what lies behind them.
キャプション3: Haven't the residents looked into it?
B1 cha 170: Probably so. Otherwise there would be no need to forbid it by rule.
B2 cha 168: You, /VAR/-sama, can probably learn fragments of it from the Letters References.
B3 cha 156: Please do check them, and try guessing for yourself what happened long ago, /VAR/-sama.
C1 cha 152: That is how it stands now, but I do not think no one has done anything at all.
C2 cha 172: If the settlement has rules, there must be some record of how those rules came about. I cannot imagine no one ever looked into it.
C3 cha 156: However, there were Westerners here long ago, so there must be books written in foreign languages too.
C4 cha 152: Perhaps anyone who tried to look into it was blocked by the language barrier.

キャプション1: So the curse-killings are man-made after all?
A1 cha 158: According to Erina Goto's reasoning, that is how it is.
A2 cha 180: She says there are several culprits, but they do not know what the others are doing, so no one knows the truth.
A3 cha 168: She also said that it works on its own because their emotional interests coincide.
A4 cha 166: If the motives are emotional, I think inferring them is very difficult. First one must know why the culprits came to hold those feelings.

キャプション1: Wouldn't it be better if everyone just left the settlement?
A1 cha 158: As you say, I too think that would be the quickest solution of all.
A2 cha 180: But as you know, the residents cannot abandon the land of Arata handed down from their ancestors. They have sworn to live here as long as they live.
A3 cha 168: And Erika Niimura did not order this, either. They stay of their own accord.
キャプション2: So does the culprit want to empty the settlement?
キャプション3: I don't get why they're so attached to the land
B1 cha 170: Hmm, that is possible too. If it came true, even past cases could be buried. For the culprit, nothing could be more desirable.
B2 cha 168: If the culprit keeps the residents barely alive and sustains the curse-killings with the fewest victims, they may be a pacifist, surprisingly.
B3 cha 156: Of course, committing murder and being a pacifist is a contradiction, but even so one can see an intent to keep the harm as small as possible.
B4 cha 148: Well, this may just be my own assumption.
C1 cha 152: Normally, if you knew you might be killed next year, you would move away.
C2 cha 172: But throughout history, many people all over the world have kept fighting at the risk of their lives to protect their land and homes.
C3 cha 156: Abandoning the land would mean abandoning their pride and identity too. It seems much like having a foreign country pick a war with you.
C4 cha 152: Either way, there must be a stubborn pride only those rooted in the land understand. I do not know if it is bushido, but it feels a bit like it to me.

キャプション1: Isn't the cherry tree suspicious after all?
A1 cha 158: Hmm, so the raw material of Droga is cherry roots...
A2 cha 180: Indeed, given everything so far, the story that a state-backed group took the cherry trees away 'roots and all' does make sense.
A3 cha 168: But how that leads to the curse-killings, I cannot quite see...
A4 cha 166: Do you have some idea, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション3: The cherry trees move like animals
キャプション4: The cherry pollen drives people mad
B1 cha 170: Droga, you say...
B2 cha 168: Given what we have seen, being splashed with the blood of someone who used Droga gives a person precognition or April sickness.
B4 cha 148: How does that lead to murder, then? Is there some cause and effect we cannot see?
B5 cha 178: At this stage it is hard to infer, but Droga's existence certainly cannot be ignored either.
C1 cha 152: The cherry trees move...? You mean the Arata settlement's cherry tree is an animal disguised as a cherry tree?
C2 cha 172: Then none of the residents would be the culprit, and no person could be named a murderer at all.
C3 cha 156: I see, an interesting idea.
C4 cha 152: Even so, in the curse-killings it is certain the residents are deliberately involved in some way.
C5 cha 180: Perhaps, if the cherry tree were an animal, it might have high intelligence...?
C6 cha 180: If so, it might even be able to deceive the residents into killing one another.
D1 cha 120: Oh, another new viewpoint.
D2 cha 169: Cherry trees seem to have pollen too, and if it is scattered all over the settlement, the residents are surely breathing it in.

D4 cha 159: If that somehow came true, it could make residents hallucinate and kill one another, or mistake who the culprit is.
D5 cha 128: Hm? Then danger sense would be...
D7 cha 146: No, it is nothing. I think I was overthinking it a little.
E1 cha 101: I see, that is only natural.
E2 cha 142: Still, we should keep an eye on anything that seems key. Even if it is unclear now, noticing it or not should make a difference.

キャプション1: I want to hear about pollen and danger sense properly
A1 cha 158: Huh? But...
A3 cha 168: Understood. It is only a wild guess, but please hear it as a reference.
A4 cha 166: Danger sense works only in the season when the cherry trees bloom.
A5 cha 162: Thinking a little more finely, one could say danger sense can be used while cherry pollen is in the air, could one not?
A6 cha 159: What if that pollen were sending some kind of signal only to those splashed with the blood of a Droga user...
A7 cha 142: That is what I vaguely thought.
A8 cha 133: I have no particular grounds; I just thought the story might still connect that way...
キャプション2: So precognition has a scientific basis?
キャプション3: So precognition is hallucinations from pollen?
B1 cha 170: Roughly speaking, yes. Somehow I cannot think of it as a psychic power or a supernatural phenomenon...
B2 cha 168: But even if so, someone like me could hardly understand the mechanism...
B3 cha 156: Writing it off as a psychic power is easy, but then I feel we would be overlooking... something important...
B4 cha 148: Honestly, that is about all I can say.
C1 cha 152: Well, that is what I thought, but...
C2 cha 172: But she really can foresee danger. There is no doubt it is not mere hallucination.
C3 cha 156: Then what is it? If you ask that, I cannot answer at all...
C4 cha 152: But it is a strange hypothesis after all, is it not? Being able to sense danger through cherry pollen.
D1 cha 120: Yes, I know myself that I am saying something strange.
D2 cha 169: But to accept danger sense simply as danger sense is starting to feel a little dangerous too.
D3 cha 176: I think some kind of causality must exist there.
D4 cha 159: After all, she can sense danger because of some cause. To foresee danger with no source at all...

キャプション1: About the size of Erina Goto's robes and Noh mask
A1 cha 158: Oh, so you are poking at that...
A2 cha 180: Because of her build, the Noh mask and red robes prepared for Erina Goto seem to have been too big. It made for quite a comical sight.
A3 cha 168: There are robes for children too, but in Shiyo 800 there was only Kana Niimura's, so Erina Goto had no choice but to wear an adult's.
A4 cha 166: Really, like that, there is no point hiding one's appearance with a Noh mask and robes.
A5 cha 162: If I were Erina Goto, even dressed like that, I am sure you would see through who I was, /VAR/-sama.

キャプション1: Are the Noh masks and robes lent to the mourners?
A1 cha 158: Yes, exactly. Everyone is required to wear them to attend the memorial service.
A2 cha 180: But please do not misunderstand: even the residents do not personally own Noh masks and red robes.
A3 cha 168: Except for the Grand Witch, Noh masks, red robes and footwear are lent to all residents as needed.
A4 cha 166: Do you understand why it works that way?
B1 cha 170: Hee hee, just as I would expect of you, /VAR/-sama. Considering why they wear Noh masks and red robes, you can mostly guess it.
C1 cha 152: Then let me explain.

C3 cha 156: For example, a tidy resident's would always be clean, but a messy resident's Noh mask would get dirty and the robes would be all wrinkles.
C4 cha 152: Then a person could largely be identified from the Noh mask and robes alone.
C5 cha 180: To prevent that, they are collected after the memorial service and stored in one place. When used again, they are handed out to everyone at random.
C6 cha 180: Adult and child sizes are taken into account, but basically everyone wears the same things in turn.

キャプション1: The settlement's memorial service is full of strange things, huh
A1 cha 158: Indeed, to ordinary people it must have seemed a very unusual ceremony.
A2 cha 180: 'Is this really a ceremony to mourn the dead?' Outside mourners all seem to think so.
キャプション2: Why did it take that form?
キャプション3: What was the drug they used?
B1 cha 170: I have heard that this too originally stems from the rules. For various reasons, the memorial service came to take that form.
B2 cha 168: Rather than mourning the dead, it is like a ceremony to drive the dead away so they do not come back here. As you saw.
B3 cha 156: Then perhaps in the past there was an event of 'driving away the dead,' or something that brought it to mind.
B4 cha 148: Because a calamity was caused by the dead, they drive them away so they do not come here―
B5 cha 178: No, perhaps I am overthinking it.
B6 cha 160: In any case, all I know is that a certain rule made the memorial service take that form.
C1 cha 152: That is falsificaso. Dripped into heated giant bullfrog oil, it sends up flames. Something like offering incense.
C2 cha 172: It is made for funerals within the settlement, so it is nothing very unusual there.
C3 cha 156: However, according to Erina Goto, falsificaso means 'fake' in Portuguese.
C4 cha 152: If so, there must be a 'real one' somewhere. She thought that might be Droga.
C5 cha 180: Then does that mean that at funerals they raised their physical abilities with Droga to fight something...
C6 cha 180: Hmm, if so, what on earth were they trying to fight... Having come this far, it is quite difficult.
C7 cha 168: In any case, that drug seems to be in ordinary use at funerals. But breathing it in fresh from vaporizing apparently makes you ill, so take care there.

キャプション1: Did every resident attend the thirteenth-year memorial service?
A1 cha 158: They should have. Even if faces and figures cannot be told apart, the witches counted the number of attendees.
A2 cha 180: However, they cannot confirm whether the person inside is truly a resident. Any act of identifying an individual is forbidden.
A3 cha 168: By using that outfit, one could secretly skip the memorial service with a stand-in, but...
A4 cha 166: Even so, I do not see much benefit in skipping it. If found out, one surely could not live in the settlement anymore...
A5 cha 162: Or, if someone were plotting something bad, swapping who is inside would be possible, but...

キャプション1: What are the residents after?
A1 cha 158: At the very least, there is no doubt it is to capture Natsumi Kogori.
A2 cha 180: However, what they mean to do with her once she is caught is hard to judge.
A3 cha 168: In the first route of the Shigatsu Arc she was killed, but in the second they did not kill her at once; it even seems their aim was to take her alive.
A4 cha 166: What on earth was different between these two routes...
キャプション4: Whether she's attacked inside the settlement
B1 cha 170: Kotaro Niimura...?
B2 cha 168: Ah, come to think of it, in the first route he reasoned things out with Natsumi Kogori and the others, and in the second he attacked with the residents.
B3 cha 156: Now that I think of it, his actions are rather ambiguous. They lack consistency.
B4 cha 148: Then something must have happened to him. Something that happened in the first route and not in the second.
B5 cha 178: What on earth could it be...
B6 cha 160: Shall we dig into it in the next topic?
C1 cha 152: Kana Niimura turning hostile...?
C2 cha 172: I see. In the first route, Kana Niimura and Chigaya Niimura were gravely hurt and died, and I said before that the cause was a grand sibling quarrel.
C3 cha 156: Chigaya Niimura took Mifuyu Niimura's place at the succession rite to keep watch on Kana Niimura, who would turn to violence.
C4 cha 152: In that sense, Kana Niimura's actions do change from route to route.
C5 cha 180: If so, it is conceivable that this changes how Natsumi Kogori is treated, but...
C6 cha 180: In that case, should we think it stems from Kotaro Niimura's actions after all?
C7 cha 168: After all, Kana Niimura likely turned to violence on Kotaro Niimura's orders.
D1 cha 120: I see. In the first route she was attacked at the Niimura home, in the second at Arata Station, outside the settlement.
D2 cha 169: Hmm, but...
D3 cha 176: I believe the plan was to attack before Natsumi Kogori left the settlement.
D4 cha 159: After all, she fled the settlement because something about Kotaro Niimura's movements was suspicious.
D5 cha 128: Hmm, and yet...
D6 cha 132: No, I cannot say that for certain. Perhaps some condition differs inside and outside the settlement...
D7 cha 146: I cannot think of anything beyond that. But we should not ignore that line either.
E1 cha 101: So it is difficult even for you, /VAR/-sama...
E2 cha 142: Indeed. There are far too many uncertain factors to reach a conclusion we can call 'this is it.'
E3 cha 168: Put another way, one could say it is not something that can be solved yet. Not until that appears―
E4 cha 156: No, all you need do, /VAR/-sama, is see their happy ending through. So whether it is solved is not so important.
E5 cha 134: Well, please just think of it as 'there must be some condition.'

キャプション1: Analyze Kotaro Niimura's actions
A1 cha 158: Then let us think more deeply about his actions in the first and second routes of the Shigatsu Arc.
A2 cha 180: In the first route he analyzed the curse-killings with Natsumi Kogori and the others, and in the second he attacked alongside the residents.
A3 cha 168: Depending on the route, he takes completely different actions like this.
A4 cha 166: /VAR/-sama, what do you make of these actions of Kotaro Niimura's?
キャプション3: Someone is giving Kotaro Niimura orders
キャプション4: Kotaro Niimura has a split personality
キャプション5: He changes what he does to fit the situation
B1 cha 170: A fake Kotaro Niimura. Hmm, how likely might that be...
B2 cha 168: He seems to have a rather unique appearance, so disguising oneself as him and acting the part would seem quite difficult, but...
B4 cha 148: No, there is just one. One person who could act the part of a fake Kotaro Niimura.
B5 cha 178: The dead Eiichiro Niimura might be able to, but...
B6 cha 160: But that is only if it is a matter of faking his looks. Eiichiro Niimura is already deceased, so surely it would be impossible.
C1 cha 152: I see. So Kotaro Niimura is not the root of it all; someone is giving him orders.
C2 cha 172: True, if those orders differ by route, his actions would end up inconsistent too.
C3 cha 156: Then who on earth is giving Kotaro Niimura orders, I wonder.
C4 cha 152: In the second route, everyone, residents included, gathered at Arata Station. So the mastermind was also at the scene then.
C5 cha 180: But everyone except the Motoki-cho group and Erika Niimura died. That would make Erika Niimura the likeliest mastermind.
C6 cha 180: But if so, it seems odd to go to the trouble of calling in backup to solve the case, and Natsumi Kogori, the first target, came back alive and well.
C7 cha 168: So should we think that in the second route the mastermind failed to achieve their goal?
C8 cha 112: In that case... the mastermind is someone who was not at Arata Station...?
C9 cha 106: ............ That is impossible, is it not? Everyone involved was gathered at Arata Station.
D1 cha 120: A split personality? Oh, I see...
D2 cha 169: So there is a personality that tries to solve the curse-killings, and one that kills people every year... no, strictly, one that tries to capture Natsumi Kogori.
D3 cha 176: In that case, though, the condition would probably be that no one knows he has a split personality.
D4 cha 159: If not only his mother, Erika Niimura, but even his 2 daughters saw through it, his actions would turn contradictory.
D5 cha 128: Or the possibility that they are all in on it together, those women included.
D6 cha 132: Mm, if they were in on it together, that seems a far bigger problem than a split personality, though...
D7 cha 146: Honestly, the split-personality theory may be a bit of a stretch.
D8 cha 155: Still, it is true that he acts in a way that makes one want to ask, 'Is it a split personality?'
D9 cha 110: Hmm, it seems it is not simply Kotaro Niimura acting on his own after all.
E1 cha 101: I see, that may be the most realistic.
E2 cha 142: He switches, depending on the situation, between helping to solve the cases and taking part in them.
E3 cha 168: Then both must hold some merit for him. Whether the cases are solved or he takes part, either way there is an outcome he welcomes.
E4 cha 156: In other words, to him it does not matter whether the cases happen or not. He makes whichever choice brings him closer to a goal beyond them.
E5 cha 134: What could that goal and merit be... There must be something beyond the cases being solved, or happening.
E6 cha 136: And on the way to that goal, there is a key: Natsumi Kogori.
E7 cha 130: If he adapts to each situation, he may be something of a bystander. One truly involved would lean to one side.

キャプション1: So Kotaro Niimura is the culprit after all?
A1 cha 158: Well, at the very least there is no doubt he was on the side of the perpetrators.
A2 cha 180: But something about him is fishy, or rather... He is hiding something, is he not?
A3 cha 168: In Erina Goto's view, he is 'covering for someone.'
A4 cha 166: In other words, by actively playing the culprit, Kotaro Niimura is trying to protect a secret he absolutely does not want known.
A5 cha 162: I think we may take it that way.
A6 cha 159: What about you, /VAR/-sama? What was Kotaro Niimura thinking when he turned to violence in the underground passage?
キャプション2: He's covering for someone after all
キャプション3: He just wants us to think so to escape the blame
B1 cha 170: So you think so too, /VAR/-sama.
B2 cha 168: Indeed, if everything he did was his own decision alone, it does not quite add up.
B3 cha 156: Taking the first route through the third as a whole, his actions lack consistency, shall we say...
B4 cha 148: There is probably some core to them, but that core seems to waver from route to route.
B5 cha 178: Either way, we will not know unless he chooses to tell the truth.
C1 cha 152: Hmm, one could think of it that way too.
C2 cha 172: He makes it look as if something lies behind it, when in fact there is nothing. He is putting on a convincing act to escape the guilt of murder.
C3 cha 156: I think that is quite possible too. That way he could also throw off the investigation afterward.
C4 cha 152: But he unquestionably committed violence. That crime cannot be erased.

キャプション1: What was Kotaro Niimura doing underground?
A1 cha 158: According to Erina Goto, that underground space shows signs that someone was going in and out frequently.
A2 cha 180: Which means that person is, in all likelihood, Kotaro Niimura.
A3 cha 168: What he was doing there, I cannot tell, but...
A4 cha 166: He probably had a secret he wanted no one to know.
A5 cha 162: Whether he turned to such violence to protect it, I wonder...
A6 cha 159: In any case, I am sure something is hidden there.
A7 cha 142: The main scenarios alone do not make it clear, so I suggest viewing them together with the References.

キャプション1: That dream with Eiichiro Niimura wasn't danger sense, right?
A1 cha 158: Indeed. As I discussed with you before, /VAR/-sama, there is much that is puzzling about Natsumi Kogori's danger sense.
A2 cha 180: His advice, 'You must not learn the truth,' could in a sense be called danger sense. However...
A3 cha 168: Yet for that, it feels a little strange, shall we say...
A4 cha 166: Forgive me, I cannot explain it well, but it feels less like danger sense than Eiichiro Niimura's own words, just as they are.
A5 cha 162: Whether Eiichiro Niimura appeared in the dream by chance, or whether it is an extension of danger sense, I do not know...
A6 cha 159: I am sorry that I can only say vague things.

キャプション1: Eiichiro Niimura said not to learn the truth, though?
A2 cha 180: Do you understand now what I said at the very beginning?
A3 cha 168: Learning the truth only invites misfortune. Rather than that, you should wish for their happy ending.
A4 cha 166: Following Eiichiro Niimura's advice, I have judged that learning the truth is inappropriate.
キャプション2: I see. Now I finally get it.
キャプション3: Isn't that different from what you said earlier?
B1 cha 170: I am glad you understand. Learning the truth would only get in the way of their happy ending.
B2 cha 168: I will not be guiding you to any such route myself.
B3 cha 156: It may be frustrating for you, /VAR/-sama, but please, forgive me.
C2 cha 172: It is true that there is something doubtful about calling Eiichiro Niimura's voice danger sense.
C3 cha 156: However, that voice has saved us time and again until now.
C4 cha 152: So whether it is danger sense or not, I believe we should follow it.
C5 cha 180: That is what I meant, so please do not misunderstand.

キャプション1: So Natsumi Kogori's chest is a size that fits under a Noh mask...
A1 cha 158: What a rather vulgar thought...
A2 cha 180: Well, that is surely true, and had it been any bigger, I think it would have led to a serious injury.
A3 cha 168: Well, it was a good thing Natsumi Kogori was that size, or, how should I put it...
A5 cha 162: Honestly! I hate dirty jokes!
A6 cha 159: /大文字//VAR/-sama, you're so naughty!

キャプション1: Why was Kotaro Niimura calling Sakura Niimura's name?
A1 cha 158: Pardon?
A2 cha 180: Was there such a scene?
A3 cha 168: I am sorry, I do not remember it well.
A4 cha 166: Well, even if that were so, he was out of his mind, after all. It is of no importance.

キャプション1: What happened to Haruka Niimura?
A1 cha 158: Do you perhaps mean the green eye?
A2 cha 180: It seems that, in very rare cases, a head injury can change the color of an eye. Perhaps that is it?
A3 cha 168: You see, Kotaro Niimura pressed her head against the underground ceiling.
キャプション2: I see, I think you're right
キャプション3: That's way too much of a coincidence...
キャプション4: Is it related to the Niimura sisters' eyes?
B1 cha 170: Yes, quite. I cannot think of anything else.
C1 cha 152: Even if you say so...
C2 cha 172: Her eye color did change, and there is surely some cause.
C3 cha 156: But is there any cause other than the injury?
C4 cha 152: There should have been no such case before now. We could speculate in many ways here, but there is nothing to base it on.
C5 cha 180: We ought not to spend effort on futile things.
D1 cha 120: Those sisters have foreigners among their ancestors, and I think they simply inherited it.
D2 cha 169: Haruka Niimura has no direct blood ties to Arata, so the cause must differ from theirs.
D3 cha 176: Well, I cannot speculate any further than that.

キャプション1: So the Shigatsu Arc ended full of mysteries after all
A1 cha 158: Well, it is true that it ended with unclear, vague things left unresolved.
A2 cha 180: But as Eiichiro Niimura warned, learning the truth invites misfortune.
A3 cha 168: Which would they wish for, the truth or happiness?
キャプション2: I still want them to pursue the truth
キャプション3: If they're happy, I don't need the truth
B2 cha 168: Well, that depends on their decision, not ours, but...
B3 cha 156: But at least Natsumi Kogori will no longer pursue the truth, I think.
B4 cha 148: If she stops cooperating, do you not think the truth will probably be out of reach?
B5 cha 178: Even if Erina Goto put her brains to work, I doubt the results would be good.
B6 cha 160: Because although Erina Goto has built up a great many deductions so far, we do not even know whether they are right.
B7 cha 138: As long as Natsumi Kogori does not seek the truth, this is as far as it goes.
B8 cha 104: So please, wish for their happy ending.
C1 cha 152: You are good sense itself, /VAR/-sama. I am grateful for your consideration.
C2 cha 172: Yes, I believe the truth is not something to pursue at the cost of sacrifice.
C3 cha 156: An extreme example, but 'Does the afterlife exist?' You would not kill yourself to find that out, would you, /VAR/-sama?
C4 cha 152: There is a limit even to confirming the truth. Please do not forget where that line is drawn.

キャプション1: A trip as a blood-related family... doesn't Mifuyu Niimura mind?
A1 cha 158: Ordinarily, there would surely be some reluctance. Sending one's adopted child on a trip with her blood-related parents, of all things.
A2 cha 180: This is a behind-the-scenes story, but it seems Mifuyu Niimura and Akane Kogori had made that promise from the start. What is more, Mifuyu Niimura apparently proposed it.
A3 cha 168: She must have felt indebted to Akane Kogori somehow, after all. It seems she wished, at least once the girl had grown, to make even a little time for them together.
A4 cha 166: I suppose it is Mifuyu Niimura's own way of expressing her gratitude.

キャプション1: Is the inn that showed up expensive?
A1 cha 158: Yes, it seems it is rather out of reach for ordinary people.
A2 cha 180: It is apparently 78,000 yen per person for one night with two meals. And since it is Golden Week, the price is said to be even higher.
A3 cha 168: Even so, at this time of year it is apparently fully booked. Perhaps people with money really do not hold back on this sort of thing.
A4 cha 166: After all, this time the reservation was only made in mid-April. It seems a good room happened to be free, by luck.
A5 cha 162: There should also be an introduction to the inn among the references, so please have a look at that as well.

キャプション1: Who's that fortune-teller?
A1 cha 158: She is apparently an authority on physiognomy, and her name is Yuko Stella. She was born in Shiyo 750.
A2 cha 180: As she said, fortune-telling is, after all, advice based on statistics. It cannot change a person's future.
A3 cha 168: So she apparently believes a fortune-teller's role is to give the kind of advice that will help that person.
A4 cha 166: In her case, that advice seems to be very well received, and I hear she sometimes takes on ordinary life counseling rather than fortune-telling.
キャプション2: You know a lot about Yuko Stella
B1 cha 170: Eh? Well, yes, I suppose so. The truth is, there was a time long ago when I was rather into fortune-telling...
B2 cha 168: Ah, though I only mean horoscopes and the like. Nothing good enough to tell /VAR/-sama's fortune.
B3 cha 156: She is famous in the fortune-telling world. An authority, yet never arrogant, she advises from the other person's viewpoint. That is apparently quite hard.
B4 cha 148: Once the title of fortune-teller grows big, some people let it go to their heads and turn arrogant, after all.
C1 cha 152: Hmm... All I can say is that it depends on the situation...
C2 cha 172: For example, I do not believe in omikuji or TV horoscopes at all. Those just push whatever comes out onto you. I think that is a little different from fortune-telling.
C3 cha 156: Fortune-telling is, after all, statistics. It is not necessarily right.
C4 cha 152: But how can one guide the client from that uncertain information? I think that very ability to respond is what fortune-telling demands.
C5 cha 180: So if it is fortune-telling like Yuko Stella's, then I can believe in it.
C6 cha 180: Yes, no one can choose the future. Whatever the fortune, whatever the fate, the one who decides what lies ahead is oneself.
C7 cha 168: For better or worse, it is a path one chose oneself. That is what I think.

キャプション1: What's this 'constitution' Natsumi Kogori and Chigaya Niimura have?
A1 cha 158: That is what Yuko Stella said to Natsumi Kogori.
A2 cha 180: Natsumi Kogori and Chigaya Niimura are very much alike in constitution. And yet their natures cannot coexist, she said.
A3 cha 168: Frankly, I do not know what it means, and I am not certain that fortune can be relied on, either.
A4 cha 166: I am sorry to turn the question back on you, but does anything come to mind for /VAR/-sama?
キャプション3: Chigaya Niimura has danger sense too
B1 cha 170: Figures?
B2 cha 168: I see, in the abandoned hut they told each other their complexes, and so―
B3 cha 156: /大文字//揺れ/No, that's absolutely not it!
B4 cha 148: Honestly, no one needs a fortune for that, and those are natures that coexist just fine...
B5 cha 178: It's absolutely not about their figures. I'll say it flat out. I have no grounds, but it's absolutely not that.
B6 cha 160: /小/...Or so I'd like to think...
C1 cha 152: Chigaya Niimura has danger sense too...?
C2 cha 172: That, I must say, I have never heard of... If so, then in the Shigatsu Arc as well, Chigaya Niimura might have used that ability―
C3 cha 156: Ah, but there were no cherry trees, so the conditions for foresight were not met. Then there is no means of verifying it...
C4 cha 152: Even so, it is certainly not something that can be ruled out. I think it is quite an interesting angle.
D1 cha 120: Some fortunes are right, some fortunes are wrong. Even a famous fortune-teller must miss sometimes.
D2 cha 169: Still, linking Chigaya Niimura and Natsumi Kogori together... that is far too much of a coincidence...
D3 cha 176: Chigaya Niimura happened to meet the fortune-teller in Tokyo, and Natsumi Kogori, by chance, at a hot spring...
D4 cha 159: The fortune-teller meeting both of them is too much of a coincidence in itself, but then telling Natsumi Kogori about it... the odds are dizzying...
D5 cha 128: Well, even so, it may just be coincidence. A constitution linking the two may be reading too much into it.

キャプション1: Haruka Niimura's eye really stands out, huh?
A1 cha 158: Yes. As one would expect, after that it seems people pointed it out at school, too.
A2 cha 180: She seems to be telling those around her it was "caused by a head injury," but even so, the true cause is still unknown.
A3 cha 168: Haruka Niimura is apparently planning to go to a larger hospital after Golden Week.
A4 cha 166: I hope that will reveal the cause... It is a truly strange phenomenon, though.
キャプション2: Were the Niimura sisters born with odd eyes?
B1 cha 170: Yes, that seems certain. Both of them have had those eye colors since birth.
B2 cha 168: So I think the Niimura sisters' condition is different from Haruka Niimura's, but...
B3 cha 156: Well, I am not a doctor, so I cannot say for certain.
C1 cha 152: Temporary...
C2 cha 172: That may be so. If an injury or illness is the cause, then once it is treated, the eye should go back to its original color.

キャプション1: How must Haruka Niimura feel, going on a trip with her real parents?
A1 cha 158: As you saw, she seems to be feeling quite awkward.
A2 cha 180: Part of it must be facing her real parents anew, but to her, Mifuyu Niimura is still her one and only parent.
A3 cha 168: So I imagine an event like that leaves her somewhat bewildered.
キャプション2: But Mifuyu Niimura was the one who suggested it, right?
B1 cha 170: Yes. It seems Mifuyu Niimura gave it to the Kogori couple as a gift, out of gratitude for everything until now.
B2 cha 168: But, how shall I put it...
B3 cha 156: It also seems she was a little short on consideration for the daughters. Then again, charging ahead like that is very like Mifuyu Niimura.
B4 cha 148: From Haruka Niimura's point of view, she might feel she was lent out by the parent who raised her to her real parents...
B5 cha 178: Well, in any case, I am glad Haruka Niimura seems to have come to see the trip in a positive light.
B6 cha 160: After all, both Akane Kogori and Mifuyu Niimura probably meant to tell her once she was old enough to think it through that far.
C1 cha 152: That is true. Suddenly learning who her real parents are, and then suddenly being told to go on a trip...
C2 cha 172: This may sound a bit like talking behind their backs, but I do wonder if they should have talked it over more with Haruka Niimura...
C3 cha 156: Though I am sure Mifuyu Niimura meant no harm at all.

キャプション1: So the trip was decided without even asking Haruka Niimura?
A1 cha 158: Pardon?
A2 cha 180: Ah... yes, that is right. So it seems.
A3 cha 168: It seems Mifuyu Niimura told her out of the blue: "Go on a trip with the Kogori family over Golden Week."
A4 cha 166: Well, it is one of those things. Consider this another bit of behind-the-scenes trivia.

キャプション1: Was the family bath scene really necessary?
A1 cha 158: Pardon?
A2 cha 180: Well, yes... um...
A3 cha 168: I chose it thinking it might get a little laugh, but...
キャプション2: Isn't /立木/ actually into dirty jokes?
キャプション3: What kind of supernatural phenomenon is the spinning Noh mask?

B4 cha 148: I thought that part was funnier too, so the bath scene was its opening act, its setup...
B5 cha 178: Oh, honestly! Let's drop this subject! The more excuses I make, the more embarrassing it gets!
C2 cha 172: Would it be better... if I simply explained that...?

キャプション1: About the dream Erina Goto was having in the car
A1 cha 158: That is surely a sign of her conviction to search out the truth of the curse-killings.
A2 cha 180: It has been nearly a month since then, yet she still has not reached the truth. She remains unconvinced, and she seems to keep piling deduction on deduction.
キャプション2: What's really behind the voice telling her not to know the truth?
キャプション3: She really does love thinking, huh
B1 cha 170: At the very least, it is probably something different from Natsumi Kogori's danger sense. She has no such ability, after all.
B2 cha 168: Most likely, the warning Mifuyu Niimura gave her on the way back from the Arata settlement, "Do not pursue the truth," is still weighing on her.
B3 cha 156: Seen the other way around, could it be that Mifuyu Niimura is vaguely starting to see the truth of the curse-killings?
B4 cha 148: If one pursues it, something bad will happen. So she is trying to stop her.
B5 cha 178: Hmm...
B6 cha 160: It may be worth thinking over Mifuyu Niimura's actions once more. There may be unexpected hints in the references and such.
C1 cha 152: That is surely part of it as well. But more than that, she probably cannot forgive the existence of someone gloating behind the scenes.
C2 cha 172: She has come to know the settlement's people; it is no longer someone else's affair. Her conviction to find whoever lurks behind it, for those dear to her, drives her on.
C3 cha 156: True, stopping as she was warned would be easy. But her sense of justice probably will not allow it.
C4 cha 152: In a sense, Erina Goto is a bit of a handful. I only hope she does not go charging off on her own...

キャプション1: So Erina Goto hates haunted houses
A1 cha 158: Yes. She believes in neither the supernatural nor ghosts. So whether it is a graveyard or a ruin, she is apparently perfectly fine even if thrown in alone.
A2 cha 180: The reason, of course, is that she believes paranormal phenomena cannot possibly occur.
A3 cha 168: But in a haunted house, things are certain to show up. And professionals in the field put all their skill into scaring you. That, it seems, she cannot handle...
A4 cha 166: As much as haunted spots do not bother her, she seems to be terribly weak against horror attractions.
キャプション2: Does she have any other weaknesses?
B1 cha 170: Speaking of Erina Goto's other weaknesses...
B2 cha 168: As you saw before, she is easily lured by food. If you can satisfy her appetite, she seems willing to grant most requests.
B3 cha 156: Other than that...
B4 cha 148: Ah, this may surprise you, but she is not good with children.
B5 cha 178: Her reason is, apparently, "because I can't tell what they're thinking."
B6 cha 160: So it seems she cannot communicate smoothly with anyone who has not reached a certain mental age.
B7 cha 138: When she first met Kana Niimura, too, she showed a rather clumsy side of herself.
C1 cha 152: Oh, you find that cute? You are quite the connoisseur...
C2 cha 172: Actually, I...
C3 cha 156: I am not good with haunted houses either...
C5 cha 180: Ah, n-no, that's not it!? I didn't say it so you'd call me "cute" too, I was simply mentioning something I have in common with Erina Goto...!
C6 cha 180: W-well, anyway, Erina Goto trembling in a haunted house is cute, isn't it! Ah ha ha ha ha!
C7 cha 168: /小/Ha ha ha...

シナリオ名: 生まれ変わる家族たち
キャプション1: Momoko Goto's feelings were really complicated, huh
A1 cha 158: At last she poured out what was in her heart. She was terribly afraid of being abandoned by her younger sister.
A2 cha 180: Her sister grew smarter than she was, and she began to doubt her own place as the older sister... Would she one day be written off as someone no longer needed?
A3 cha 168: Then attending her boyfriend's funeral made her heart give way. The only choice left to her was to push her sister away before she could be abandoned, and to disappear.
A4 cha 166: From some angles it may look like an easy way out, but surely it was the result of her thinking it through in her own way.
キャプション2: Maybe she just didn't have the courage to take that first step
キャプション3: But they'll be okay now, right
B1 cha 170: Indeed. But I think the same was true not only of Momoko Goto but of Erina Goto as well.
B2 cha 168: She could not bring herself to approach her sister, and their hearts stayed apart for 5 whole years, surely because each was afraid to step toward the other.
B3 cha 156: Even if they reached out, if they stayed at odds, their bond as sisters would truly be cut. That fear was what had been tearing them apart.
B4 cha 148: To an onlooker it may seem almost comical, but I think this is a hard thing indeed, and not only for them.
B5 cha 178: Just as with Akane Kogori and Mifuyu Niimura: had they talked properly, the Megasawa City case would never have happened.
B6 cha 160: In the same way, had Natsumi Kogori and Haruka Niimura talked about the curse from the start, no tragedy beyond the flayed-body case would have happened either.
B7 cha 138: Stepping toward another takes more courage than one imagines. So I think it is very good that they reached this reconciliation at all.
C2 cha 172: Indeed. I believe the Goto sisters will surely be able to return to being sisters who need each other.
C3 cha 156: Yes, I am sure the two of them will find happiness...
C4 cha 152: That is what I believe.

シナリオ名: 生まれ変わる家族たち
キャプション1: Who was Momoko Goto's boyfriend who died?
A1 cha 158: His name was Hiromitsu Fujino. He was Momoko Goto's classmate.
A2 cha 180: His grades were among the top of his year, but he was not very used to women, and he confessed to Momoko Goto fully prepared to go down in flames―
A3 cha 168: Momoko Goto, for her part, was more than a little fond of him for his brains, and though she apparently hesitated somewhat, they started going out.
A4 cha 166: But given his personality, he did not know how to date a girl, and it seems that even after they started going out, he could hardly bring himself to talk to her.
A5 cha 162: Knowing that about him, Momoko Goto watched over him patiently and warmly, waiting for him to make a move.
A6 cha 159: But a month in, a car with a blown tire plowed into the two of them as they walked. He pulled Momoko Goto clear by the hand and died in her place.
A7 cha 142: They say that was the first and last time she ever touched him. She was terribly, terribly devastated, it seems.
キャプション2: And then his family said cruel things to her, too
キャプション3: I wonder if Momoko Goto ever got over it
B1 cha 170: Yes. As Momoko Goto said, at the funeral they pointed out her natural hair color, and it seems her heart finally gave way.
B2 cha 168: Everyone in his family was highly educated. Being spoken to like that set off a chain reaction, and her fear of Erina Goto exploded as well.
B3 cha 156: In truth, his family had nowhere to aim their anger, so they lashed out at Momoko Goto, who had been with him. The driver died in the crash too.
B4 cha 148: So they did not truly blame her for her hair color.
B5 cha 178: Misfortune piled on misfortune, and in the end it tore the sisters apart.
B6 cha 160: Well, the exchange at the funeral was certainly the trigger. But I think that even without the accident, they were fated to fall out sooner or later.
B7 cha 138: Momoko Goto was already doubting her own place as the older sister, after all.
B8 cha 104: No, but...
B9 cha 120: If he had lived and she could have confided in him, perhaps a different path would have opened up...
C1 cha 152: I wonder. Even I cannot see into her heart, though...
C2 cha 172: But it is certain that the accident kept casting a darkness over her heart. Even if she got past his death, the darkness it cast stayed with her.
C3 cha 156: No, but then again, I wonder...
C4 cha 152: As you saw, Momoko Goto never took another boyfriend after that. Plenty of men seem to have approached her, but none of it ever turned into romance―
C5 cha 180: By her own account, it was "because I've got no time for fun with all my part-time jobs," yet she never tried to find anyone to lean on, which must mean that even now...
C6 cha 180: ............Anything more would only be piling guess on guess. Surely Momoko Goto herself does not know that part either.
C7 cha 168: In any case, I hope her reconciliation with Erina Goto gives her back the will to search for happiness once more.

キャプション1: What happened when Erika Niimura died?
A1 cha 158: At 5 p.m. on May 3, Shiyo 800, Erika Niimura and Kana Niimura went out together to shop for groceries at a supermarket in Toyotake.
A2 cha 180: While they were there, she apparently just collapsed inside the store.
A3 cha 168: An ambulance was called at once and she was taken to the hospital, but about 5 hours later she died during surgery. The cause was a heart attack.
A4 cha 166: There were many witnesses, and she died in a hospital, so one may safely say there was no foul play at all.
キャプション2: I wonder why she had a heart attack
キャプション3: Was there really no foul play?
B1 cha 170: Most likely the strain of the curse-killings took its toll.
B2 cha 168: Tormented for 10 whole years, and then nearly every resident, her son included, was arrested. Then the aftermath and the questioning. It must have been a heavy burden.
B3 cha 156: Also, after the incident, a doctor prescribed her antidepressants, that is, medicine for depression.
B4 cha 148: Erika Niimura's actions after the incident are not depicted, but her heart must have grown sick enough that she herself knew it.
B5 cha 178: But given her character, she would not have let any of it show, and would have kept up a cheerful face, I imagine.
B6 cha 160: It is odd to call it the price of averting the curse-killings, but I believe she was able to fulfill her duties as the Grand Witch.
B7 cha 138: May she rest in peace over there...
C1 cha 152: Judging from the autopsy results and the circumstances, it does seem certain that she died of illness.
C2 cha 172: To overturn this result, I do think one would need to look at the situation again from a new angle, but...
C3 cha 156: At present, however, I have no information that would overturn the finding of death by illness.
C4 cha 152: For now, it should be fine to treat it as death by illness. Should anything new come up, I will let you know as needed.

キャプション1: So Natsumi Kogori is giving up on the truth
A1 cha 158: Yes. Following the advice of Eiichiro Niimura and the fortune-teller, and after talking it over with Erina Goto, that seems to be what she decided.
A2 cha 180: I expect /VAR/-sama would like her to chase the truth, but...
A3 cha 168: This is the decision she made. Please, I would ask that you respect it.
キャプション2: So the truth really stays unknown?
キャプション3: Erina Goto's bound to do something about it
B1 cha 170: At the very least... Let me see...
B2 cha 168: Natsumi Kogori will never learn the truth.
B3 cha 156: As far as I know, Natsumi Kogori... the truth...
B5 cha 178: /VAR/-sama, the end point of this world is also close at hand now.
B6 cha 160: Please, watch over them to their happy ending.
B7 cha 138: The truth is not something to be obtained at the cost of trampling on happiness.
C1 cha 152: Erina Goto...
C2 cha 172: Indeed, I am sure that she will keep chasing the truth, whatever walls stand in her way.
C3 cha 156: Even if it takes a great deal of time and effort, her sense of justice will not allow her to stop.
C4 cha 152: Natsumi Kogori and Erina Goto seem to think about such things entirely differently.
C5 cha 180: Still, if Erina Goto, too, seemed about to call forth a new misfortune, surely she would stop at that point...
C6 cha 180: But how far in the future that would be, I cannot even imagine.
C7 cha 168: Perhaps Erina Goto can no longer break free of this fate.
C8 cha 112: That is why I would rather she seek happiness than the 'mere cause' at the end of her pursuit.
C9 cha 106: Even if she learned the truth, she would only think, "Oh, I see."

キャプション1: So Chigaya Niimura is the mastermind?
A2 cha 180: Well, I wonder about that.
A3 cha 168: I do not know.
キャプション2: Then what about the cursed green eyes?
キャプション3: At least Chigaya Niimura did kill people, right?
B1 cha 170: Cursed green eyes...
B2 cha 168: I have turned it over in many ways myself, but nothing in particular comes to mind...
B3 cha 156: Perhaps she truly is cursed, or perhaps Chigaya Niimura has merely convinced herself of it.
B4 cha 148: After all, by that logic, Chigaya Niimura, Kana Niimura, and Haruka Niimura too would all be cursed.
B5 cha 178: Haruka Niimura aside, to think the Niimura sisters have lived under a curse all this time...
B6 cha 160: Could it be that they are seized by sudden fits of killing people? And that this is the truth of the curse-killings?
B7 cha 138: Surely not... Something like that...
C1 cha 152: Given her confession, that is how it looks. Erina Goto's deduction was correct.
C2 cha 172: And yet something does not fit. What settled that were her words, "I wanted to kill Mom too."

C4 cha 152: Did Sakura Niimura have some reason she had to be killed by her own daughter?
C5 cha 180: And on top of that, she kept up the curse-killings because of it...
C7 cha 168: Truly, it makes no sense to me.

キャプション1: What did Erina Goto realize from talking with Chigaya Niimura?
A1 cha 158: That is............ a difficult point...
A2 cha 180: Judging from the circumstances, Erina Goto seems to have suspected that Chigaya Niimura was the mastermind.
A3 cha 168: But the single remark "I wanted to kill Mom too" turned Erina Goto's deduction upside down.
A4 cha 166: In other words, the core of the curse-killings ought to lie in that part, but...
A5 cha 162: Well, then again, learning the truth brings misfortune.
A6 cha 159: Whatever point there may be in our chasing the truth―
キャプション2: We've come this far, let's think it through together
キャプション3: So /立木/ doesn't know any more than this either?
B1 cha 170: Even if you put it that way...
B2 cha 168: Well then, if I must say something...
B3 cha 156: Please try looking back over every reference so far. There is a great deal of information that is not in the main story.
C2 cha 172: To put it plainly, yes, that is the case.
C3 cha 156: I may be the guide, but more than I know is stirring behind the scenes.
C4 cha 152: I am sorry, but there is no other way to put it.

キャプション1: So this is where we say goodbye to Haruka Niimura
A1 cha 158: It seems that is what she has decided.
A2 cha 180: Haruka Niimura has a stubborn side, so she will not be talked out of it so easily.
A3 cha 168: But as she says, once the people are gone, it is only a matter of time before the settlement perishes.
A4 cha 166: If the settlement is to survive, I think that, too, is a choice one could make.
キャプション2: I wonder if she'll manage all right
B1 cha 170: Naturally, at first there will be one failure and setback after another.
B2 cha 168: But she is prepared for that. Nothing begins if one does nothing but despair.
B3 cha 156: She must have decided that taking some action was the only way to protect the settlement.
B4 cha 148: Yes: not making it succeed, but first beginning something. Success and failure alike are results that come only from action.
B5 cha 178: She now stands at that starting point.
B6 cha 160: All that remains is to watch over her.
C1 cha 152: How it ends...
C2 cha 172: One scenario remains before the final destination of this world.
C3 cha 156: Please see it with your own eyes, /VAR/-sama.

キャプション1: So this world is ending too.
A1 cha 158: Yes. One more, and we reach the final destination of this world.
A2 cha 180: Looking back, how was it? What did you think, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション2: Will we learn the truth at the end?
キャプション3: Too many things are still vague
キャプション4: I think it turned out pretty well
B2 cha 168: The truth is not something one can catch so easily.
B3 cha 156: All the more so now, when there are many problems that must be solved before the truth.
B4 cha 148: If, even after those are settled, they still seek the truth―
B5 cha 178: then perhaps the truth really will appear before their eyes.
C1 cha 152: I understand very well what you mean, /VAR/-sama. Even after coming this far, we still cannot see the bottom of it.
C2 cha 172: Not only that, but new facts keep coming to light, and the road to the truth gets twisted.
C3 cha 156: But the truth is already a thing of the past. It does not necessarily lead to the future.
C4 cha 152: Right now, they are looking to the future. Each sees it differently, but each is chasing happiness as she herself understands it.
C5 cha 180: Knowing the truth would only get in the way of their happiness.
C6 cha 180: For now, how will they seize their happiness? That is what I would like you to watch.
D1 cha 120: Thank you. Hearing you say so, I can truly feel that guiding you this far was worth it.
D2 cha 169: In that case...
D3 cha 176: it means my farewell with /VAR/-sama is near as well.
D4 cha 159: Thank you truly for coming this far. I offer you my heartfelt gratitude.
D5 cha 128: All that remains is for you to watch their happy ending.
